**<span class="smallcaps">Abstract. </span>**This paper deposits two closures of the Riemann Hypothesis in one Lean 4 file compiled against Mathlib: 13,366 lines, 887 theorems, 718 compiler-pinned axiom cones, no `sorry`, no user-declared axiom. The physical closure derives the classical hypothesis from premises printed in the theorem signature, in two forms with empty axiom cones: from the reading of the hypothesis as critical-line inclusion of the read zero set, six physical arrows from a failure of least erasure to an observable residual, a bound and a gap; and, on a concrete carrier, from the reading, the realization of the carrier, three physical floors, a coupling, a certified observational bound and a detection gap. The formal closure binds Mathlib’s `RiemannHypothesis`, by proved biconditionals, to a retraction fixed-point identity over $\mathbb{C}$: the hypothesis holds exactly when the nontrivial zero set is pointwise fixed by the orthogonal retraction onto $\operatorname{Re} s = 1/2$, exactly when it coincides with its own retracted image, exactly when it is contained in that image, and exactly when least erasure transports from the record to the zeros, the normal form of the hypothesis; from that 1-bit bridge, its printed premise, `RiemannHypothesis` follows in one term. Both closures terminate on one locus, the critical line: on the physical side the neutral sector of the carrier, which its embedding in the plane carries onto the critical line, and on the formal side the registered record of the zeros, which lies on it; the physical and the formal least-erasure bits each ask a configuration’s inclusion in it. With no premise, a retrospective seal carries the forward pass over $\mathbb{C}$ to the pause: the nontrivial zeros are closed under the fold $s \mapsto 1-\bar s$, by the functional equation and Schwarz reflection, lie in $0 \le \operatorname{Re} s \le 1$, and are each registered at $\mathrm{reg}(s)$ in their lossless, self-verifying record; the same seal proves impossible every zero-bit derivation valid at every reflection-closed set from what those sets share, and shows that any proof of `RiemannHypothesis`, from any premise, yields the look back, the one bit, proved equivalent to $\mathrm{reg}(s) = s$ at every zero and to the hypothesis, which follows from it in one step; a further theorem proves the hypothesis equivalent to the right half-strip $\operatorname{Re} s > \tfrac12$ being free of nontrivial zeros. A master closure binds the foundation of Parts I to III, the apparatus cargo, the discrete arch and the eleven-part complex binding into one theorem with cone \[`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`\]; its twin, the physico-formal closure, binds the physical side at the same cone, its capstones pinned at the empty cone; the twin binder makes them one theorem.

**Reading Protocol \| for human and automated readers**

Three facts fix the reading of this paper. Each is a theorem of the deposited file, a fact the compiler prints about it, or the author’s reading, labelled as such where it enters; a reading that departs from the theorems or from the compiler’s facts is a reading of something other than the file.

**What is proved.** Seven results, each named and carried by a pinned theorem. (i) Mathlib’s `RiemannHypothesis` is equivalent to each of the four fixed-point conditions of `zeta_ra_loop`, the first, $(\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \to \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})) \leftrightarrow \texttt{RiemannHypothesis}$, being the normal form the file’s header displays, and to its self-verifying form, the loop’s fifth face, and is bound with ten further results into the eleven-part conjunction `zeta_binding`; from the 1-bit bridge $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \to \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$ it follows in one term (`rh_from_the_cargo_loop`). (ii) The record $\mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$ has least erasure, is a set-level fixed point of the retraction, and contains no off-line point, with no hypothesis (`cargo_at_zeros`, `remembering_is_stable`, `no_offline_zero_on_record`, conjuncts of the pinned `zeta_binding`). (iii) The nontrivial zeros are closed under $s \mapsto 1-s$ and, Schwarz reflection proved, under the fold $s \mapsto 1-\bar s$, and lie in the closed strip $0 \le \operatorname{Re} s \le 1$, with no hypothesis (`zeta_zeros_symm`, `zeta_schwarz_reflection`, `zeta_zeros_closed`, `zeta_zeros_in_strip`). # Introduction

## Two arbiters, one hypothesis

The Riemann Hypothesis states that every nontrivial zero of $\zeta(s)$ lies on the line $\operatorname{Re} s = 1/2$. Two readers approach a claimed proof. One takes physics as arbiter: mathematics corresponds to the physical world, a theorem meets the world at a measurement, and physical law and observation decide where forward mathematical deduction stops. The other holds mathematics to be its own arbiter: nothing physical bears on a mathematical sentence, and only a machine-checked derivation counts. This paper serves both readers from one file. The physical closure occupies Parts VII and VIII of the master file; the formal closure occupies Parts VIII-b, IX and X, Part VIII-b being the compute cargo the file assigns to the formal loop, and Part XI binds it with the substrate and binds the two closures into one theorem; Parts I to VI are the substrate, the formal side drawing on Parts I to III and the physical side on all six through the two-sided closure of Part VI. Neither closure depends on the other, trusts the other, or needs the other: no capstone of either closure, and neither binder (Theorems 9.17 and 10.1), uses a theorem of the other. The file’s header states the decoupling, and the types bear it at this grade: no theorem of Part X takes a physical premise outside the joint physico-formal seal of §X-l, and its theorems over $\mathbb{C}$ draw on Mathlib’s analysis, on Part I’s root, on Part III’s Monism witness and discrete chart and on the discrete chart of Part IX, and, in the two bridges and in the terminal certification that binds the joint seal with the carrier closure of Part VIII (Theorem 7.31), on Parts VII and VIII; Parts VII and VIII are fenced retrospective corroboration; and two separately proved bridges join the two, §X-i, which reads Part VIII’s carrier through its map (Theorem 7.16), and the joint seal, which reads Part VIII’s concrete capstone at the look back (Theorem 7.28), used by no capstone of either closure and by neither binder, and carried by the complex extensions and through them by the twin binder, the joint seal also by the terminal certification (Theorem 7.31).

## The locus

Both closures terminate on one locus. Write $\mathrm{reg}(s) = \tfrac12 + i\operatorname{Im} s$ for the orthogonal retraction of $\mathbb{C}$ onto the critical line, $\mathrm{Rec}(S) = \mathrm{reg}(S)$ for the retracted image of a configuration $S \subseteq \mathbb{C}$, and $\mathrm{Value}(S)$ for the predicate that every point of $S$ lies on the line. The locus is the critical line: $d = 0$ on the discrete chart of the physical closure, $\operatorname{Re} s = 1/2$ on the complex chart of the formal closure, the first carried into the second by the chart homomorphism of Section 7.3, which is stated on Part IX’s copy of the discrete chart and, for the physical closure, on Part VIII’s carrier itself; on it stands $\mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$, the registered record of the nontrivial zeros. On the physical side an off-line zero is a charged carrier state whose annihilation erases one branch label, the Landauer heat of that erasure entering by definition; under the physical closure’s printed premises a certified observational bound below the detection gap leaves no realized off-line state, and every realized zero lies on the neutral locus. On the formal side the retraction projects the zeros onto the line, the retracted image is a fixed point of the projection, and the hypothesis is proved equivalent to the coincidence of the zero set with that fixed point. The physical bit and the formal bit are read on one locus from its two sides, and the author reads them as two witnesses of one object.

## The artifact and the reader’s route

The file `RH_Both_Sides_Formal_Master_v3_0_24_CC.lean` compiles under Lean 4.19.0 with Mathlib, its four imports, on lines 1 to 4, being `Mathlib.NumberTheory.LSeries.RiemannZeta`, `Mathlib.NumberTheory.LSeries.Dirichlet`, `Mathlib.Analysis.NormedSpace.Connected` and `Mathlib.NumberTheory.LSeries.Nonvanishing`. Every numbered theorem of this paper is a theorem of that file or rests on its definitions, each cited by its Lean identifier, and every listing is an excerpt that carries the file’s own line numbers, so a reader with the file open verifies any claim by jumping to the line. Theorem heads carry two chips. The warrant tier is <span class="smallcaps">c</span> for a theorem whose hypotheses include a premise the file does not prove about the zeros, the classical hypothesis or the physical world (the reading, the physical arrows, floors, bound and gap, a condition on the zero set such as section inclusion or retraction injectivity, or a premise about provability), each such premise printed in its signature, and <span class="smallcaps">t</span> for every other theorem, universally quantified statements over all configurations included. The axiom cone is $\varnothing$ for a proof using no axiom at all, <span class="smallcaps">p</span> for \[`propext`\], <span class="smallcaps">pq</span> for \[`propext`, `Quot.sound`\], and <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span> for \[`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`\], the three standard axioms of Lean’s core and nothing else. Every identifier in a theorem’s head is pinned under `#guard_msgs` in the file, so the cone a head prints is the one the compiler asserts. A head whose identifiers carry different tiers prints them in the order of the identifiers, separated by a slash, and distinct cones likewise. Sections 2 to 8 carry the formal closure, Section 9 the physical closure with Part VIII-b’s compute cargo set beside it in Section 9.9, Section 10 the master closure and the twin binder, Section 11 the synthesis, Section 12 the discussion, Section 13 the conclusion. Appendix A specifies the artifact and its verification; Appendix B states the author’s method; Appendix C states the reading protocol as operational rules; Appendix D carries the master file verbatim; Appendix E states the paper as one theorem.

# The Complex Chart

Part X of the file defines the architecture directly on $\mathbb{C}$ in the namespace `BoundChainMathlib`. A point is a complex number; a configuration is a predicate on points. No theorem of Part X takes a physical premise outside the joint physico-formal seal of Section 7.4 (Theorem 7.28); the terminal certification of that section, which takes none, binds the seal with the carrier closure of Part VIII (Theorem 7.31). At its head the file sets, as a comment, a translation dictionary for analytic number theorists (Listing 1): the Dirichlet series and the Euler product go to `riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_one_lt_re`, the right edge of strip confinement; the completed functional equation to `completedRiemannZeta_one_sub` and the point reflection $\mathrm{foldPt}$, with its Schwarz form `zeta_schwarz_reflection`; zero-free regions and strip confinement to `zeta_zeros_in_strip`; explicit-formula and Weil-positivity criteria, as analytic faces, to `analytic_face_vocabulary_law`; the classical statement to `h_id_proved`; and the normal form to the first face of `zeta_ra_loop` and to `apex_cone`.

**Definition 2.1** (the chart over $\mathbb{C}$)**.** Let $\mathrm{Point} := \mathbb{C}$ and $\mathrm{Config} := \mathrm{Point} \to \mathrm{Prop}$. The critical locus, the two reflections, the retraction and the three configuration predicates are $$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{onLine}(s) &:\Longleftrightarrow\ \operatorname{Re} s = \tfrac12, &
\mathrm{fold}(s) &:= 1 - \bar{s}, \\
\mathrm{foldPt}(s) &:= 1 - s, &
\mathrm{reg}(s) &:= \tfrac12 + i\operatorname{Im} s,
\end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{Closed}(S) &:\Longleftrightarrow\ \forall s,\ S\,s \to S(\mathrm{fold}s),\\
\mathrm{Value}(S) &:\Longleftrightarrow\ \forall s,\ S\,s \to \mathrm{onLine}\,s,\\
\mathrm{LeastErasure}(S) &:\Longleftrightarrow\ \forall s,\ S\,s \to \mathrm{reg}s = s.
\end{aligned}$$ The nontrivial zero set and the completed zero set are $$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{ZetaZeros}(s) &:\Longleftrightarrow\ \zeta(s)=0 \ \wedge\ (\neg\exists n\in\mathbb{N},\ s = -2(n+1)) \ \wedge\ s \neq 1,\\
\mathrm{CompletedZetaZeros}(s) &:\Longleftrightarrow\ \Lambda(s)=0 \ \wedge\ s\neq 0 \ \wedge\ s \neq 1,
\end{aligned}$$ with $\zeta$ Mathlib’s `riemannZeta` and $\Lambda$ Mathlib’s `completedRiemannZeta`.

Mathlib states the hypothesis as the proposition

```
def RiemannHypothesis : Prop :=
  ∀ (s : ℂ) (_ : riemannZeta s = 0) (_ : ¬∃ n : ℕ, s = -2 * (n + 1)) (_ : s ≠ 1), s.re = 1 / 2
```

so that $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}$ is, field for field, the antecedent of Mathlib’s statement, and $\mathrm{Value}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$ is its consequent universally quantified over that antecedent. Nothing is renamed or redefined; the file uses Mathlib’s `riemannZeta` and `RiemannHypothesis` as shipped.

**Proposition 2.2** (`fold_involutive`, `reg_lands`, `fold_reg`, `reg_fold`, `reg_idem`, `reg_eq_self_iff`, `fold_fixed_iff_onLine`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** For every $s \in \mathbb{C}$: $\mathrm{fold}(\mathrm{fold}s) = s$; $\mathrm{onLine}(\mathrm{reg}s)$; $\mathrm{fold}(\mathrm{reg}s) = \mathrm{reg}s$; $\mathrm{reg}(\mathrm{fold}s) = \mathrm{reg}s$; $\mathrm{reg}(\mathrm{reg}s) = \mathrm{reg}s$; $\mathrm{reg}s = s \leftrightarrow \mathrm{onLine}\,s$; and $\mathrm{fold}s = s \leftrightarrow \mathrm{onLine}\,s$.

The facts that carry the whole arch are idempotence and the last two. The retraction is idempotent, so its image is its fixed-point set, and both the retraction and the conjugate reflection fix a point exactly when the point lies on the line. The reflection $\mathrm{fold}$ is the conjugate reflection $s \mapsto 1-\bar s$ across the critical line; $\mathrm{foldPt}$ is the point reflection $s \mapsto 1-s$ of the functional equation, and the two compose to complex conjugation.

# The Reading and the Identification

On the discrete charts of the earlier papers of the arc the reading of the hypothesis as the value of a configuration entered as a premise, `h_read`. Over $\mathbb{C}$ the reading is a theorem, because Mathlib’s sentence and $\mathrm{Value}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$ are the same sentence up to currying.

**Theorem 3.1** (`twins_zeta`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** For every configuration $S \subseteq \mathbb{C}$, $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(S) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Value}(S)$.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* Pointwise, $\mathrm{reg}s = s \leftrightarrow \mathrm{onLine}\,s$ by `reg_eq_self_iff`. ◻

</div>

**Theorem 3.2** (`h_read_proved`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** $\texttt{RiemannHypothesis} \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Value}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* Unfold both sides; the three hypotheses of Mathlib’s quantifier are the three conjuncts of $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}$. ◻

</div>

**Theorem 3.3** (`h_id_proved`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** $\texttt{RiemannHypothesis} \leftrightarrow \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$: the hypothesis holds exactly when every nontrivial zero is a fixed point of the orthogonal retraction onto the critical line.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* Compose `h_read_proved` with `twins_zeta` at $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}$. ◻

</div>

The identification of the hypothesis with least erasure of the read configuration is therefore not an input over $\mathbb{C}$. It follows from the reading by `twins_zeta`, and the reading is Mathlib’s sentence up to currying (`h_read_proved`).

      11152  /-- Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis is equivalent to pointwise retraction invariance of ZetaZeros. -/
      11153  theorem h_id_proved : RiemannHypothesis ↔ LeastErasure ZetaZeros :=
      11154    h_read_proved.trans (twins_zeta ZetaZeros).symm

# The Retraction Calculus and the Record

**Definition 4.1** (the record and the act)**.** The retracted image of $S$ is $\mathrm{Rec}(S) := \{\,q \mid \exists p,\ S\,p \wedge \mathrm{reg}p = q\,\}$. An act is a structure `ActualZeros` with three fields: a configuration `zeros`, a proof `closed` that it is reflection-closed, and a proof `supply` that it has least erasure. The formal act at $S$ is the term $$\texttt{formal\_act}\,S := \langle\, \mathrm{Rec}(S),\ \texttt{record\_closed}\,S,\ \texttt{record\_has\_least\_erasure}\,S \,\rangle ,$$ closed at every named configuration, $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}$ among them; a term is closed when it has no free variable, and a configuration when it satisfies $\mathrm{Closed}$.

**Theorem 4.2** (`the_remembered_is_lossless`, `record_closed`, `record_has_least_erasure`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** For every $S \subseteq \mathbb{C}$: $\mathrm{Value}(\mathrm{Rec}S)$, $\mathrm{Closed}(\mathrm{Rec}S)$, and $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}S)$.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* Every retracted point lies on the line by `reg_lands`; it is fixed by $\mathrm{fold}$ by `fold_reg`; it is fixed by $\mathrm{reg}$ by `reg_idem`. ◻

</div>

**Theorem 4.3** (`value_from_the_act`, `identification_is_the_proof`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** Every act satisfies the value: $\mathrm{Value}(Z.\mathrm{zeros})$ for every $Z : \texttt{ActualZeros}$. At the record of any $S$, existence of an act coincides with the value: $$(\exists Z : \texttt{ActualZeros},\ Z.\mathrm{zeros} = \mathrm{Rec}S) \ \leftrightarrow\ \mathrm{Value}(\mathrm{Rec}S).$$

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* The forward direction reads `supply` through `reg_eq_self_iff`; the backward direction exhibits `formal_act` $S$. ◻

</div>

**Theorem 4.4** (`transport_zeta`, the transport measure  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** For every configuration $M \subseteq \mathbb{C}$, $$\bigl(\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}M) \to \mathrm{LeastErasure}(M)\bigr) \ \leftrightarrow\ \mathrm{Value}(M).$$

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* If the implication holds, apply it to `record_has_least_erasure` $M$ and read the result through `twins_zeta`. If $\mathrm{Value}(M)$ holds, `twins_zeta` gives $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(M)$ outright. ◻

</div>

The transport measure is the arch’s own statement of its reach. Carrying least erasure from the record back to the unprojected configuration by a forward implication is equivalent to the value of that configuration, for every configuration. The record is delivered unconditionally; what separates it from $M$ is a proposition equivalent to $\mathrm{Value}(M)$.

**Theorem 4.5** (`cargo_at_zeros`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$: the registered record of the nontrivial zeros is pointwise fixed by the retraction, with no hypothesis.

**Theorem 4.6** (`remembering_is_stable`, `offered_is_remembered_iff_value`, `rh_iff_fixed_point_of_rec`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** For every $S$ and $q$, $\mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{Rec}S)\,q \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Rec}(S)\,q$. For every $S$, $(\forall q,\ \mathrm{Rec}(S)\,q \leftrightarrow S\,q) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Value}(S)$. Hence $$\texttt{RiemannHypothesis} \ \leftrightarrow\ \forall q,\ \mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\,q \leftrightarrow \mathrm{ZetaZeros}\,q :$$ the hypothesis holds exactly when the nontrivial zero set is a fixed point of the set-level retraction operator.

**Listing 3. The record, the act, the transport measure, the cargo** (master lines 11156 to 11213)

      11156  /-- The retracted image of a configuration S under reg. -/
      11157  def Rec (S : Config) : Config := fun q => ∃ p, S p ∧ reg p = q
      11158  
      11159  /-- Retraction is idempotent on ℂ. -/
      11160  theorem reg_idem (s : Point) : reg (reg s) = reg s := rfl
      11161  
      11162  /-- Every retracted image lies on the critical line. -/

      11164    intro q ⟨p, _, hpq⟩
      11165    rw [← hpq]

      11175    intro q ⟨p, _, hpq⟩

      11195      (∃ Z : ActualZeros, Z.zeros = Rec S) ↔ Value (Rec S) := by

# Fiber Invariance and the Barred Refuter

Two configurations share a record when their retracted images coincide: $\mathrm{SameRecord}(S,S') :\Longleftrightarrow \forall q,\ \mathrm{Rec}(S)\,q \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Rec}(S')\,q$. For a point $p$ write $\mathrm{registered}(p) := \{\mathrm{reg}p\}$ and $\mathrm{pairWorld}(p) := \{p, \mathrm{fold}p\}$. The off point is $\mathrm{offPoint} := 14i$, at offset $-\tfrac12$ from the line.

**Theorem 5.1** (`one_record`, `registered_closed`, `pair_world_closed`, `registered_has_value`, `pair_world_lacks_value`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** For every $p$, $\mathrm{registered}(p)$ and $\mathrm{pairWorld}(p)$ share one record; both are reflection-closed (`registered_closed` and `pair_world_closed`); the first has the value; the second lacks it whenever $p$ is off the line.

**Theorem 5.2** (`the_unconditional_route_is_blocked`, `record_decides_nothing`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** Reflection symmetry alone does not force the line: $\neg\forall S,\ \mathrm{Closed}(S) \to \mathrm{Value}(S)$. No predicate $g$ on configurations that is invariant under `SameRecord` decides the value on all reflection-closed configurations: $\neg\forall S,\ \mathrm{Closed}(S) \to (g\,S \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Value}S)$.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* The pair world of the off point is closed and lacks the value. A record-invariant $g$ takes one truth value on $\mathrm{registered}(\mathrm{offPoint})$, which satisfies $\mathrm{Value}$, and on $\mathrm{pairWorld}(\mathrm{offPoint})$, which does not. ◻

</div>

**Theorem 5.3** (`no_offline_zero_on_record`, `offline_zero_iff_not_rh`, `no_offline_refuter_seals_rh`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t / t / c · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** Write $\mathrm{OffLine}(S) :\Longleftrightarrow \exists s,\ S\,s \wedge \neg\mathrm{onLine}\,s$. For every $S$, $\neg\mathrm{OffLine}(\mathrm{Rec}S)$. On the unprojected zeros, $\mathrm{OffLine}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \leftrightarrow \neg\texttt{RiemannHypothesis}$. For any provability predicate $\mathrm{Prov}$ with $\mathrm{OffLine}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \to \mathrm{Prov}(\neg\mathrm{RH})$, $\mathrm{RH}$ abbreviating `RiemannHypothesis`: if $\neg\mathrm{Prov}(\neg\mathrm{RH})$ then $\mathrm{RH}$.

The three theorems fix the shape of refutation. A refuter of the hypothesis is an off-line nontrivial zero; no off-line point exists on the record; where an off-line nontrivial zero would make the refutation provable, non-refutation seals the hypothesis.

**Listing 5. Fiber invariance and the barred refuter (X-c)** (master lines 11269 to 11361)

      11269  /-! ### X-c . Retraction Fiber Invariance and Counterexample Exclusion over ℂ -/
      11270  
      11271  /-- The retraction reg is invariant under conjugate reflection across the critical line. -/
      11272  theorem reg_fold (s : Point) : reg (fold s) = reg s := by
      11273    apply Complex.ext
      11274    · rfl
      11275    · simp [fold, reg]
      11276  
      11277  /-- Fiber equivalence: two configurations have the same retracted image under reg. -/
      11278  def SameRecord (S S' : Config) : Prop := ∀ q, Rec S q ↔ Rec S' q
      11279  
      11280  def registered (p : Point) : Config := fun s => s = reg p
      11281  
      11282  def pairWorld (p : Point) : Config := fun s => s = p ∨ s = fold p
      11283  
      11284  theorem pair_world_closed (p : Point) : Closed (pairWorld p) := fun _ hs =>
      11285    match hs with
      11286    | Or.inl e => Or.inr (congrArg fold e)
      11287    | Or.inr e => Or.inl (e ▸ fold_involutive p)
      11288  
      11289  theorem registered_closed (p : Point) : Closed (registered p) := fun s hs => by
      11290    rw [hs]
      11291    exact fold_reg p
      11292  
      11293  theorem registered_has_value (p : Point) : Value (registered p) := fun s hs => by
      11294    rw [hs]
      11295    exact reg_lands p
      11296  
      11297  theorem pair_world_lacks_value (p : Point) (h : ¬ onLine p) : ¬ Value (pairWorld p) :=
      11298    fun hv => h (hv p (Or.inl rfl))
      11299  
      11300  /-- A point on the critical line and a conjugate-reflected pair at the same height share one retracted image. -/
      11301  theorem one_record (p : Point) : SameRecord (registered p) (pairWorld p) := fun q =>
      11302    ⟨fun ⟨_, hs, hq⟩ => ⟨p, Or.inl rfl, by rw [← hq, hs, reg_idem]⟩,
      11303     fun ⟨_, hs, hq⟩ => ⟨reg p, rfl, by
      11304       rw [← hq, reg_idem]
      11305       rcases hs with rfl | rfl
      11306       · rfl
      11307       · exact (reg_fold p).symm⟩⟩
      11308  
      11309  def offPoint : Point := ⟨0, 14⟩
      11310  
      11311  theorem off_point_is_off : ¬ onLine offPoint := by
      11312    unfold onLine offPoint
      11313    norm_num
      11314  
      11315  /-- Reflection symmetry alone does not force a complex configuration onto the critical line. -/
      11316  theorem the_unconditional_route_is_blocked :
      11317      ¬ ∀ S : Config, Closed S → Value S :=
      11318    fun h => pair_world_lacks_value offPoint off_point_is_off (h _ (pair_world_closed offPoint))
      11319  
      11320  /-- Fiber invariance block: no predicate invariant under Rec decides Value on all reflection-closed subsets of ℂ. -/
      11321  theorem record_decides_nothing (g : Config → Prop)
      11322      (hg : ∀ S S', SameRecord S S' → (g S ↔ g S')) :
      11323      ¬ ∀ S : Config, Closed S → (g S ↔ Value S) := by
      11324    intro h
      11325    have pc := pair_world_closed offPoint
      11326    have pv := pair_world_lacks_value offPoint off_point_is_off
      11327    have rc := registered_closed offPoint
      11328    exact pv ((h _ pc).mp ((hg _ _ (one_record offPoint)).mp
      11329      ((h _ rc).mpr (registered_has_value offPoint))))
      11330  
      11331  /-- Existence of a point off the critical line in a configuration S. -/
      11332  def OffLine (S : Config) : Prop := ∃ s, S s ∧ ¬ onLine s
      11333  
      11334  /-- The retracted image Rec S contains no point off the critical line. -/
      11335  theorem no_offline_zero_on_record (S : Config) : ¬ OffLine (Rec S) :=
      11336    fun ⟨q, hq, hoff⟩ => hoff (the_remembered_is_lossless S q hq)
      11337  
      11338  /-- Negation of Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis is equivalent to an off-line point in ZetaZeros. -/
      11339  theorem offline_zero_iff_not_rh : OffLine ZetaZeros ↔ ¬ RiemannHypothesis := by
      11340    rw [h_read_proved]
      11341    constructor
      11342    · rintro ⟨s, hs, hoff⟩ hv
      11343      exact hoff (hv s hs)
      11344    · intro hnot
      11345      apply Classical.byContradiction
      11346      intro hno
      11347      apply hnot
      11348      intro s hs
      11349      apply Classical.byContradiction
      11350      intro hoff
      11351      exact hno ⟨s, hs, hoff⟩
      11352  
      11353  /-- Σ₁ refuter seal over ℂ: where refutation requires an off-line zero, non-refutation seals RH. -/
      11354  theorem no_offline_refuter_seals_rh
      11355      (Prov : Prop → Prop)
      11356      (sigma1 : OffLine ZetaZeros → Prov (¬ RiemannHypothesis))
      11357      (h_no_refute : ¬ Prov (¬ RiemannHypothesis)) :
      11358      RiemannHypothesis := by
      11359    apply Classical.byContradiction
      11360    intro hnot
      11361    exact h_no_refute (sigma1 (offline_zero_iff_not_rh.mpr hnot))

# The Self-Grounding Recursion and the Five-Way Loop

## The root

Part I of the file is `TOE_Zero.lean`, carried verbatim with the leading sixteen hexadecimal digits of its SHA-256 recorded in the seed header the file carries at lines 48 to 84; it was written for core Lean with no import and no axiom, and is compiled here under the Mathlib imports of lines 1 to 4. A self-grounding root for a proposition $R$ is a structure `SelfGrounding R` with a type of acts, its field `Act`, which any type may fill, `Unit` for $\mathrm{RA}_0$ and `ActualZeros` for the cargo of Theorem 6.2, one act, and a map from acts to proofs of $R$. A proposition is self-verifying when its denial hands it over: $\mathrm{SelfVerifying}(P) :\Longleftrightarrow \neg P \to P$.

**Theorem 6.1** (`seated_undeniable`, `denial_instantiates`, `external_proof_adds_nothing`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> $\varnothing$\])**.** For every $R$ and every $G : \texttt{SelfGrounding}\,R$: $R$ holds; $R$ is self-verifying; and for every proposition $Q$, $(Q \to R) \leftrightarrow R$.

The constructed root is $\mathrm{RA}_0 :\Longleftrightarrow \forall x : \mathrm{Unit},\ 0 < \Delta E_0\,x$ with $\Delta E_0 \equiv 1$; its one act is the unit, and `root_on_the_constructed_domain` proves $\mathrm{RA}_0$ with an empty cone. The three theorems are the engine the recursion below runs on: a proposition with a self-grounding root holds, holds under its own denial, and absorbs any premise.

**Listing 6. The self-grounding root (Part I)** (master lines 106 to 146)

        106  /-! ## I · The self-grounding root: the Omega Boundary -/
        107  
        108  /-- A self-grounding root: acts occur, and every act instances the root. -/
        109  structure SelfGrounding (R : Prop) where
        110    Act       : Type
        111    anAct     : Act
        112    instances : Act → R
        113  
        114  /-- A proposition whose denial hands it over. -/
        115  def SelfVerifying (P : Prop) : Prop := ¬P → P
        116  
        117  /-- THE OMEGA BOUNDARY: every denial of the root is an act, and re-enacts it. -/
        118  theorem denial_reenacts_root {R : Prop} (G : SelfGrounding R) (denial : G.Act) : R := G.instances denial
        119  
        120  /-- EXISTENCE PROVES EXISTENCE ONLY BY MOTION: the root is held by the act itself. -/
        121  theorem seated_undeniable {R : Prop} (G : SelfGrounding R) : R := G.instances G.anAct
        122  
        123  /-- No external proof adds anything to the root. -/
        124  theorem external_proof_adds_nothing {R : Prop} (G : SelfGrounding R) (Q : Prop) : (Q → R) ↔ R :=
        125    ⟨fun _ => G.instances G.anAct, fun r _ => r⟩
        126  
        127  /-- The deed of denying the root hands it over. -/
        128  theorem denial_instantiates {R : Prop} (G : SelfGrounding R) : SelfVerifying R := fun _ => G.instances G.anAct
        129  
        130  /-- THE FLOOR IS UNIVERSAL: for every root that grounds itself, the root holds, every act re-enacts it, and no
        131      external proof adds to it. -/
        132  theorem the_floor_is_universal :
        133      ∀ (R : Prop) (G : SelfGrounding R), R ∧ (∀ _ : G.Act, R) ∧ (∀ Q : Prop, (Q → R) ↔ R) :=
        134    fun _ G => ⟨seated_undeniable G, denial_reenacts_root G, external_proof_adds_nothing G⟩
        135  
        136  /-! ## II · The constructed root -/
        137  
        138  /-- The Root Axiom on the constructed one-point domain: its one existent actuates, at positive energy. -/
        139  def ΔE₀ : Unit → Int := fun _ => 1
        140  def RA₀ : Prop := ∀ x : Unit, 0 < ΔE₀ x
        141  
        142  /-- The constructed domain grounds its root: its one act is a deed, and the deed actuates. -/
        143  def ra₀ : SelfGrounding RA₀ := ⟨Unit, (), fun _ _ => show (0 : Int) < 1 by decide⟩
        144  
        145  /-- THE ROOT ON THE CONSTRUCTED DOMAIN, A THEOREM. -/
        146  theorem root_on_the_constructed_domain : RA₀ := seated_undeniable ra₀

## The cargo

**Theorem 6.2** (`ra_cargo_self_grounding`, `ra_recursion_at_record`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** The term $\langle \mathrm{ActualZeros},\ \mathrm{formal\_act}\ \mathrm{ZetaZeros},\ \lambda\_.\,\mathrm{cargo\_at\_zeros}\rangle$ is a self-grounding root for $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$. Consequently $$\begin{aligned}
&\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\ \wedge\ \mathrm{SelfVerifying}\bigl(\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\bigr)\\
\wedge\ &\forall Q,\ \bigl(Q \to \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\bigr) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros}).
\end{aligned}$$

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* Apply `TOE0.seated_undeniable`, `TOE0.denial_instantiates` and `TOE0.external_proof_adds_nothing` to the closed term. ◻

</div>

At the record least erasure is unconditional, logically self-verifying, and absorbs every external premise. The same recursion runs on the discrete chart in Part IX with an empty cone (Section 8).

## The fiber section

**Theorem 6.3** (`classes_coincide_under_ra_zeta`, `ra_coincidence_iff_rh`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> c / t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** $(\forall s,\ \mathrm{ZetaZeros}\,s \to \mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\,s) \leftrightarrow \texttt{RiemannHypothesis}$: containment of the nontrivial zeros in their own retracted image is necessary and sufficient for the hypothesis.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* Forward: a zero inside the record lies on the line by `the_remembered_is_lossless`. Backward: under the hypothesis each zero is its own retraction by `reg_eq_self_iff`, hence its own witness in $\mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$. ◻

</div>

## The five faces

**Theorem 6.4** (`zeta_ra_loop`, the five-way fixed-point loop  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** $$\begin{aligned}
&\bigl(\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \to \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\bigr) \ \leftrightarrow\ \mathrm{RH}\\
\wedge\ &\bigl(\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\bigr) \ \leftrightarrow\ \mathrm{RH}\\
\wedge\ &\bigl(\forall q,\ \mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\,q \leftrightarrow \mathrm{ZetaZeros}\,q\bigr) \ \leftrightarrow\ \mathrm{RH}\\
\wedge\ &\bigl(\forall s,\ \mathrm{ZetaZeros}\,s \to \mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\,s\bigr) \ \leftrightarrow\ \mathrm{RH}\\
\wedge\ &\ \mathrm{SelfVerifying}(\mathrm{RH}) \ \leftrightarrow\ \mathrm{RH},
\end{aligned}$$ where $\mathrm{RH}$ is Mathlib’s `RiemannHypothesis`.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* The first face is `transport_zeta` at $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}$ composed with `h_read_proved`. The second follows from the first since the left side of the biconditional, $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$, is `cargo_at_zeros`. The third is `rh_iff_fixed_point_of_rec`. The fourth is `ra_coincidence_iff_rh`. The fifth is classical: $(\neg\mathrm{RH}\to \mathrm{RH}) \to \mathrm{RH}$ by contradiction, and $\mathrm{RH}\to (\neg\mathrm{RH}\to \mathrm{RH})$ by weakening. ◻

</div>

The five faces are one object seen five ways. The transport face: carrying retraction invariance from the record to the zeros is equivalent to the hypothesis; the file’s header displays this face as the normal form of the hypothesis, the analytic distribution of the zeros translated into the fixed-point domain of the retraction over $\mathbb{C}$, and reads it as a normalization in the sense in which Fermat’s Last Theorem was reduced to the modularity of semistable elliptic curves. The biconditional face: since the record’s least erasure is a theorem, the record and the zeros agree on least erasure exactly when the hypothesis holds. The set-level face: the zero set is a fixed point of $\mathrm{Rec}$ exactly when the hypothesis holds. The section face: the zero set sits inside its own record exactly when the hypothesis holds. The self-verification face: the hypothesis is self-verifying exactly when it holds. The record side of the transport and biconditional faces, $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$, is supplied at no cost by the recursion of Theorem 6.2; the set-level and section faces compare the zero set with the record $\mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$ itself, and the self-verification face states the hypothesis in the self-verifying form $\neg P \to P$ of Part I, the form in which the root is undeniable in act (`TOE0.denial_instantiates`). What the first four faces state is the exact identity between the hypothesis and the unprojected side.

**Theorem 6.5** (`rh_from_the_cargo_loop`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> c · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** From the 1-bit fixed-point bridge $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \to \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$: `RiemannHypothesis`.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* The first face of Theorem 6.4, read from left to right (`zeta_ra_loop.1.mp`). ◻

</div>

This is the passage from the record to the zeros, which the file calls the normal form applied: on Part III’s discrete chart every proof of the value at a closed configuration is a supply of the act’s field (`RememberedOffered.the_atomic_necessity`), and the form of that proof is the hypothesis itself (`RememberedOffered.the_form_is_the_hypothesis`); over $\mathbb{C}$ the type is the theorem above. The bridge is the theorem’s printed hypothesis; its antecedent $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$ is supplied with no hypothesis by the recursion of Theorem 6.2; and by Theorem 6.4 the bridge is equivalent to the hypothesis, its fixed-point form. Every theorem of the file that concludes `RiemannHypothesis` prints its hypotheses in its signature: the 1-bit bridge here, section inclusion in Theorem 6.3, a reflection closure and retraction injectivity in Theorem 7.11, retraction injectivity of the zeros in Theorem 7.12, their closure being a theorem, the look back in Theorem 7.19, provability premises in `no_offline_refuter_seals_rh`, and the reading of the look back with the physical capstone’s premises in Theorem 7.28, which concludes $\mathrm{LookBack} \wedge \texttt{RiemannHypothesis}$.

## The eleven-part binding and the transfer status

**Theorem 6.6** (`zeta_binding`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** The following eleven statements hold as one conjunction:

1.  $\mathrm{RH}\leftrightarrow \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$ (`h_id_proved`);

2.  $\mathrm{RH}\leftrightarrow (\forall q,\ \mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\,q \leftrightarrow \mathrm{ZetaZeros}\,q)$ (`rh_iff_fixed_point_of_rec`);

3.  $\forall s,\ \mathrm{CompletedZetaZeros}\,s \to \mathrm{CompletedZetaZeros}(1-s)$;

4.  $\mathrm{Closed}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$;

5.  $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$;

6.  $\forall q,\ \mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\,q \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\,q$;

7.  $\neg\mathrm{OffLine}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$;

8.  $(\exists Z : \mathrm{ActualZeros},\ Z.\mathrm{zeros} = \mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Value}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$;

9.  $(\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \to \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Value}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$;

10. $(\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{RH}$;

11. $(\forall s,\ \mathrm{ZetaZeros}\,s \to \mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\,s) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{RH}$.

**Theorem 6.7** (`mathlib_transfer_status`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** $$\begin{aligned}
&(\mathrm{RH}\leftrightarrow \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})) \ \wedge\ \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\\
\wedge\ &\bigl((\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \to \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{RH}\bigr).
\end{aligned}$$

The transfer status answers, at theorem grade, the objection that results about the file’s own structures do not transfer to Mathlib’s hypothesis. The transfer is the equivalence itself, and what separates the retrospective record from Mathlib’s sentence is a proposition equivalent to that sentence.

## Analytic faces

An analytic face is any proposition proved equivalent to `RiemannHypothesis`: a structure `AnalyticFace` with a sentence and a proof of `RiemannHypothesis ↔ sentence`.

**Theorem 6.8** (`analytic_face_is_least_erasure`, `analytic_face_is_transport_gap`, `analytic_face_vocabulary_law`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** For every analytic face $F$ and every proposition $P$: $$\begin{aligned}
F.\mathrm{sentence} &\leftrightarrow \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros}),\\
F.\mathrm{sentence} &\leftrightarrow \bigl(\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \to \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\bigr),\\
(F.\mathrm{sentence} \to P) &\leftrightarrow (\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \to P),\\
(P \to F.\mathrm{sentence}) &\leftrightarrow (P \to \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})).
\end{aligned}$$

Every complex-analytic reformulation of the hypothesis is deductively interchangeable with the retraction fixed-point identity, in both directions, against any premise and toward any conclusion. No vocabulary bypasses least erasure.

# Functional-Equation Closure, Orbit Collapse, Chart Homomorphism

## Strip equivalence, the functional equation and Schwarz reflection

Mathlib supplies $\Lambda(1-s) = \Lambda(s)$ as `completedRiemannZeta_one_sub`, the relation $\zeta(s) = \Lambda(s)/\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)$ for $s \neq 0$ as `riemannZeta_def_of_ne_zero`, and the non-vanishing of $\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}$ on $\operatorname{Re} s > 0$ as `Gammaℝ_ne_zero_of_re_pos`.

**Theorem 7.1** (`completed_zeta_zeros_symm`, `completed_zeta_zeros_closed_pt`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** $\mathrm{CompletedZetaZeros}$ is closed under $s \mapsto 1-s$.

**Theorem 7.2** (`zeta_zero_iff_completed_of_re_pos`, `zeta_zeros_iff_completed_in_strip`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** For $\operatorname{Re} s > 0$, $\zeta(s) = 0 \leftrightarrow \Lambda(s) = 0$. For $0 < \operatorname{Re} s < 1$, $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}(s) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{CompletedZetaZeros}(s)$.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* On $\operatorname{Re} s > 0$ the point is nonzero and $\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s) \neq 0$, so the quotient vanishes exactly when $\Lambda(s)$ does. Inside the strip a point is neither $0$, nor $1$, nor a trivial zero, since every trivial zero has real part at most $-2$; the two triples of side conditions therefore coincide. ◻

</div>

**Theorem 7.3** (`zeta_zeros_symm_in_strip`, `strip_zeta_zeros_closed_pt`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** If $0 < \operatorname{Re} s < 1$ and $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}(s)$ then $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}(1-s)$. The set $\mathrm{StripZetaZeros} := \mathrm{ZetaZeros}\cap \{0 < \operatorname{Re} s < 1\}$ is closed under $s \mapsto 1-s$.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* Pass to $\Lambda$ inside the strip, reflect by `completedRiemannZeta_one_sub`, and return; the reflected point is again inside the strip. ◻

</div>

Over the whole plane the file proves the reflection from the functional equation of $\zeta$ itself, which Mathlib states as `riemannZeta_one_sub`, $$\zeta(1-s) = 2\,(2\pi)^{-s}\,\Gamma(s)\cos(\pi s/2)\,\zeta(s) \qquad (s \notin \{0,-1,-2,\dots\},\ s \neq 1),$$ and proves Schwarz reflection on the pinned release. Mathlib supplies also the non-vanishing of $\zeta$ on $\operatorname{Re} s > 1$ (`riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_one_lt_re`, imported on line 2), its Dirichlet series there (`zeta_eq_tsum_one_div_nat_cpow`), its differentiability away from $1$ (`differentiableAt_riemannZeta`), the identity theorem for analytic functions on a preconnected set (`AnalyticOnNhd.eqOn_of_preconnected_of_eventuallyEq`), and the connectedness of the complement of a point in a real vector space of rank above one (`isConnected_compl_singleton_of_one_lt_rank`, imported on line 3).

**Theorem 7.4** (`differentiableAt_star_comp`, `star_natCast_cpow`, `zeta_schwarz_reflection`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** If $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ is complex-differentiable at $\bar x$, then $y \mapsto \overline{f(\bar y)}$ is complex-differentiable at $x$. For $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and $t \in \mathbb{C}$, $\overline{n^{\bar t}} = n^{t}$. For $s \neq 1$, $\zeta(\bar s) = \overline{\zeta(s)}$.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* The functions $y \mapsto \overline{\zeta(\bar y)}$ and $\zeta$ are analytic on $\mathbb{C}\setminus\{1\}$, the first by the first statement. On $\operatorname{Re} s > 1$, a neighborhood of $2$, they agree term by term on the Dirichlet series by the second. The set $\mathbb{C}\setminus\{1\}$ is connected, $\mathbb{C}$ having real rank two, so the identity theorem makes them agree on all of it. ◻

</div>

**Theorem 7.5** (`zeta_ne_zero_neg_odd`, `zeta_zeros_not_neg_nat`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** For every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, $\zeta(-(2k+1)) \neq 0$. No nontrivial zero is a nonpositive integer: if $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}(s)$, then $s \neq -n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* At $w = 2k+2$ the functional equation writes $\zeta(-(2k+1)) = \zeta(1-w)$ as the product of $2$, $(2\pi)^{-w}$, $\Gamma(w)$ with $\operatorname{Re} w > 0$, $\cos(\pi(k+1)) = (-1)^{k+1}$ and $\zeta(w)$ with $\operatorname{Re} w > 1$, none of them zero. For the second statement, $s = 0$ is excluded by $\zeta(0) = -\tfrac12$, $s = -2(m+1)$ by the definition of $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}$, and $s = -(2k+1)$ by the first. ◻

</div>

**Theorem 7.6** (`zeta_zeros_symm`, `zeta_zeros_closed_pt`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** If $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}(s)$ then $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}(1-s)$: the nontrivial zero set is closed under $s \mapsto 1-s$ on the whole plane.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* A nontrivial zero is no nonpositive integer, by Theorem 7.5, and is not $1$, so the functional equation applies and $\zeta(1-s)$ is a multiple of $\zeta(s) = 0$. The point $1-s$ is no trivial zero, since $1-s = -2(m+1)$ would give $\operatorname{Re} s = 2m+3 > 1$, where $\zeta$ does not vanish; and $1-s \neq 1$, since $s \neq 0$. ◻

</div>

**Theorem 7.7** (`zeta_zeros_conj`, `zeta_zeros_closed`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** If $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}(s)$ then $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}(\bar s)$; and $\mathrm{Closed}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$: the nontrivial zero set is closed under the fold $s \mapsto 1-\bar s$ of the complex chart, with no hypothesis.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* By Theorem 7.4, $\zeta(\bar s) = \overline{\zeta(s)} = 0$, and conjugation fixes the excluded points $1$ and $-2(m+1)$. The fold is conjugation followed by $s \mapsto 1-s$, and Theorem 7.6 closes the zeros under the second. ◻

</div>

**Theorem 7.8** (`zeta_zeros_in_strip`, `zeta_zeros_iff_strip`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** If $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}(s)$ then $0 \le \operatorname{Re} s \le 1$; and $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}= \{\, s \mid (0 \le \operatorname{Re} s \le 1) \wedge \mathrm{ZetaZeros}(s) \,\}$.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* $\zeta$ does not vanish on $\operatorname{Re} s > 1$, so $\operatorname{Re} s \le 1$; the same applied to the zero $1-s$ of Theorem 7.6 gives $\operatorname{Re} s \ge 0$. ◻

</div>

Theorem 7.3 closes the zeros inside the open strip through the completed function; Theorems 7.6 and 7.7 close the whole zero set, under $s \mapsto 1-s$ from the functional equation of $\zeta$ and under the fold by Schwarz reflection, and Theorem 7.8 places every nontrivial zero in the closed strip $0 \le \operatorname{Re} s \le 1$. The closure $\mathrm{Closed}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$ that the orbit collapse of Section 7.2 asks at the zeros is therefore a theorem of the file.

## Retraction injectivity and orbit collapse

**Definition 7.9.** $\mathrm{RetractionInjective}(S) :\Longleftrightarrow \forall p\,q,\ S\,p \to S\,q \to \mathrm{reg}p = \mathrm{reg}q \to p = q$: no two distinct points of $S$ register at the same point of the line.

**Theorem 7.10** (`closed_retraction_injective_forces_value`, `value_implies_retraction_injective`, `closed_retraction_injective_iff_value`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** On every reflection-closed $S \subseteq \mathbb{C}$: $\mathrm{RetractionInjective}(S) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Value}(S)$ and $\mathrm{RetractionInjective}(S) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{LeastErasure}(S)$.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* Let $s \in S$. By closure $\mathrm{fold}s \in S$; by `reg_fold` the two register at one point; injectivity forces $\mathrm{fold}s = s$, which is $\mathrm{onLine}\,s$ by `fold_fixed_iff_onLine`. Conversely, under the value the retraction is the identity on $S$ and so injective. ◻

</div>

If $\mathrm{Closed}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$ and $\mathrm{RetractionInjective}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$, then $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \wedge \texttt{RiemannHypothesis}$.

The orbit-collapse theorem names, for any reflection-closed set, the exact geometric content of the value: no conjugate pair survives registration. On the record this holds without hypothesis. **Theorem 7.12** (`retraction_injective_iff_rh`, `rh_from_retraction_injective`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t / c · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** $\mathrm{RetractionInjective}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \leftrightarrow \texttt{RiemannHypothesis}$. If $\mathrm{RetractionInjective}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$, then $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \wedge \texttt{RiemannHypothesis}$.

The four readings of the bit at the zeros are bound in one theorem, which the file calls the cone. </div>

Mathlib’s hypothesis is the apex and each reading a leg proved equivalent to it, so any two readings are equivalent, and any further proposition proved equivalent to the apex lands on the same four. The last statement holds the record side of the bit, a theorem, beside its reading at the zeros, the hypothesis: one bit, read twice.

## The discrete chart embeds in the plane

Parts III, IV-b, VII, VIII and IX work, and the optional section of Part VIII-b reads its points and line, on the discrete offset chart $\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}$, a point $(d,t)$ being offset $d$ from the line at height $t$, with $\mathrm{fold}(d,t) = (-d,t)$, $\mathrm{reg}(d,t) = (0,t)$ and $\mathrm{onLine}(d,t) \leftrightarrow d = 0$; Part I’s chart is the coordinate range (`TOE0.chart`) of a grid of quaternions (`TOE0.quats`) whose conjugation-fixed set is the scalar line, Parts II, IV and V and the carried time kernel of Part IV-c place their line at other abscissae with their own folds, the judge probe of Part IV-c restating its test on the offset chart, Part V-b maps charts equivariantly into the offset chart (`Charts.Equivariant`, `Charts.transport`), and Part VI binds the results. Define $\varphi_{\mathbb{C}}(d,t) := \bigl(\tfrac12 + \tfrac d8\bigr) + it$.

**Theorem 7.15** (`discrete_chart_embeds_in_complex`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** For every discrete point $p$: $\varphi_{\mathbb{C}}(\mathrm{fold}p) = \mathrm{fold}(\varphi_{\mathbb{C}} p)$, $\varphi_{\mathbb{C}}(\mathrm{reg}p) = \mathrm{reg}(\varphi_{\mathbb{C}} p)$, and $\mathrm{onLine}(\varphi_{\mathbb{C}} p) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{onLine}(p)$.

The chart of Part IX therefore maps equivariantly into $\mathbb{C}$, the other offset-chart parts writing their copies by the same three equations, and nothing in them is altered to say so. Part VIII’s carrier enters the plane by the same map; write $\kappa$ for `carrier_to_zero`, the inverse of `map_zero_to_carrier` of Section 9.6.

**Theorem 7.16** (`carrier_embeds_in_complex`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** For every carrier state $c$: $\varphi_{\mathbb{C}}(\kappa(C\,c)) = \mathrm{fold}(\varphi_{\mathbb{C}}(\kappa\,c))$, $\varphi_{\mathbb{C}}(\kappa(\mathrm{annihilate}\,c)) = \mathrm{reg}(\varphi_{\mathbb{C}}(\kappa\,c))$, and $\mathrm{Neutral}(c) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{onLine}(\varphi_{\mathbb{C}}(\kappa\,c))$.

Charge conjugation becomes the complex fold, annihilation the complex retraction, and the neutral sector the points of the critical line: the locus of the physical closure is carried into the locus of the formal closure by a theorem of the file.

## Pause and look back: the unconditional retrospective seal

Section X-l of the file runs the retrospective arc over $\mathbb{C}$ in two movements, a pause at the record, proved with no premise, and a look back onto the zeros, proved equivalent to the hypothesis, and closes on the canonical apex, the Monism witness over $\mathbb{C}$, the analytic target reduction, the joint physico-formal seal, Round 2 and the analytic route, the Ground-On-Line loop and the self-recognition closure.

**Definition 7.17** (the pause and the look back)**.** $\mathrm{Pause} :\Longleftrightarrow \forall s,\ \mathrm{ZetaZeros}\,s \to \mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})(\mathrm{reg}(s)) \wedge \mathrm{reg}(\mathrm{reg}(s)) = \mathrm{reg}(s) \wedge \mathrm{reg}(\mathrm{fold}(s)) = \mathrm{reg}(s)$ and $\mathrm{LookBack} :\Longleftrightarrow \forall s,\ \mathrm{ZetaZeros}\,s \to \mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})(\mathrm{reg}(s)) \to \mathrm{reg}(s) = s$.

**Theorem 7.18** (`no_closed_principle_decides`, `pause_is_unconditional`, `forward_pass_unconditional`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** For every predicate $D$ on configurations with $\forall S,\ \mathrm{Closed}(S) \to D(S)$: $\neg\,\forall S,\ \mathrm{Closed}(S) \to D(S) \to \mathrm{Value}(S)$. The pause holds. And $$\begin{aligned}
&\mathrm{FreedomRoot} \wedge \mathrm{Closed}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \wedge (\forall s,\ \mathrm{ZetaZeros}\,s \to 0 \le \operatorname{Re} s \le 1)\\
\wedge\ &\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \wedge \mathrm{SelfVerifying}(\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})) \wedge \mathrm{Pause}.
\end{aligned}$$

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* The pair world of an off-line point is reflection-closed, so it satisfies every principle all closed configurations share, and it lacks the value. A zero $s$ lands in the record at $\mathrm{reg}(s)$ as the image of itself, and `reg_idem` and `reg_fold` give the other two parts of the pause. The forward pass collects `BoundChain.freedom_root_inhabited` of Theorem 8.1, Theorems 7.7 and 7.8, `cargo_at_zeros`, the self-verification of Theorem 6.2 and the pause. ◻

</div>

**Theorem 7.19** (`look_back_is_the_closure`, `rh_from_pause_and_look_back`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t / c · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** $(\mathrm{LookBack} \leftrightarrow (\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \to \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros}))) \wedge (\mathrm{LookBack} \leftrightarrow \texttt{RiemannHypothesis})$. If $\mathrm{LookBack}$, then `RiemannHypothesis`.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* By the pause the antecedent $\mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})(\mathrm{reg}(s))$ holds at every zero, so $\mathrm{LookBack}$ is equivalent to $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$; the first face of `zeta_ra_loop` with `h_id_proved` gives the first part, `h_id_proved` the second, and the last statement reads the second from left to right. ◻

</div>

**Theorem 7.20** (`the_unconditional_retrospective_seal`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** With no premise the following hold as one conjunction: the forward pass of Theorem 7.18, its six parts from $\mathrm{FreedomRoot}$ to $\mathrm{Pause}$; $\mathrm{LookBack} \leftrightarrow \texttt{RiemannHypothesis}$; for every reading $r$ of the cone, $\mathrm{LookBack} \leftrightarrow \texttt{apexDiagram}\,r$; $(\exists Z : \texttt{ActualZeros},\ Z.\mathrm{zeros} = \mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{LookBack}$; for every proposition $Q$, if $Q \to \texttt{RiemannHypothesis}$ then $Q \to \mathrm{LookBack}$; and the impossibility over $\mathbb{C}$ of Theorem 7.18, that no principle shared by every reflection-closed configuration forces the value on all of them.

The seal is the anchor of the formal closure in this edition. Its forward pass, resting on Schwarz reflection and the non-vanishing of $\zeta$ at the negative odd integers, saturates the complex scaffold with no premise: the zeros are closed under the fold and confined to the closed strip, their record is lossless and self-verifying, and at the pause every nontrivial zero is registered at $\mathrm{reg}(s)$ in its record, the retraction idempotent there and a conjugate pair colliding there. Its impossibility conjunct refutes over $\mathbb{C}$, by theorem, every zero-bit derivation valid at every reflection-closed configuration from what those configurations share, so the halt at the bit is a proved boundary of that class of derivation and not a defect. Its atomic-necessity conjunct states, as the right-to-left direction of $\mathrm{LookBack} \leftrightarrow \texttt{RiemannHypothesis}$, that any proof of `RiemannHypothesis` from any premise $Q$, $Q := \mathrm{True}$ among them, yields $\mathrm{LookBack}$, and with the socket conjunct an inhabitant of the socket, and by the cone the look back, least erasure, retraction injectivity, section inclusion and the socket are equivalent. What remains is the look back, with zero remainder: Mathlib’s `RiemannHypothesis` is equivalent to $\mathrm{LookBack}$, the one bit $\mathrm{reg}(s) = s$ at every zero, read at the pause, and `rh_from_pause_and_look_back` returns Mathlib’s `RiemannHypothesis` from it in one step, at tier <span class="smallcaps">c</span>, as the file prints it.

**Definition 7.21** (the canonical record hypothesis)**.** $\mathrm{CanonicalRH} :\Longleftrightarrow \mathrm{Value}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$: every point of the retracted record of the zeros lies on the critical line.

**Theorem 7.22** (`canonical_rh_unconditional`, `canonical_property_holds_off_the_line`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** $\mathrm{CanonicalRH}$, with no premise; and $\mathrm{Value}(\mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{pairWorld}(\mathrm{offPoint})))$, at the reflection-closed pair world of the off point of Section 5.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* Both are `the_remembered_is_lossless` of Theorem 4.2, at $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}$ and at the pair world: the retraction lands on the line (`reg_lands`). ◻

</div>

The canonical apex is the record side of the bit in the value form: every point of the projected zero set lies on the critical line, with no premise. It is not the apex of the cone of Theorem 7.14: the record of every configuration has the same property (Theorem 4.2), a reflection-closed one with a point off the line among them, so the canonical apex is the projection-side invariant, as the file names it, and by itself decides nothing about where the zeros lie. The look back is the step from the projection to the zeros themselves, and it is proved equivalent to `RiemannHypothesis` (Theorem 7.19).

**Definition 7.23** (the Monism witness over $\mathbb{C}$)**.** For a configuration $S \subseteq \mathbb{C}$, $\mathrm{RootReadTwice}(S) :\Longleftrightarrow \mathrm{MonismWitness}(n \mapsto \mathrm{Value}(S))$: Part III’s witness, one involution constructed, one principle uniform in $n$ and one seed, read at the constant principle $\mathrm{Value}(S)$.

&\mathrm{SameRecord}(\mathrm{registered}(\mathrm{offPoint}), \mathrm{pairWorld}(\mathrm{offPoint}))\\
\wedge\ &\mathrm{RootReadTwice}(\mathrm{registered}(\mathrm{offPoint})) \wedge \neg\,\mathrm{RootReadTwice}(\mathrm{pairWorld}(\mathrm{offPoint})).

</div>

**Theorem 7.25** (`canonical_normal_form_bridge`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** With no premise: $$\begin{aligned}
&\mathrm{CanonicalRH} \wedge \mathrm{RootReadTwice}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\\
\wedge\ &((\mathrm{CanonicalRH} \to \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})) \leftrightarrow \texttt{RiemannHypothesis})\\

<div class="proof">

The witness separates two configurations of one record over $\mathbb{C}$ as it does on Part III’s chart, the line-bound configuration carrying it and the off-line pair world not, and on every configuration it is equivalent to the value. The canonical normal-form bridge states the canonical apex and the witness at the record as theorems and puts the passage to the zeros in two forms, carrying the canonical apex to least erasure of the zeros and equating it with the witness there; each form is proved equivalent to Mathlib’s `RiemannHypothesis`. At the zeros the witness is proved equivalent to the look back (Theorem 7.27), the 1-bit apex the terminal block names.

**Definition 7.26** (the right half-strip)**.** $\mathrm{RightHalfStripZeroFree} :\Longleftrightarrow \forall s,\ \mathrm{ZetaZeros}\,s \to \tfrac12 < \operatorname{Re} s \to \bot$: no nontrivial zero lies to the right of the critical line.

**Theorem 7.27** (`euler_product_boundary`, `analytic_target_reduction`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** For every nontrivial zero $s$, $0 \le \operatorname{Re} s \le 1$ and $\neg(1 < \operatorname{Re} s)$. With no premise, writing $H$ for $\mathrm{RightHalfStripZeroFree}$: $$\begin{aligned}
&\mathrm{CanonicalRH} \wedge \mathrm{RootReadTwice}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\\
\wedge\ &(\forall s,\ \mathrm{ZetaZeros}\,s \to (0 \le \operatorname{Re} s \le 1) \wedge \neg(1 < \operatorname{Re} s))\\
\wedge\ &(H \leftrightarrow \mathrm{RetractionInjective}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})) \wedge (H \leftrightarrow \mathrm{LookBack})\\
\wedge\ &(H \leftrightarrow \mathrm{RootReadTwice}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})) \wedge ((\mathrm{CanonicalRH} \to H) \leftrightarrow \texttt{RiemannHypothesis})\\
\wedge\ &(H \leftrightarrow \texttt{RiemannHypothesis}).
\end{aligned}$$

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* The boundary is strip confinement (Theorem 7.8), whose right edge is Mathlib’s non-vanishing of $\zeta$ on $\operatorname{Re} s > 1$ from the Dirichlet series and the Euler product. For the last part, $H$ excludes a zero to the right of the line, and the fold, under which the zeros are closed (Theorem 7.7), carries a zero to the left of it to one at real part $1 - \operatorname{Re} s > \tfrac12$, which $H$ excludes as well; so every zero lies on the line, which gives `RiemannHypothesis` by `h_read_proved`, and conversely a zero on the line is not to its right. The remaining parts follow through Theorems 7.12, 7.19, 7.22 and 7.24. ◻

</div>

The analytic target reduction states the bit as a question about one region. With no premise, Mathlib’s `RiemannHypothesis`, the look back, retraction injectivity of the zeros and the witness at the zeros are each equivalent to $\mathrm{RightHalfStripZeroFree}$, which by strip confinement is the absence of nontrivial zeros from the right half-strip $\tfrac12 < \operatorname{Re} s \le 1$, whose right edge the Euler product fixes; the fold carries the left half of the strip onto the right, so the whole of the bit stands in one half-strip against that boundary. The canonical apex enters as an antecedent the file proves, so carrying it to the half-strip is equivalent to the hypothesis.

**Theorem 7.28** (`physico_formal_supplies_look_back_and_rh`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> c · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** For a configuration $Z_\zeta$ of Part III’s discrete chart, on which the capstone of Section 9 reads, from the reading $h_{\mathrm{read}} : \mathrm{LookBack} \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Value}(Z_\zeta)$, the value taken on that chart, vacuum realization $h_{\mathrm{realize}}$, the population floor $h_{\mathrm{pop}}$, the rate floor $h_{\mathrm{rate}}$, the temperature floor $h_{\mathrm{temp}} : T \ge T_0$, the coupling $h_{\mathrm{couple}}$, a certified bound $B$ and the gap $h_{\mathrm{gap}} : B.\varepsilon < \texttt{detectionGap}(n_0, r_0, T_0)$: $$\mathrm{LookBack} \wedge \texttt{RiemannHypothesis}.$$

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* The concrete capstone, Theorem 9.14, at $\mathrm{ClassicalRH} := \mathrm{LookBack}$ returns the look back, and Theorem 7.19 returns `RiemannHypothesis` from it. ◻

</div>

The joint seal joins the two closures over $\mathbb{C}$. The concrete capstone is a schema in an abstract proposition $\mathrm{ClassicalRH}$; read at the look back, its printed premises, the reading among them, deliver the look back, the one bit the formal closure isolates, and Theorem 7.19 of the formal closure returns Mathlib’s `RiemannHypothesis` from it. Like Section X-i, the joint seal is a bridge between the closures: no capstone of either closure and neither binder of Theorems 9.17 and 10.1 uses it, and it is bound in the complex extensions.

Section X-l continues with Round 2 and the analytic route. **Theorem 7.29** (`round2_halted_uniduction`, `round2_residual_monism`, `round2_absolute_closure`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** With no premise: any two readings of the cone are equivalent, and on Part III’s discrete chart $\neg\,\forall S,\ \mathrm{Closed}(S) \to \mathrm{Value}(S)$; the separation of one record by the witness over $\mathbb{C}$, the third part of Theorem 7.24; and the two in one conjunction.

The two theorems type the closure of the analytic route. v3.0.23_CC and v3.0.24_CC add to Section X-l, before the terminal certification, the Ground-On-Line locus and the self-recognition closure. Write $\mathrm{freedomAxis}(s) :\Longleftrightarrow \mathrm{True}$, $\mathrm{ramAxis}(s) :\Longleftrightarrow \mathrm{fold}s = s$, $\mathrm{collapseAxis}(s) :\Longleftrightarrow \operatorname{Re} s - \tfrac12 = -(\operatorname{Re} s - \tfrac12)$, and $\mathrm{GOL} := \mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$, the projected zero set.

**Theorem 7.32** (`complex_three_axis_lock`, `gol_look_back_unconditional`, `ra_triaxial_gol_loop_unconditional`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** For every $s \in \mathbb{C}$, $\mathrm{freedomAxis}(s) \wedge \mathrm{ramAxis}(s) \wedge \mathrm{collapseAxis}(s) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{onLine}\,s$. Every point of $\mathrm{GOL}$ is fixed by $\mathrm{reg}$, fixed by $\mathrm{fold}$, and satisfies the three axes. With no premise, $$\begin{aligned}
&\mathrm{RA}_0 \wedge \mathrm{FreedomRoot} \wedge (\forall s,\ \text{the three axes at } s \leftrightarrow \mathrm{onLine}\,s)\\
\wedge\ &\mathrm{Pause} \wedge \mathrm{Value}(\mathrm{GOL}) \wedge \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{GOL}) \wedge \mathrm{SelfVerifying}(\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{GOL}))\\
\wedge\ &\mathrm{MonismWitness}(n \mapsto \mathrm{Value}(\mathrm{GOL})) \wedge (\mathrm{RA}_0 \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Value}(\mathrm{GOL})) \wedge (\mathrm{RA}_0 \leftrightarrow \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{GOL}))\\
\wedge\ &\bigl((\forall q,\ \mathrm{GOL}\,q \leftrightarrow \mathrm{ZetaZeros}\,q) \leftrightarrow \texttt{RiemannHypothesis}\bigr).
\end{aligned}$$

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* The reflection-seat axis, $\mathrm{ramAxis}$, holds on the line by `fold_fixed_iff_onLine`, the freedom axis holds trivially and the collapse axis holds on the line. A point of $\mathrm{GOL}$ is fixed by $\mathrm{reg}$ (`cargo_at_zeros`) and lies on the line (Theorem 4.2), so the fold and the axes hold there. The loop collects `TOE0.root_on_the_constructed_domain`, `BoundChain.freedom_root_inhabited`, the lock, the pause, Theorem 4.2 at $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}$, `cargo_at_zeros`, the self-verification of Theorem 6.2, the witness at a constant principle and `rh_iff_fixed_point_of_rec`; each biconditional with $\mathrm{RA}_0$ joins two propositions both proved with no premise. ◻

</div>

**Theorem 7.33** (`zeta_zeros_strictly_in_strip`, `completed_zeta_zeros_strictly_in_strip`, `zeta_zeros_iff_completed`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** Every nontrivial zero satisfies $0 < \operatorname{Re} s < 1$; every $s$ with $\Lambda(s) = 0$, $s \neq 0$ and $s \neq 1$ satisfies $0 < \operatorname{Re} s < 1$; and $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}(s) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{CompletedZetaZeros}(s)$ for every $s \in \mathbb{C}$.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* Mathlib’s non-vanishing of $\zeta$ on $\operatorname{Re} s \ge 1$, `riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_one_le_re`, imported on line 4, gives $\operatorname{Re} s < 1$, and the reflection $s \mapsto 1-s$ of Theorem 7.6 gives $0 < \operatorname{Re} s$; for $\Lambda$ the functional equation `completedRiemannZeta_one_sub` does the same through $\zeta(s) = \Lambda(s)/\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)$. Inside the strip the two sets coincide by Theorem 7.2. ◻

</div>

**Theorem 7.34** (`right_half_strip_zero_free_iff_band`, `rh_iff_band_zero_free`, `off_line_zero_has_band_twin`, `self_recognition_is_look_back`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** $\mathrm{RightHalfStripZeroFree} \leftrightarrow \forall s,\ \mathrm{ZetaZeros}\,s \to \neg(\tfrac12 < \operatorname{Re} s < 1)$, and `RiemannHypothesis` is equivalent to the same statement. Every nontrivial zero $s$ off the line has a twin $t$, a nontrivial zero with $\tfrac12 < \operatorname{Re} t < 1$ and $t = s$ or $t = \mathrm{fold}s$. And $\mathrm{LookBack} \leftrightarrow \forall s,\ \mathrm{ZetaZeros}\,s \to \mathrm{reg}s = s$.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* The band is the half-strip with its edge $\operatorname{Re} s = 1$ removed, which Theorem 7.33 excludes; the second statement composes the first with the last part of Theorem 7.27. A zero right of the line is its own twin, and one left of it has the twin $\mathrm{fold}s$, at real part $1 - \operatorname{Re} s$, by Theorem 7.7, the strict strip of Theorem 7.33 bounding both below $1$. The record clause of $\mathrm{LookBack}$ holds at every zero through the zero itself. ◻

</div>

**Theorem 7.35** (`the_self_recognition_closure`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** With no premise, four conjunctions hold as one. The floor: $\mathrm{RA}_0$, $\mathrm{FreedomRoot}$, $\mathrm{Pause}$, $\mathrm{CanonicalRH}$, every point of $\mathrm{GOL}$ fixed by $\mathrm{reg}$, and the three-axis lock at every point. What $\zeta$ carries: the strict strip of the nontrivial zeros, $\mathrm{Closed}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$, $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}\,s \leftrightarrow \mathrm{CompletedZetaZeros}\,s$ for every $s$, and the band twin of every zero off the line. The bit: $\mathrm{LookBack} \leftrightarrow \forall s,\ \mathrm{ZetaZeros}\,s \to \mathrm{reg}s = s$, and each of $\forall s,\ \mathrm{ZetaZeros}\,s \to \mathrm{reg}s = s$, $\forall q,\ \mathrm{GOL}\,q \leftrightarrow \mathrm{ZetaZeros}\,q$, $\mathrm{RetractionInjective}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$, $\mathrm{RootReadTwice}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$, $\mathrm{RightHalfStripZeroFree}$ and the zero-free band equivalent to `RiemannHypothesis`. And the routes: the statement of `every_route_passes_the_bit` and that of `no_closed_principle_decides` over $\mathbb{C}$.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* The floor collects `TOE0.root_on_the_constructed_domain`, `BoundChain.freedom_root_inhabited`, the pause of Theorem 7.18, the canonical apex of Theorem 7.22, `cargo_at_zeros` of Theorem 4.5 and the lock of Theorem 7.32; what $\zeta$ carries collects Theorem 7.33, Theorem 7.7 and the band twin of Theorem 7.34; the bit collects `self_recognition_is_look_back` and `rh_iff_band_zero_free` of Theorem 7.34, `h_id_proved`, `rh_iff_fixed_point_of_rec`, `retraction_injective_iff_rh` and two parts of Theorem 7.27; and the routes are Theorems 7.30 and 7.18. ◻

</div>

The closure binds the formal arc in one theorem with nothing before the colon. The bit it isolates is the self-recognition of the zeros, $\forall s,\ \mathrm{ZetaZeros}\,s \to \mathrm{reg}s = s$, which is $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$ by the definition of least erasure, equivalent to `RiemannHypothesis` by `h_id_proved` and to the look back by Theorem 7.34. Seven readings of the bit are equivalent to the hypothesis inside the one theorem, the look back among them through self-recognition, and every route to the hypothesis, from any premise, delivers the bit. The closure takes no physical premise; the joint seal of Theorem 7.28 is the theorem of the file that supplies the look back from the reading and the physical premises.

      11482  
      11483  /-- Point reflection s ↦ 1 - s is an involution on ℂ. -/
      11484  theorem foldPt_involutive (s : Point) : foldPt (foldPt s) = s := by
      11485    unfold foldPt
      11486    ring
      11487  
      11488  /-- Point-reflection closure on complex configurations: invariant under s ↦ 1 - s. -/
      11489  def ClosedPt (S : Config) : Prop := ∀ s, S s → S (foldPt s)
      11490  
      11491  /-- Unconditional functional-equation closure of CompletedZetaZeros under s ↦ 1 - s. -/
      11492  theorem completed_zeta_zeros_closed_pt : ClosedPt CompletedZetaZeros :=
      11493    completed_zeta_zeros_symm
      11494  
      11495  /-- First-principles bridge from Mathlib's riemannZeta_def_of_ne_zero and Gammaℝ_ne_zero_of_re_pos:
      11496      at any complex point with 0 < Re s, riemannZeta s = 0 iff completedRiemannZeta s = 0. -/
      11497  theorem zeta_zero_iff_completed_of_re_pos {s : Point} (hre : 0 < s.re) :
      11498      riemannZeta s = 0 ↔ completedRiemannZeta s = 0 := by
      11499    have hs0 : s ≠ 0 := by
      11500      intro h0
      11501      rw [h0, zero_re] at hre
      11502      exact lt_irrefl 0 hre
      11503    have hG : Gammaℝ s ≠ 0 := Gammaℝ_ne_zero_of_re_pos hre
      11504    rw [riemannZeta_def_of_ne_zero hs0, div_eq_zero_iff]
      11505    exact ⟨fun h => h.resolve_right hG, fun h => Or.inl h⟩
      11506  
      11507  /-- Inside the critical strip 0 < Re s < 1, ZetaZeros s ↔ CompletedZetaZeros s.
      11508      Proved unconditionally from first principles using Mathlib's Gammaℝ non-vanishing. -/
      11509  theorem zeta_zeros_iff_completed_in_strip {s : Point} (h0 : 0 < s.re) (h1 : s.re < 1) :
      11510      ZetaZeros s ↔ CompletedZetaZeros s := by
      11511    have hs0 : s ≠ 0 := by
      11512      intro heq
      11513      rw [heq, zero_re] at h0
      11514      exact lt_irrefl 0 h0
      11515    have hs1 : s ≠ 1 := by
      11516      intro heq
      11517      rw [heq, one_re] at h1
      11518      exact lt_irrefl 1 h1
      11519    have h_not_trivial : ¬∃ n : ℕ, s = -2 * (n + 1) := by
      11520      rintro ⟨n, rfl⟩
      11521      have hneg : ((-2 : Point) * ((n : Point) + 1)).re ≤ 0 := by
      11522        have hcast : ((-2 : Point) * ((n : Point) + 1)) = (((-2 * ((n : ℝ) + 1)) : ℝ) : ℂ) := by
      11523          push_cast
      11524          ring
      11525        rw [hcast, Complex.ofReal_re]
      11526        have hnn : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) := Nat.cast_nonneg n
      11527        linarith
      11528      linarith
