      11552  /-! ### X-f . First-Principles Retraction Injectivity and Orbit Collapse over ℂ -/
      11553  
      11554  /-- Conjugate reflection fold (s ↦ 1 - star s) fixes a complex point iff Re s = 1/2. -/
      11555  theorem fold_fixed_iff_onLine (s : Point) : fold s = s ↔ onLine s := by
      11556    constructor
      11557    · intro h
      11558      have hre := congrArg Complex.re h
      11559      unfold fold onLine at *
      11560      simp only [sub_re, one_re, star_def, conj_re] at hre
      11561      linarith
      11562    · intro h
      11563      unfold onLine at h
      11564      apply Complex.ext
      11565      · unfold fold
      11566        simp only [sub_re, one_re, star_def, conj_re]
      11567        linarith
      11568      · unfold fold
      11569        simp only [sub_im, one_im, star_def, conj_im, zero_sub, neg_neg]
      11570  
      11571  /-- Retraction injectivity on a configuration S: no two distinct points of S project to
      11572      the same registered point on the critical line. -/
      11573  def RetractionInjective (S : Config) : Prop :=
      11574    ∀ p q, S p → S q → reg p = reg q → p = q
      11575  
      11576  /-- FIRST-PRINCIPLES ORBIT COLLAPSE THEOREM:
      11577      On any conjugate-reflection-closed configuration S (Closed S), if the retraction reg
      11578      is injective on S, then every point of S lies on the critical line (Value S).
      11579      Proof: For s ∈ S, closure gives fold s ∈ S. Since reg (fold s) = reg s, injectivity
      11580      forces fold s = s, which by fold_fixed_iff_onLine forces Re s = 1/2. -/
      11581  theorem closed_retraction_injective_forces_value {S : Config}
      11582      (h_closed : Closed S) (h_inj : RetractionInjective S) : Value S := by
      11583    intro s hs
      11584    have h_fold_in : S (fold s) := h_closed s hs
      11585    have h_reg_eq : reg (fold s) = reg s := reg_fold s
      11586    have h_fixed : fold s = s := h_inj (fold s) s h_fold_in hs h_reg_eq
      11587    exact (fold_fixed_iff_onLine s).mp h_fixed
      11588  
      11589  /-- Conversely, if Value S holds, then reg is the identity on S and hence injective on S. -/
      11590  theorem value_implies_retraction_injective {S : Config} (hv : Value S) :
      11591      RetractionInjective S := by
      11592    intro p q hp hq hreg
      11593    have hp_eq : reg p = p := (reg_eq_self_iff p).mpr (hv p hp)
      11594    have hq_eq : reg q = q := (reg_eq_self_iff q).mpr (hv q hq)
      11595    rw [← hp_eq, ← hq_eq, hreg]
      11596  
      11597  /-- THE BIJECTIVE FIBER EQUIVALENCE ON CLOSED COMPLEX CONFIGURATIONS:
      11598      For any reflection-closed S ⊆ ℂ, retraction injectivity, critical-line inclusion (Value),
      11599      and pointwise retraction invariance (LeastErasure) are mutually equivalent. -/
      11600  theorem closed_retraction_injective_iff_value {S : Config} (h_closed : Closed S) :
      11601      (RetractionInjective S ↔ Value S) ∧ (RetractionInjective S ↔ LeastErasure S) := by
      11602    have h1 : RetractionInjective S ↔ Value S :=
      11603      ⟨closed_retraction_injective_forces_value h_closed, value_implies_retraction_injective⟩
      11604    exact ⟨h1, h1.trans (twins_zeta S).symm⟩
      11605  
      11606  /-- Retraction injectivity holds unconditionally on the retracted image Rec S of every S ⊆ ℂ. -/
      11607  theorem record_retraction_injective (S : Config) : RetractionInjective (Rec S) :=
      11608    value_implies_retraction_injective (the_remembered_is_lossless S)
      11609  
      11610  /-- THE 1-BIT BRIDGE IN ORBIT-COLLAPSE SPELLING:
      11611      On a reflection-closed ZetaZeros, retraction injectivity collapses each fiber to its
      11612      critical-line point, and Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis follows. By
      11613      `closed_retraction_injective_iff_value` this is the same 1-bit bridge as
      11614      `rh_from_the_cargo_loop`: on reflection-closed S, RetractionInjective S is
      11615      equivalent to LeastErasure S. By § X-b (`analytic_face_is_least_erasure`,
      11616      `analytic_face_is_transport_gap`, `analytic_face_vocabulary_law`) every analytic
      11617      face equivalent to RH is identical to `LeastErasure ZetaZeros` and cannot bypass
      11618      it. The two hypotheses are the bridge in analytic spelling. -/
      11619  theorem rh_from_closed_and_retraction_injective
      11620      (h_closed : Closed ZetaZeros)
      11621      (h_inj : RetractionInjective ZetaZeros) :
      11622      LeastErasure ZetaZeros ∧ RiemannHypothesis := by
      11623    have hv : Value ZetaZeros := closed_retraction_injective_forces_value h_closed h_inj
      11624    exact ⟨(twins_zeta ZetaZeros).mpr hv, h_read_proved.mpr hv⟩

      12171  /-! ### X-k . The Cone: One Apex, Every Reading, No Category Gap -/
      12172  
      12173  /-- The readings of the apex: the four registers' readings of the one bit. -/
      12174  inductive ApexReading where
      12175    | leastErasure
      12176    | retraction
      12177    | socket
      12178    | coincidence
      12179    deriving DecidableEq, Repr
      12180  
      12181  /-- The diagram: each reading as a proposition over ℂ. -/
      12182  def apexDiagram : ApexReading → Prop
      12183    | .leastErasure => LeastErasure ZetaZeros
      12184    | .retraction   => RetractionInjective ZetaZeros
      12185    | .socket       => ∃ Z : ActualZeros, Z.zeros = ZetaZeros
      12186    | .coincidence  => ∀ s, ZetaZeros s → Rec ZetaZeros s
      12187  
      12188  /-- THE CONE: Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis is the apex; every leg is a proved
      12189      equivalence. The category gaps between the readings are eliminated: a gap is
      12190      the absence of an identity leg, and every leg is exhibited here. -/
      12191  theorem apex_cone : ∀ r, apexDiagram r ↔ RiemannHypothesis := by
      12192    intro r
      12193    cases r
      12194    · exact h_id_proved.symm
      12195    · exact retraction_injective_iff_rh
      12196    · exact socket_at_zeta_zeros.1
      12197    · exact ra_coincidence_iff_rh

      12200  #guard_msgs in
      12201  #print axioms BoundChainMathlib.apex_cone
      12202  
      12203  /-- ONE GAP: any two readings are the same proposition. -/
      12204  theorem apex_one_gap (r s : ApexReading) : apexDiagram r ↔ apexDiagram s :=
      12205    (apex_cone r).trans (apex_cone s).symm
      12206  
      12207  /-- info: 'BoundChainMathlib.apex_one_gap' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -/
      12208  #guard_msgs in
      12209  #print axioms BoundChainMathlib.apex_one_gap
      12210  
      12211  /-- THE HALT: every proposition proved equivalent to the apex lands on the same
      12212      apex as the four readings. -/
      12213  theorem apex_regress_halts (P : Prop) (hP : P ↔ RiemannHypothesis) (r : ApexReading) :
      12214      P ↔ apexDiagram r :=
      12215    hP.trans (apex_cone r).symm
      12216  
      12217  /-- info: 'BoundChainMathlib.apex_regress_halts' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -/
      12218  #guard_msgs in

      12231  /-! ### X-l . Pause and Look Back: The Unconditional Retrospective Seal -/
      12232  
      12233  /-- No principle shared by all conjugate-reflection-closed subsets of ℂ forces
      12234      critical-line inclusion. -/
      12235  theorem no_closed_principle_decides (D : Config → Prop) (hD : ∀ S, Closed S → D S) :
      12236      ¬ ∀ S : Config, Closed S → D S → Value S :=
      12237    fun hall => pair_world_lacks_value offPoint off_point_is_off
      12238      (hall _ (pair_world_closed offPoint) (hD _ (pair_world_closed offPoint)))
      12239

      12241  #guard_msgs in
      12242  #print axioms BoundChainMathlib.no_closed_principle_decides
      12243  
      12244  /-- THE PAUSE AT THE TERMINAL CARGO. Every nontrivial zero s lands in the
      12245      retracted record Rec ZetaZeros at reg s, where retraction is idempotent
      12246      and reflection partners collide. -/
      12247  def Pause : Prop :=
      12248    ∀ s, ZetaZeros s →
      12249      Rec ZetaZeros (reg s) ∧ reg (reg s) = reg s ∧ reg (fold s) = reg s
      12250  
      12251  /-- The Pause is inhabited unconditionally by a closed term. -/
      12252  theorem pause_is_unconditional : Pause :=
      12253    fun s hs => ⟨⟨s, hs, rfl⟩, reg_idem s, reg_fold s⟩
      12254  
      12255  /-- info: 'BoundChainMathlib.pause_is_unconditional' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -/
      12256  #guard_msgs in
      12257  #print axioms BoundChainMathlib.pause_is_unconditional
      12258

      12280  /-- LOOK BACK. At the inhabited Pause locus Rec ZetaZeros (reg s), reading
      12281      retraction invariance back onto the preimage s gives reg s = s. -/
      12282  def LookBack : Prop :=
      12283    ∀ s, ZetaZeros s → Rec ZetaZeros (reg s) → reg s = s

      12374  /-- The Monism witness lifted to complex configurations S ⊆ ℂ. -/
      12375  def RootReadTwice (S : Config) : Prop :=
      12376    RememberedOffered.MonismWitness (fun _ => Value S)
      12377  
      12378  /-- On every complex configuration, the Monism witness is equivalent to Value. -/
      12379  theorem root_read_twice_iff_value (S : Config) :
      12380      RootReadTwice S ↔ Value S :=
      12381    ⟨fun w => w.seed,
      12382     fun hv => ⟨RememberedOffered.one_involution_constructed, fun _ _ => Iff.rfl, hv⟩⟩
      12383

      12390    (root_read_twice_iff_value (Rec ZetaZeros)).mpr canonical_rh_unconditional
      12391

      12393  #guard_msgs in

      12396  /-- On ℂ, the line-bound world and the off-line pair world share one projected
      12397      record, and the Monism witness separates them: the true world carries monism
      12398      and the false world carries no monism. -/
      12399  theorem monism_separates_shared_record :
      12400      SameRecord (registered offPoint) (pairWorld offPoint) ∧

      12402      ¬ RootReadTwice (pairWorld offPoint) :=

      12404     (root_read_twice_iff_value _).mpr (registered_has_value offPoint),

      12406

      12411  /-- THE CANONICAL NORMAL-FORM BRIDGE. CanonicalRH and the Monism witness hold
      12412      unconditionally at the projected record Rec ZetaZeros, and carrying
      12413      CanonicalRH to ZetaZeros (or equating CanonicalRH with the Monism witness
      12414      at ZetaZeros) is logically identical to Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis. -/
      12415  theorem canonical_normal_form_bridge :

**Listing 22. The Euler product boundary and the analytic target reduction (X-l)** (master lines 12431 to 12504)

      12431  /-- The Euler product boundary on ZetaZeros: Mathlib's Euler product and
      12432      Dirichlet series establish non-vanishing for 1 < Re s, so every nontrivial
      12433      zero has Re s ≤ 1, and the reflection s ↦ 1 − s (`zeta_zeros_symm`) carries
      12434      the bound to 0 ≤ Re s. Mathlib's non-vanishing on Re s = 1 makes both
      12435      bounds strict (`zeta_zeros_strictly_in_strip`). -/
      12436  theorem euler_product_boundary (s : Point) (hs : ZetaZeros s) :
      12437      (0 ≤ s.re ∧ s.re ≤ 1) ∧ ¬ (1 < s.re) := by
      12438    have h := zeta_zeros_in_strip hs
      12439    refine ⟨h, ?_⟩
      12440    intro hgt
      12441    linarith
      12442  
      12443  /-- info: 'BoundChainMathlib.euler_product_boundary' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -/
      12444  #guard_msgs in
      12445  #print axioms BoundChainMathlib.euler_product_boundary
      12446  
      12447  /-- Non-vanishing in the right half of the critical strip, 1/2 < Re s. With
      12448      Mathlib's non-vanishing on Re s ≥ 1, its whole content is the band
      12449      1/2 < Re s < 1 (`right_half_strip_zero_free_iff_band`). -/
      12450  def RightHalfStripZeroFree : Prop :=
      12451    ∀ s : Point, ZetaZeros s → 1 / 2 < s.re → False
      12452  
      12453  /-- ANALYTIC TARGET REDUCTION (TIER T, ZERO PREMISES). Binds CanonicalRH,
      12454      the complex Monism witness at the record, and the Euler product boundary
      12455      (Re s ≤ 1), and proves unconditionally via conjugate-reflection closure
      12456      (zeta_zeros_closed) that RetractionInjective ZetaZeros, LookBack,
      12457      RootReadTwice ZetaZeros, and Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis reduce to
      12458      non-vanishing in the right half-strip 1/2 < Re s ≤ 1. -/
      12459  theorem analytic_target_reduction :
      12460      CanonicalRH ∧
      12461      RootReadTwice (Rec ZetaZeros) ∧
      12462      (∀ s, ZetaZeros s → (0 ≤ s.re ∧ s.re ≤ 1) ∧ ¬ (1 < s.re)) ∧
      12463      (RightHalfStripZeroFree ↔ RetractionInjective ZetaZeros) ∧
      12464      (RightHalfStripZeroFree ↔ LookBack) ∧
      12465      (RightHalfStripZeroFree ↔ RootReadTwice ZetaZeros) ∧
      12466      ((CanonicalRH → RightHalfStripZeroFree) ↔ RiemannHypothesis) ∧
      12467      (RightHalfStripZeroFree ↔ RiemannHypothesis) := by
      12468    have h_rh : RightHalfStripZeroFree ↔ RiemannHypothesis := by
      12469      rw [h_read_proved]
      12470      constructor
      12471      · intro h s hs
      12472        have h1 : s.re ≤ 1 / 2 := by
      12473          by_contra hgt
      12474          push_neg at hgt
      12475          exact h s hs hgt
      12476        have h2 : (fold s).re ≤ 1 / 2 := by
      12477          by_contra hgt
      12478          push_neg at hgt
      12479          exact h (fold s) (zeta_zeros_closed s hs) hgt
      12480        have h3 : (fold s).re = 1 - s.re := by
      12481          unfold fold
      12482          simp only [sub_re, one_re, star_def, conj_re]
      12483        unfold onLine
      12484        linarith
      12485      · intro hv s hs hgt
      12486        have heq : s.re = 1 / 2 := hv s hs
      12487        linarith
      12488    have h_rrt : RightHalfStripZeroFree ↔ RootReadTwice ZetaZeros :=
      12489      h_rh.trans (h_read_proved.trans (root_read_twice_iff_value ZetaZeros).symm)
      12490    have h_can : (CanonicalRH → RightHalfStripZeroFree) ↔ RiemannHypothesis :=
      12491      ⟨fun h => h_rh.mp (h canonical_rh_unconditional),
      12492       fun hrh _ => h_rh.mpr hrh⟩
      12493    exact ⟨canonical_rh_unconditional,
      12494           canonical_record_carries_monism,
      12495           euler_product_boundary,
      12496           h_rh.trans retraction_injective_iff_rh.symm,
      12497           h_rh.trans look_back_is_the_closure.2.symm,
      12498           h_rrt,
      12499           h_can,
      12500           h_rh⟩
      12501  
      12502  /-- info: 'BoundChainMathlib.analytic_target_reduction' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -/
      12503  #guard_msgs in
      12504  #print axioms BoundChainMathlib.analytic_target_reduction

**Listing 25. The analytic route sealed (X-l)** (master lines 12616 to 12642)

      12616  /-- THE ANALYTIC ROUTE, LOCATED AND CLOSED ON THE BIT. (1) On Part III's discrete chart no
      12617      derivation valid at every reflection-closed configuration yields the value
      12618      (`RememberedOffered.the_unconditional_route_is_blocked`). (2) The analytic target is
      12619      exactly `RightHalfStripZeroFree`, proved equivalent to `RiemannHypothesis`
      12620      (`analytic_target_reduction`). (3) Round 2 halts for every uniform route
      12621      (`round2_halted_uniduction`). (4) Every route to `RiemannHypothesis`, from any premise,
      12622      delivers `RightHalfStripZeroFree` and `LookBack` (`every_route_passes_the_bit`). A route
      12623      that uses properties of the zeros beyond reflection closure lies outside the class of
      12624      (1); by (4), if it reaches the hypothesis it has supplied the bit. No premise. -/
      12625  theorem analytic_route_sealed :

**Listing 26. The complex three-axis lock, the Ground-On-Line locus and its loop (X-l)** (master lines 12644 to 12731)

      12644  /-- Complex Triaxiality (lifted from Part II `PrimeFreedom.three_axis_lock` to ℂ):
      12645      the freedom axis, the reflection-seat axis (`fold s = s`), and the
      12646      displacement-collapse axis (`s.re - 1/2 = -(s.re - 1/2)`). -/
      12647  def freedomAxis (_ : Point) : Prop := True
      12648  def ramAxis (s : Point) : Prop := fold s = s
      12649  def collapseAxis (s : Point) : Prop := s.re - 1 / 2 = -(s.re - 1 / 2)
      12650  
      12651  /-- THE COMPLEX THREE-AXIS LOCK (UNCONDITIONAL, ZERO PREMISES). All three axes
      12652      hold at a complex point s if and only if s lies on the critical line. -/
      12653  theorem complex_three_axis_lock (s : Point) :
      12654      (freedomAxis s ∧ ramAxis s ∧ collapseAxis s) ↔ onLine s := by
      12655    constructor
      12656    · intro ⟨_, hram, _⟩
      12657      exact (fold_fixed_iff_onLine s).mp hram
      12658    · intro h
      12659      refine ⟨trivial, (fold_fixed_iff_onLine s).mpr h, ?_⟩
      12660      unfold collapseAxis onLine at *
      12661      linarith
      12662  
      12663  /-- info: 'BoundChainMathlib.complex_three_axis_lock' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -/
      12664  #guard_msgs in
      12665  #print axioms BoundChainMathlib.complex_three_axis_lock
      12666  
      12667  /-- Ground-On-Line (`GOL`): the canonical retracted zero locus `Rec ZetaZeros`. -/
      12668  def GOL : Config := Rec ZetaZeros
      12669  
      12670  /-- GOL LOOKS BACK (UNCONDITIONAL, ZERO PREMISES). At the Ground-On-Line locus
      12671      `GOL`, looking back requires no hypothesis: every point of `GOL` is fixed
      12672      by retraction (`reg q = q`), fixed by the reflection fold (`fold q = q`),
      12673      and locked on all three axes. This is the look-back at the record, and it
      12674      holds at `Rec S` for every configuration `S` (`record_has_least_erasure`).
      12675      At the zeros themselves the look-back is `LookBack`, the self-recognition
      12676      of the zeros (`self_recognition_is_look_back`), one statement with
      12677      `RiemannHypothesis` (`the_self_recognition_closure`). -/
      12678  theorem gol_look_back_unconditional :
      12679      (∀ q, GOL q → reg q = q) ∧
      12680      (∀ q, GOL q → fold q = q) ∧
      12681      (∀ q, GOL q → freedomAxis q ∧ ramAxis q ∧ collapseAxis q) :=
      12682    ⟨cargo_at_zeros,
      12683     fun q hq => (fold_fixed_iff_onLine q).mpr (the_remembered_is_lossless ZetaZeros q hq),
      12684     fun q hq => (complex_three_axis_lock q).mpr (the_remembered_is_lossless ZetaZeros q hq)⟩
      12685  
      12686  /-- info: 'BoundChainMathlib.gol_look_back_unconditional' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -/
      12687  #guard_msgs in
      12688  #print axioms BoundChainMathlib.gol_look_back_unconditional
      12689  
      12690  /-- THE RA-TRIAXIALITY-GOL-RA LOOP (UNCONDITIONAL, ZERO PREMISES).
      12691      1. Root (`RA`): `TOE0.RA₀` and `BoundChain.FreedomRoot` hold unconditionally.
      12692      2. Triaxiality: the three axes lock onto `onLine` across ℂ.
      12693      3. Pause at `GOL`: every zero projects into `GOL` (`Pause`), where `Value GOL`,
      12694         `LeastErasure GOL`, and `SelfVerifying (LeastErasure GOL)` hold unconditionally.
      12695      4. `GOL` Looks Back and Finds `RA`: at `GOL`, retraction invariance and the
      12696         Monism witness hold unconditionally, closing the biconditional loop back to
      12697         the Root Axiom (`TOE0.RA₀ ↔ Value GOL` and `TOE0.RA₀ ↔ LeastErasure GOL`)
      12698         with zero premises.
      12699      5. Normal-Form Coincidence: Mathlib's `RiemannHypothesis` is equivalent to
      12700         the coincidence of `ZetaZeros` with `GOL` (`∀ q, GOL q ↔ ZetaZeros q`). -/
      12701  theorem ra_triaxial_gol_loop_unconditional :
      12702      TOE0.RA₀ ∧
      12703      BoundChain.FreedomRoot ∧
      12704      (∀ s : Point, (freedomAxis s ∧ ramAxis s ∧ collapseAxis s) ↔ onLine s) ∧
      12705      Pause ∧
      12706      Value GOL ∧
      12707      LeastErasure GOL ∧
      12708      TOE0.SelfVerifying (LeastErasure GOL) ∧
      12709      RememberedOffered.MonismWitness (fun _ => Value GOL) ∧
      12710      (TOE0.RA₀ ↔ Value GOL) ∧
      12711      (TOE0.RA₀ ↔ LeastErasure GOL) ∧
      12712      ((∀ q, GOL q ↔ ZetaZeros q) ↔ RiemannHypothesis) :=
      12713    ⟨TOE0.root_on_the_constructed_domain,
      12714     BoundChain.freedom_root_inhabited,
      12715     complex_three_axis_lock,
      12716     pause_is_unconditional,
      12717     the_remembered_is_lossless ZetaZeros,
      12718     cargo_at_zeros,
      12719     ra_recursion_at_record.2.1,
      12720     ⟨RememberedOffered.one_involution_constructed,
      12721      fun _ _ => Iff.rfl,
      12722      the_remembered_is_lossless ZetaZeros⟩,
      12723     ⟨fun _ => the_remembered_is_lossless ZetaZeros,
      12724      fun _ => TOE0.root_on_the_constructed_domain⟩,
      12725     ⟨fun _ => cargo_at_zeros,
      12726      fun _ => TOE0.root_on_the_constructed_domain⟩,
      12727     rh_iff_fixed_point_of_rec.symm⟩
      12728  
      12729  /-- info: 'BoundChainMathlib.ra_triaxial_gol_loop_unconditional' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -/
      12730  #guard_msgs in
      12731  #print axioms BoundChainMathlib.ra_triaxial_gol_loop_unconditional

**Listing 27. The strict strip, the completed zeros, and the zero-free band (X-l)** (master lines 12733 to 12840)

      12733  /-! **THE SELF-RECOGNITION CLOSURE.** Mathlib's non-vanishing of ζ on `1 ≤ Re s`
      12734  (`riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_one_le_re`) closes both edges of the critical strip. The bit is the
      12735  self-recognition of the zeros, every zero fixed by its own retraction, and seven readings of it
      12736  are proved one statement with `RiemannHypothesis`. `the_self_recognition_closure` binds the
      12737  whole formal arc in one theorem with nothing before the colon. -/
      12738  
      12739  /-- Every nontrivial zero lies strictly inside the critical strip, `0 < Re s < 1`. Mathlib's
      12740      non-vanishing of ζ on `1 ≤ Re s` gives the right edge, and the reflection `s ↦ 1 − s`
      12741      (`zeta_zeros_symm`) carries it to the left edge. -/
      12742  theorem zeta_zeros_strictly_in_strip : ∀ s : Point, ZetaZeros s → 0 < s.re ∧ s.re < 1 := by
      12743    have hlt : ∀ {w : Point}, ZetaZeros w → w.re < 1 := by
      12744      intro w hw
      12745      by_contra h
      12746      push_neg at h
      12747      exact (riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_one_le_re h) hw.1
      12748    intro s hs
      12749    have h1 : s.re < 1 := hlt hs
      12750    have h0 : (foldPt s).re < 1 := hlt (zeta_zeros_symm hs)
      12751    unfold foldPt at h0
      12752    simp only [sub_re, one_re] at h0
      12753    exact ⟨by linarith, h1⟩
      12754  
      12755  /-- info: 'BoundChainMathlib.zeta_zeros_strictly_in_strip' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -/
      12756  #guard_msgs in
      12757  #print axioms BoundChainMathlib.zeta_zeros_strictly_in_strip
      12758  
      12759  /-- Every zero of the completed zeta function away from its two junk points `0` and `1` lies
      12760      strictly inside the critical strip: non-vanishing on `1 ≤ Re s` at `s`, and the functional
      12761      equation `completedRiemannZeta_one_sub` at `1 − s`. -/
      12762  theorem completed_zeta_zeros_strictly_in_strip :
      12763      ∀ s : Point, CompletedZetaZeros s → 0 < s.re ∧ s.re < 1 := by
      12764    have key : ∀ {w : Point}, w ≠ 0 → completedRiemannZeta w = 0 → w.re < 1 := by
      12765      intro w hw0 hw
      12766      by_contra h
      12767      push_neg at h
      12768      apply riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_one_le_re h
      12769      rw [riemannZeta_def_of_ne_zero hw0, hw, zero_div]
      12770    intro s hc
      12771    obtain ⟨hz, hs0, hs1⟩ := hc
      12772    have h1 : s.re < 1 := key hs0 hz
      12773    have hne : (1 - s) ≠ 0 := fun h => hs1 (sub_eq_zero.mp h).symm
      12774    have h0 : (1 - s).re < 1 := key hne (by rw [completedRiemannZeta_one_sub]; exact hz)
      12775    simp only [sub_re, one_re] at h0
      12776    exact ⟨by linarith, h1⟩
      12777  
      12778  /-- info: 'BoundChainMathlib.completed_zeta_zeros_strictly_in_strip' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -/
      12779  #guard_msgs in
      12780  #print axioms BoundChainMathlib.completed_zeta_zeros_strictly_in_strip
      12781  
      12782  /-- The nontrivial zeros of ζ and the zeros of the completed zeta function coincide on all
      12783      of ℂ: both sets lie strictly inside the strip, where `zeta_zeros_iff_completed_in_strip` equates
      12784      them. -/
      12785  theorem zeta_zeros_iff_completed : ∀ s : Point, ZetaZeros s ↔ CompletedZetaZeros s := by
      12786    intro s
      12787    constructor
      12788    · intro hs
      12789      obtain ⟨h0, h1⟩ := zeta_zeros_strictly_in_strip s hs
      12790      exact (zeta_zeros_iff_completed_in_strip h0 h1).mp hs
      12791    · intro hc
      12792      obtain ⟨h0, h1⟩ := completed_zeta_zeros_strictly_in_strip s hc
      12793      exact (zeta_zeros_iff_completed_in_strip h0 h1).mpr hc
      12794  
      12795  /-- info: 'BoundChainMathlib.zeta_zeros_iff_completed' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -/
      12796  #guard_msgs in
      12797  #print axioms BoundChainMathlib.zeta_zeros_iff_completed
      12798  
      12799  /-- With the edge `Re s = 1` closed, `RightHalfStripZeroFree` is exactly the statement that the
      12800      band `1/2 < Re s < 1` carries no zero. -/
      12801  theorem right_half_strip_zero_free_iff_band :
      12802      RightHalfStripZeroFree ↔ ∀ s : Point, ZetaZeros s → ¬ (1 / 2 < s.re ∧ s.re < 1) := by
      12803    constructor
      12804    · intro h s hs hb
      12805      exact h s hs hb.1
      12806    · intro h s hs h1
      12807      exact h s hs ⟨h1, (zeta_zeros_strictly_in_strip s hs).2⟩
      12808  
      12809  /-- info: 'BoundChainMathlib.right_half_strip_zero_free_iff_band' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -/
      12810  #guard_msgs in
      12811  #print axioms BoundChainMathlib.right_half_strip_zero_free_iff_band
      12812  
      12813  /-- The Riemann Hypothesis is exactly the statement that the band `1/2 < Re s < 1`
      12814      carries no zero (`analytic_target_reduction`, `right_half_strip_zero_free_iff_band`). -/
      12815  theorem rh_iff_band_zero_free :
      12816      RiemannHypothesis ↔ ∀ s : Point, ZetaZeros s → ¬ (1 / 2 < s.re ∧ s.re < 1) :=
      12817    (analytic_target_reduction.2.2.2.2.2.2.2).symm.trans right_half_strip_zero_free_iff_band
      12818  
      12819  /-- info: 'BoundChainMathlib.rh_iff_band_zero_free' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -/
      12820  #guard_msgs in
      12821  #print axioms BoundChainMathlib.rh_iff_band_zero_free
      12822  
      12823  /-- Every zero off the critical line has a twin in the band `1/2 < Re s < 1`: itself when
      12824      it lies right of the line, its fold image `1 − s̄` when it lies left of it. -/
      12825  theorem off_line_zero_has_band_twin :
      12826      ∀ s : Point, ZetaZeros s → ¬ onLine s →
      12827        ∃ t : Point, ZetaZeros t ∧ (1 / 2 < t.re ∧ t.re < 1) ∧ (t = s ∨ t = fold s) := by
      12828    intro s hs hoff
      12829    obtain ⟨h0, h1⟩ := zeta_zeros_strictly_in_strip s hs
      12830    have hne : s.re ≠ 1 / 2 := hoff
      12831    have h3 : (fold s).re = 1 - s.re := by
      12832      unfold fold
      12833      simp only [sub_re, one_re, star_def, conj_re]
      12834    rcases hne.lt_or_lt with hlt | hgt
      12835    · exact ⟨fold s, zeta_zeros_closed s hs, ⟨by linarith, by linarith⟩, Or.inr rfl⟩
      12836    · exact ⟨s, hs, ⟨hgt, h1⟩, Or.inl rfl⟩
      12837  
      12838  /-- info: 'BoundChainMathlib.off_line_zero_has_band_twin' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -/
      12839  #guard_msgs in
      12840  #print axioms BoundChainMathlib.off_line_zero_has_band_twin

**Listing 28. The self-recognition of the zeros and the self-recognition closure (X-l)** (master lines 12842 to 12909)

      12842  /-- THE BIT IS SELF-RECOGNITION. `LookBack` is the self-recognition of the zeros: every zero is
      12843      fixed by its own retraction, `reg s = s`. The record clause of `LookBack` holds at every
      12844      zero through `p := s`, so the bit is self-recognition and nothing besides. -/
      12845  theorem self_recognition_is_look_back :
      12846      LookBack ↔ ∀ s : Point, ZetaZeros s → reg s = s :=
      12847    ⟨fun h s hs => h s hs ⟨s, hs, rfl⟩, fun h s hs _ => h s hs⟩
      12848  
      12849  /-- info: 'BoundChainMathlib.self_recognition_is_look_back' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -/
      12850  #guard_msgs in
      12851  #print axioms BoundChainMathlib.self_recognition_is_look_back
      12852  
      12853  /-- THE SELF-RECOGNITION CLOSURE (ZERO PREMISES). The whole formal arc in one theorem, nothing
      12854      before the colon.
      12855      I · THE FLOOR FROM FREEDOM. The root `TOE0.RA₀` and `BoundChain.FreedomRoot`
      12856      (`TOE0.root_on_the_constructed_domain`, `BoundChain.freedom_root_inhabited`, each on no
      12857      axiom); `Pause`; `CanonicalRH`; the look-back at the Ground-On-Line locus, every point of
      12858      `GOL` fixed by its own retraction; the complex three-axis lock.
      12859      II · WHAT ζ CARRIES. Every nontrivial zero lies strictly inside the strip `0 < Re s < 1`; the zero
      12860      set is closed under the fold `s ↦ 1 − s̄`; it coincides with the zero set of the completed
      12861      zeta function on all of ℂ; every zero off the line has a twin in the band
      12862      `1/2 < Re s < 1`.
      12863      III · THE BIT IS SELF-RECOGNITION. Seven readings of the bit are one statement with
      12864      `RiemannHypothesis`: `LookBack`; the self-recognition of the zeros,
      12865      `∀ s, ZetaZeros s → reg s = s`; the coincidence of `GOL` with `ZetaZeros`; retraction
      12866      injectivity of the zeros; the Monism witness at the zeros; `RightHalfStripZeroFree`; and the
      12867      zero-free band.
      12868      IV · NOTHING ESCAPES THE BIT. Every route to `RiemannHypothesis`, from any premise, delivers the bit
      12869      (`every_route_passes_the_bit`), and no principle shared by every reflection-closed
      12870      configuration decides the value (`no_closed_principle_decides`).
      12871      The formal side carries no premise: it proves that `RiemannHypothesis` and the
      12872      self-recognition of the zeros are one statement, and that nothing else remains. The physical
      12873      carrier supplies that self-recognition under its stated premises
      12874      (`physico_formal_supplies_look_back_and_rh`). -/
      12875  theorem the_self_recognition_closure :
      12876      (TOE0.RA₀ ∧ BoundChain.FreedomRoot ∧ Pause ∧ CanonicalRH ∧
      12877        (∀ q, GOL q → reg q = q) ∧
      12878        (∀ s : Point, (freedomAxis s ∧ ramAxis s ∧ collapseAxis s) ↔ onLine s)) ∧
      12879      ((∀ s : Point, ZetaZeros s → 0 < s.re ∧ s.re < 1) ∧
      12880        Closed ZetaZeros ∧
      12881        (∀ s : Point, ZetaZeros s ↔ CompletedZetaZeros s) ∧
      12882        (∀ s : Point, ZetaZeros s → ¬ onLine s →
      12883          ∃ t : Point, ZetaZeros t ∧ (1 / 2 < t.re ∧ t.re < 1) ∧ (t = s ∨ t = fold s))) ∧
      12884      ((LookBack ↔ ∀ s : Point, ZetaZeros s → reg s = s) ∧
      12885        ((∀ s : Point, ZetaZeros s → reg s = s) ↔ RiemannHypothesis) ∧
      12886        ((∀ q, GOL q ↔ ZetaZeros q) ↔ RiemannHypothesis) ∧
      12887        (RetractionInjective ZetaZeros ↔ RiemannHypothesis) ∧
      12888        (RootReadTwice ZetaZeros ↔ RiemannHypothesis) ∧
      12889        (RightHalfStripZeroFree ↔ RiemannHypothesis) ∧
      12890        (RiemannHypothesis ↔ ∀ s : Point, ZetaZeros s → ¬ (1 / 2 < s.re ∧ s.re < 1))) ∧
      12891      ((∀ Q : Prop, (Q → RiemannHypothesis) → Q →
      12892          RightHalfStripZeroFree ∧ LookBack ∧ RetractionInjective ZetaZeros ∧
      12893            RootReadTwice ZetaZeros) ∧
      12894        (∀ D : Config → Prop, (∀ S, Closed S → D S) →
      12895          ¬ ∀ S : Config, Closed S → D S → Value S)) :=
      12896    ⟨⟨TOE0.root_on_the_constructed_domain, BoundChain.freedom_root_inhabited,
      12897       pause_is_unconditional, canonical_rh_unconditional, cargo_at_zeros,

      12899     ⟨zeta_zeros_strictly_in_strip, zeta_zeros_closed, zeta_zeros_iff_completed,

      12904       analytic_target_reduction.2.2.2.2.2.2.2, rh_iff_band_zero_free⟩,
      12905     ⟨every_route_passes_the_bit, no_closed_principle_decides⟩⟩
      12906

# The Discrete Arch

Part IX is `RH_Bound_Chain_v1.0.1.lean`, in the namespace `BoundChain`, which resolves every identifier this section cites, carried into the master with the recursion of Theorem 8.2 and its self-grounding term inserted in v3.0.7 ahead of its pin block, their two pins added inside it, and eleven further pins added inside it in v3.0.10, the earlier editions of the master standing in the repository; it was written for core Lean with no import. It runs the same calculus on the discrete chart, where every theorem below has an empty cone: no axiom at all, not even propositional extensionality, quotients or choice.

**Theorem 8.1** (`bound_chain`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> $\varnothing$\])**.** The formal root $\mathrm{FreedomRoot} := \exists f : \mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N},\ \forall a,\ f\,a = a$ is inhabited; for every $S$, $\mathrm{Value}(\mathrm{Rec}S) \wedge \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}S) \wedge \exists Z,\ Z.\mathrm{zeros} = \mathrm{Rec}S$; reflection symmetry alone forces nothing; no principle shared by all closed configurations forces the value; no inhabited proposition forces the value; no record-invariant predicate decides the value; and Stage 1 of Part IX is inhabited.

**Theorem 8.2** (`transport_needs_value`, `identification_is_the_proof`, `ra_recursion_at_record`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> $\varnothing$\])**.** On the discrete chart: for every $M$, $(\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}M) \to \mathrm{LeastErasure}M) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Value}(M)$; for every $S$, $(\exists Z,\ Z.\mathrm{zeros} = \mathrm{Rec}S) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Value}(\mathrm{Rec}S)$; and for every $S$, $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}S)$, its self-verification, and its absorption of every premise, from the term `ra_cargo_self_grounding` $S$.

The discrete arch is the formal closure with every axiom removed. What Part X adds is the binding of the same shape to Mathlib’s $\zeta$, at the cost of the three standard axioms Mathlib itself rests on.

# The Physical Closure

Parts VII and VIII carry the hypothesis from premises about the physical world, each premise printed in a theorem signature, the measurement entering the concrete capstone as the certificate field of the bound structure its signature takes. The chart is the discrete offset chart, the classical hypothesis enters as an abstract proposition $\mathrm{ClassicalRH}$, and the reading $\mathrm{ClassicalRH} \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Value}(Z_\zeta)$ is the one identification of the classical hypothesis that the reader grants, entered as the printed premise $h_{\mathrm{read}}$ of a theorem schema in $\mathrm{ClassicalRH}$ and $Z_\zeta$; the discrete configuration $Z_\zeta$ is supplied with the reading and granted with it, the file fixing no map from the zeros of $\zeta$ to the chart. Over $\mathbb{C}$, Section 3 proves the corresponding reading for Mathlib’s sentence as `h_read_proved`, a theorem of the complex chart that the discrete schema does not consume; the chart homomorphism of Section 7.3 carries the discrete line into $\operatorname{Re} s = 1/2$, a discrete point lying on the line exactly when its image does.

## The least-erasure kernel

A system of the kernel (`LeastErasureDoF.System`) has $\mathrm{distinct}$ macro-records, $\mathrm{free}$ binary labels and $\mathrm{total} = \mathrm{distinct}\cdot 2^{\mathrm{free}}$ microstates. A discard halves the count of macro-records and frees one label with the total preserved; an erasure keeps that count, loses one free label, and halves the total. With $\ln 2$ scaled by $10^6$ as $\texttt{ln2\_scaled} = 693147$:

**Theorem 9.1** (`discard_is_free`, `sysEntropy_decrease`, `null_forces_zero`, `density_bound_from_residual_bound`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t / t / c / c · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> $\varnothing$\])**.** A discard satisfies $\mathrm{after.distinct}\cdot 2 = \mathrm{before.distinct}$ and $\mathrm{after.free} = \mathrm{before.free}+1$. An erasure lowers the system entropy $\mathrm{free}\cdot\ln 2$ by exactly $\ln 2$. With $\mathrm{residual}(\rho, r, q) := \rho r q$: if $r>0$, $q>0$ and $\mathrm{residual}(\rho,r,q) = 0$ then $\rho = 0$; and if $\mathrm{residual}(\rho,r,q) \le \varepsilon$, $r \ge r_0$, $q \ge q_0$ then $\rho\, r_0\, q_0 \le \varepsilon$.

The exact-null and finite-sensitivity regimes are kept apart by type. A null result at finite sensitivity bounds a population, $\rho\, r_0\, q_0 \le \varepsilon$, and in the kernel’s natural units, the floors positive, it reads $\rho \le \lfloor \varepsilon/(r_0\, q_0)\rfloor$ (`density_le_div`), which is zero when $\varepsilon < r_0\, q_0$. Landauer’s law enters as the definition $\texttt{landauerHeatPerEvent}\,T := T\cdot\texttt{ln2\_scaled}$; what the theorems derive is the count of erased labels and that at positive temperature the heat is positive exactly when the count is.

## The identification reduced to the reading, and the act as the premise packaged

**Theorem 9.2** (`le_iff_value`, `classical_rh_iff_le_of_reading`, `the_act_is_the_premise_packaged`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t / c / t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> $\varnothing$\])**.** For every discrete configuration, $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(S) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Value}(S)$. Whoever grants $\mathrm{ClassicalRH} \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Value}(Z_\zeta)$ has granted $\mathrm{ClassicalRH} \leftrightarrow \mathrm{LeastErasure}(Z_\zeta)$. An act exists at $S$ exactly when $\mathrm{Closed}(S) \wedge \mathrm{LeastErasure}(S)$.

## The bridge of six arrows, composed

**Theorem 9.3** (`off_line_zero_forces_observable_signal`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> c · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> $\varnothing$\])**.** Let $\mathrm{Realizes}, \mathrm{Erases}$ be predicates on a carrier type and $\mathrm{density}, \mathrm{rate}, \mathrm{heat}$ natural-valued functions on it. Grant the six arrows: a failure of least erasure at $Z_\zeta$ realizes a carrier; a realized carrier erases; an erasing carrier has population at least $n_0$; rate at least $r_0$; heat per event at least $q_0$; and the residual observable $R$ covers its contribution, $R \ge \mathrm{density}\cdot\mathrm{rate}\cdot\mathrm{heat}$. Then $\neg\mathrm{LeastErasure}(Z_\zeta) \to R \ge n_0 r_0 q_0$.

The threshold $n_0 r_0 q_0$ depends neither on the carrier nor on which point stands off the line: it is uniform over the class the arrows name. Positive rate and positive heat alone do not reach it; the population floor and the coupling are needed and are named.

## The capstones

**Theorem 9.4** (`classical_rh_from_identification_gap_and_bound`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> c · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> $\varnothing$\])**.** From $h_{\mathrm{id}} : \mathrm{ClassicalRH} \leftrightarrow \mathrm{LeastErasure}(Z_\zeta)$, $h_{\mathrm{bridge}} : \neg\mathrm{LeastErasure}(Z_\zeta) \to R \ge \delta$, $h_{\mathrm{bound}} : R \le \varepsilon$, $h_{\mathrm{gap}} : \varepsilon < \delta$ and $0 < \delta$: $\mathrm{ClassicalRH}$.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* Pointwise and constructive. At each read point the registration either fixes the point, or it does not and the bridge puts $R \ge \delta > \varepsilon \ge R$. ◻

</div>

**Theorem 9.5** (`classical_rh_from_the_arrows`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> c · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> $\varnothing$\])**.** From the reading $h_{\mathrm{read}} : \mathrm{ClassicalRH} \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Value}(Z_\zeta)$, the six arrows of Theorem 9.3, the bound $R \le \varepsilon$ and the gap $\varepsilon < n_0 r_0 q_0$: $\mathrm{ClassicalRH}$.

**Theorem 9.6** (`no_third_position`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> c · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> $\varnothing$\])**.** Under the identification, the bound and the gap, $\neg\bigl(\neg\mathrm{ClassicalRH} \wedge (\neg\mathrm{LeastErasure}(Z_\zeta) \to R \ge \delta)\bigr)$: the denial of the hypothesis and the bridge cannot both stand.

A reader who denies the hypothesis has named the bridge as the arrow that fails; a reader who grants the bridge has granted the hypothesis.

**Listing 31. The capstone in both forms (§VII-e)** (master lines 9415 to 9462)

       9425  theorem classical_rh_from_identification_gap_and_bound
       9426      {ClassicalRH : Prop} {Zζ : Config} {R δ ε : Nat}
       9427      (h_id     : ClassicalRH ↔ LeastErasure Zζ)
       9428      (h_bridge : ¬ LeastErasure Zζ → R ≥ δ)

       9459      (classical_rh_iff_le_of_reading h_read)

       9462      h_bound h_gap (Nat.lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.zero_le ε) h_gap)

## The inputs are keyed, by witness

**Theorem 9.7** (`the_reading_is_keyed`, `the_bridge_is_keyed`, `the_bound_alone_decides_nothing`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> $\varnothing$\])**.** There exist a proposition $P$ and a closed configuration $S$ with $\neg(P \leftrightarrow \mathrm{LeastErasure}(S))$. There exist a closed $S$ lacking least erasure and $R, \delta$ with $\neg(\neg\mathrm{LeastErasure}(S) \to R \ge \delta)$. For every $\varepsilon$ there is a closed $S$ lacking least erasure with $0 \le \varepsilon$.

The witnesses are the true proposition and the pair world of the discrete off point $(1,0)$, with $R = 0$, $\delta = 1$. No theorem of the interface identifies an arbitrary proposition with least erasure or lifts the residual from a failure of least erasure, and the pair world, reflection-closed and lacking least erasure, stands beside every sensitivity $\varepsilon$ (`the_bound_alone_decides_nothing`), no residual entering without the bridge. The reading and the bridge are therefore inputs, the reading granted by name and the bridge derived from the physics at the grade of its arrows or granted by name, neither read off the chart.

       9515      pair world with R = 0 and δ = 1 the bridge fails. The bridge is therefore an input: derived from the physics
       9516      at the grade of its arrows, or granted by name, never read off the chart. -/
       9517  theorem the_bridge_is_keyed :
       9518      ∃ (S : Config) (R δ : Nat), Closed S ∧ ¬ LeastErasure S ∧ ¬ (¬ LeastErasure S → R ≥ δ) :=
       9519    ⟨pairWorld offPoint, 0, 1, pair_world_lacks_le.1, pair_world_lacks_le.2,
       9520     fun h => Nat.not_succ_le_zero 0 (h pair_world_lacks_le.2)⟩
       9521  
       9522  /-- THE BOUND DOES NOT CLOSE ALONE. A bound R ≤ ε with no bridge leaves least erasure undecided: the pair world
       9523      is closed, lacks least erasure, and is consistent with every bound. -/
       9524  theorem the_bound_alone_decides_nothing (ε : Nat) :
       9525      ∃ S : Config, Closed S ∧ ¬ LeastErasure S ∧ (0 : Nat) ≤ ε :=
       9526    ⟨pairWorld offPoint, pair_world_lacks_le.1, pair_world_lacks_le.2, Nat.zero_le ε⟩

## The physical carrier and the bijection from zeros

**Definition 9.8** (`PhysicalCarrier`, `C`, `Neutral`, `annihilate`)**.** A carrier state is either $\mathrm{selfConjugate}(t)$, the neutral state at height $t$, or $\mathrm{conjugatePair}(m,t,\mathrm{sign})$, a member of the pair of magnitude $m+1$ at height $t$ carrying the one label that tells it from its partner. Charge conjugation $C$ fixes the neutral sector and flips the sign; $\mathrm{Neutral}$ is the self-conjugate sector; annihilation sends a pair member to the neutral state at its height and fixes a neutral state, keeping the sign in no register.

**Theorem 9.9** (`C_involutive`, `neutral_iff_C_fixed`, `annihilate_fixes_iff_neutral`, `pair_is_two_states_one_image`, `the_closure_on_the_physical_carrier`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> $\varnothing$\])**.** $C$ is an involution whose fixed set is the neutral sector; annihilation fixes a state exactly when it is neutral; a conjugate pair is two distinct states with one annihilation image. The carrier instantiates the abstract fold and registration of Part II’s carrier interface (`carrierFold`, `carrierReg`).

**Theorem 9.10** (`map_zero_to_carrier` and its equivariance  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> $\varnothing$\])**.** The map $(0,t) \mapsto \mathrm{selfConjugate}(t)$, $(n+1,t) \mapsto \mathrm{conjugatePair}(n,t,\mathrm{true})$, $(-(n+1),t) \mapsto \mathrm{conjugatePair}(n,t,\mathrm{false})$ is a bijection from the discrete chart onto the carrier (`map_left_inverse`, `map_right_inverse`) under which $\mathrm{fold}$ becomes $C$ (`map_fold`), $\mathrm{onLine}$ becomes $\mathrm{Neutral}$ (`map_neutral_iff_onLine`), and $\mathrm{reg}$ becomes $\mathrm{annihilate}$ (`map_reg`).

**Theorem 9.11** (`mathematical_violation_forces_physical_discard`, `on_line_discards_nothing`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> $\varnothing$\])**.** If $p$ is off the line, its carrier is charged, $C$ moves it, annihilation does not fix it, and annihilation sends it and its conjugate partner to one state. If $p$ is on the line, its carrier is neutral and annihilation fixes it.

On the concrete carrier two of the six arrows become theorem up to realization: that the carrier of an off-line zero is charged, and that its annihilation erases one label. That the carrier is realized is the premise $h_{\mathrm{realize}}$, an input by witness (`realization_is_the_premise`). A violation of the critical line is carried into the charged sector, where its branch label is irreversibly lost. The file names annihilation a physical discard in its theorem names and builds one annihilation as an erasure process of the kernel (`oneAnnihilation`); the file’s docstring identifies the label erased with the branch label.

**Listing 33. The physical carrier, charge conjugation, annihilation, the map (§VIII-a, §VIII-b)** (master lines 9691 to 9780)

       9691  /-! ## VIII-a · the carrier, by constructors; conjugation and annihilation, by cases -/
       9692  
       9693  /-- THE PHYSICAL CARRIER. A state of the sector in which a zero is realized is one of two kinds:
       9694      `selfConjugate t`, a state at height t that charge conjugation fixes, the neutral sector; or
       9695      `conjugatePair m t sign`, a member of the conjugate pair of magnitude m + 1 at height t, with `sign` the one
       9696      label that tells it from its partner, the charged sector. A type given by its constructors, inhabited at every
       9697      height; which of its states the vacuum instantiates is the premise h_realize of VIII-e, not a field here. -/
       9698  inductive PhysicalCarrier where
       9699    | selfConjugate (t : Int)
       9700    | conjugatePair (m : Nat) (t : Int) (sign : Bool)
       9701  
       9702  /-- Charge conjugation: it fixes the neutral sector and flips the sign in the charged sector. -/
       9703  def C : PhysicalCarrier → PhysicalCarrier
       9704    | .selfConjugate t => .selfConjugate t
       9705    | .conjugatePair m t s => .conjugatePair m t (!s)
       9706  
       9707  theorem C_involutive (c : PhysicalCarrier) : C (C c) = c := by
       9708    cases c with
       9709    | selfConjugate t => rfl
       9710    | conjugatePair m t s => cases s <;> rfl
       9711  
       9712  /-- The neutral sector: the self-conjugate states. -/
       9713  def Neutral : PhysicalCarrier → Prop
       9714    | .selfConjugate _ => True
       9715    | .conjugatePair _ _ _ => False
       9716  
       9717  /-- The neutral sector is exactly the fixed locus of charge conjugation. -/
       9718  theorem neutral_iff_C_fixed (c : PhysicalCarrier) : Neutral c ↔ C c = c := by
       9719    cases c with
       9720    | selfConjugate t => exact ⟨fun _ => rfl, fun _ => trivial⟩
       9721    | conjugatePair m t s => exact ⟨fun h => h.elim, fun h => by cases s <;> cases h⟩
       9722  
       9723  /-- Fixedness under charge conjugation is decided on the carrier, by cases. -/
       9724  theorem carrier_em (c : PhysicalCarrier) : C c = c ∨ C c ≠ c := by
       9725    cases c with
       9726    | selfConjugate t => exact Or.inl rfl
       9727    | conjugatePair m t s => exact Or.inr (fun h => by cases s <;> cases h)
       9728  
       9729  /-- Annihilation, the physical discard: a member of a pair goes to the neutral state at its height; a neutral state
       9730      stays. The sign is kept in no register of the carrier. -/
       9731  def annihilate : PhysicalCarrier → PhysicalCarrier
       9732    | .selfConjugate t => .selfConjugate t
       9733    | .conjugatePair _ t _ => .selfConjugate t
       9734  
       9735  theorem annihilate_lands (c : PhysicalCarrier) : C (annihilate c) = annihilate c := by
       9736    cases c <;> rfl
       9737  
       9738  theorem annihilate_fixes (c : PhysicalCarrier) (h : C c = c) : annihilate c = c := by
       9739    cases c with
       9740    | selfConjugate t => rfl
       9741    | conjugatePair m t s => cases s <;> cases h
       9742  
       9743  theorem annihilate_forgets (c : PhysicalCarrier) : annihilate (C c) = annihilate c := by
       9744    cases c <;> rfl
       9745  
       9746  /-- Annihilation fixes a state exactly when the state is neutral. -/
       9747  theorem annihilate_fixes_iff_neutral (c : PhysicalCarrier) : annihilate c = c ↔ Neutral c := by
       9748    cases c with
       9749    | selfConjugate t => exact ⟨fun _ => trivial, fun _ => rfl⟩
       9750    | conjugatePair m t s => exact ⟨fun h => (by cases h), fun h => h.elim⟩
       9751  
       9752  /-- A conjugate pair is two states with one image under annihilation: the sign is the bit that annihilation erases. -/
       9753  theorem pair_is_two_states_one_image (m : Nat) (t : Int) :
       9754      PhysicalCarrier.conjugatePair m t true ≠ PhysicalCarrier.conjugatePair m t false ∧
       9755      annihilate (.conjugatePair m t true) = annihilate (.conjugatePair m t false) :=
       9756    ⟨fun h => (by cases h), rfl⟩
       9757  
       9758  /-- THE PHYSICAL CARRIER IS AN INSTANCE OF THE SEED'S CARRIER ABSTRACTION (Part II): charge conjugation is a fold. -/
       9759  def carrierFold : PrimeFreedom.Carrier.Fold PhysicalCarrier := ⟨C, C_involutive⟩
       9760  
       9761  /-- Annihilation is a registration for that fold: it lands on the neutral sector, fixes it, and forgets the sign. -/
       9762  def carrierReg : PrimeFreedom.Carrier.Registration carrierFold :=
       9763    ⟨annihilate, annihilate_lands, annihilate_fixes, annihilate_forgets⟩
       9764  
       9765  /-- THE CLOSURE ON THE PHYSICAL CARRIER: the four laws Part II proves on any carrier, instantiated on this one by
       9766      theorem. Least erasure is the value; the value is lossless registration; the lossless member of a record is
       9767      unique; every charged state gives two worlds of one record that differ in the value. -/
       9768  theorem the_closure_on_the_physical_carrier :
       9769      type_of% (PrimeFreedom.Carrier.the_closure_on_any_carrier carrierReg carrier_em) :=
       9770    PrimeFreedom.Carrier.the_closure_on_any_carrier carrierReg carrier_em
       9771  
       9772  /-! ## VIII-b · the map from a zero to its carrier, total and bijective, equivariant -/
       9773  
       9774  /-- THE MAP FROM A ZERO TO ITS CARRIER. A point of the chart at offset d and height t goes: on the line, to the
       9775      self-conjugate state at t; at offset n + 1, to the positive member of the pair of magnitude n + 1 at t; at offset
       9776      −(n + 1), to the negative member. Total, by the integer's three constructors. -/
       9777  def map_zero_to_carrier : Point → PhysicalCarrier
       9778    | (Int.ofNat 0, t) => .selfConjugate t
       9779    | (Int.ofNat (n + 1), t) => .conjugatePair n t true
       9780    | (Int.negSucc n, t) => .conjugatePair n t false

**Listing 34. Mathematical violation forces physical discard (§VIII-c)** (master lines 9841 to 9862)

       9841  /-! ## VIII-c · the mathematical violation forces the physical discard -/
       9842  
       9843  /-- MATHEMATICAL VIOLATION FORCES PHYSICAL DISCARD. A zero off the line is carried to the charged sector; there
       9844      charge conjugation moves it, annihilation does not fix it, and annihilation sends it and its conjugate partner
       9845      to one state. One label, the sign, is lost and kept in no register of the carrier. Theorem; no premise. This
       9846      is h_carrier and h_erase of Part VII, discharged on the concrete carrier. -/
       9847  theorem mathematical_violation_forces_physical_discard (p : Point) (h : ¬ onLine p) :
       9848      ¬ Neutral (map_zero_to_carrier p) ∧
       9849      C (map_zero_to_carrier p) ≠ map_zero_to_carrier p ∧
       9850      annihilate (map_zero_to_carrier p) ≠ map_zero_to_carrier p ∧
       9851      annihilate (C (map_zero_to_carrier p)) = annihilate (map_zero_to_carrier p) :=
       9852    have hn : ¬ Neutral (map_zero_to_carrier p) := fun hN => h ((map_neutral_iff_onLine p).mp hN)
       9853    ⟨hn,
       9854     fun hC => hn ((neutral_iff_C_fixed _).mpr hC),
       9855     fun hA => hn ((annihilate_fixes_iff_neutral _).mp hA),
       9856     annihilate_forgets _⟩
       9857  
       9858  /-- ON THE LINE NOTHING IS DISCARDED: the carrier is neutral and annihilation fixes it. -/
       9859  theorem on_line_discards_nothing (p : Point) (h : onLine p) :
       9860      Neutral (map_zero_to_carrier p) ∧ annihilate (map_zero_to_carrier p) = map_zero_to_carrier p :=
       9861    have hN := (map_neutral_iff_onLine p).mpr h
       9862    ⟨hN, (annihilate_fixes_iff_neutral _).mpr hN⟩

## Energetic bookkeeping

**Theorem 9.12** (`oneAnnihilation`, `discard_forces_heat_generation`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t / c · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> $\varnothing$\])**.** The kernel’s erasure process has a one-label instance, which the file names for annihilation. For a finite configuration $F$ with $\mathrm{erased}(F)$ labels and any $T > 0$: $\mathrm{landauerHeat}(\mathrm{erased}\,F, T) = 0 \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Value}(F.\mathrm{pts})$, and $\neg\mathrm{Value}(F.\mathrm{pts}) \to \mathrm{landauerHeat}(\mathrm{erased}\,F, T) > 0$.

At any positive temperature the Landauer heat of registering a finite configuration is zero exactly at the value and positive whenever a point stands off the line.

## The certified bound, the detection gap, the concrete capstone

A measurement is a premise by its nature and is entered as the type it is. The structure `CertifiedObservationalBound` packages the residual $B.R$, the sensitivity $B.\varepsilon$, the certificate $B.R \le B.\varepsilon$, and the dataset name. The detection gap is $\delta := \texttt{detectionGap}(n_0,r_0,T_0) = n_0\, r_0\,(T_0\ln 2)$, the uniform floor one realized charged carrier puts under the residual; where a list of inputs names the detection gap, it names the premise $h_{\mathrm{gap}} : B.\varepsilon < \delta$; elsewhere in Section 9 and in Appendix E, $\delta$ names the gap of the theorems that take it as a variable, and the concrete capstone and `signal_floor` fix it at the detection gap. The capstone fixes no value for $n_0$, $r_0$, $T_0$, $T$, $R$ or $\varepsilon$, nor does the arrow form fix its heat floor $q_0$: they enter as variables, naturals in the file’s scaled units, the heat in those of `landauerHeatPerEvent`, and $\delta$ takes a value when the floors are supplied. The file’s one named temperature, `cmb_mK` $:= 2725$ of §VII-a, enters only statements of heat at that temperature, `the_master_seal` and `heat_at_cmb_positive` among them, and `landauer_is_entered_not_derived` evaluates the heat at temperature zero to show that it enters by definition. The certificate is the inequality $B.R \le B.\varepsilon$; the dataset field names its source, and the identification of $B.R$ with a measured residual is the reader’s to grant. Each physical premise has its own refuting observation: a point of $Z_\zeta$ whose carrier is not realized refutes $h_{\mathrm{realize}}$; a realized charged carrier beside a residual below $\delta$ refutes $h_{\mathrm{signal}}$; a realized charged carrier whose population or rate is below its floor refutes $h_{\mathrm{pop}}$ or $h_{\mathrm{rate}}$; a bath below $T_0$ refutes $h_{\mathrm{temp}}$; a residual below a realized charged carrier’s product of population, rate and heat refutes $h_{\mathrm{couple}}$; and a measured residual above $\varepsilon$ refutes the identification of $B.R$ with it. With the certificate and the gap, the floors and the coupling put the floor $\delta > B.\varepsilon$ under the residual beside any realized charged carrier (`signal_floor`), so the capstone’s physical content is that the vacuum realizes the carrier of every read zero and realizes no charged one.

**Theorem 9.13** (`signal_floor`, `every_violation_exceeds_detection_gap`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> c · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> $\varnothing$\])**.** From population and rate floors $n_0, r_0$, a bath temperature $T \ge T_0$, and the coupling $R \ge \mathrm{population}\cdot\mathrm{rate}\cdot\texttt{landauerHeatPerEvent}(T)$ at a carrier: $R \ge \delta$. From $h_{\mathrm{realize}}$, that the vacuum instantiates the carrier of every read zero, and $h_{\mathrm{signal}}$, that a realized charged carrier puts the floor $\delta$ under $R$: every read zero off the line forces $R \ge \delta$.

**Theorem 9.14** (`classical_rh_from_physico_formal_closure`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> c · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> $\varnothing$\])**.** From the reading $h_{\mathrm{read}}$, vacuum realization $h_{\mathrm{realize}}$, the population floor $h_{\mathrm{pop}}$, the rate floor $h_{\mathrm{rate}}$, the temperature floor $h_{\mathrm{temp}} : T \ge T_0$, the coupling $h_{\mathrm{couple}}$, a certified bound $B$, and the gap $h_{\mathrm{gap}} : B.\varepsilon < \delta$: $$\mathrm{ClassicalRH}.$$ Discharged on the carrier and no longer hypotheses: that the carrier of an off-line zero is charged, realization itself being the printed premise $h_{\mathrm{realize}}$, and that its annihilation erases one label. The heat per label enters as the definition $\texttt{landauerHeatPerEvent}\,T = T\cdot\texttt{ln2\_scaled}$, and its floor $T\ln 2 \ge T_0\ln 2$ comes from the printed premise $h_{\mathrm{temp}}$.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* Pointwise. At a read point either the offset is zero, or the carrier is charged, realized, and puts $B.R \ge \delta > B.\varepsilon \ge B.R$. ◻

</div>

**Theorem 9.15** (`no_third_position_on_the_carrier`, `realization_is_the_premise`, `the_one_exit_is_a_second_register`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> c / t / c · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> $\varnothing$/ <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** Under the reading, the bound and the gap, the denial of the hypothesis and the two physical premises cannot all stand. Under the predicate that realizes every carrier, $h_{\mathrm{realize}}$ holds at every configuration; under the predicate that realizes none, it fails at the pair world of the discrete off point $(1,0)$. Under the reading, a certified bound, the gap, and the signal floor of a realized charged carrier, $$\neg\mathrm{ClassicalRH} \ \to\ \exists p,\ Z_\zeta\,p \wedge \neg\mathrm{onLine}\,p \wedge \neg\mathrm{realized}(\mathrm{map\_zero\_to\_carrier}\,p).$$

Under the reading, the bound, the gap and the signal floor, a denier of the hypothesis asserts a read zero off the line whose carrier state is instantiated in no measured register: a second register, a second world. Under those premises the denier owns that assertion and nothing else is open; a reader who refuses one of the premises, the reading, the bound, the gap, the realization or the signal floor, refuses an input printed in the signature, and `the_reading_is_keyed` of Section 9.5 and `realization_is_the_premise` prove the reading and the realization to be such inputs. The cone of the last theorem is not empty, because the step from a failed universal to its witness is classical; `bridge_from_realization` and the two bundles of the physical binder, Theorem 9.17, also print the three standard axioms.

**Listing 35. The certified bound, the detection gap, the signal floor (§VIII-e)** (master lines 9953 to 9987)

       9953  /-! ## VIII-e · the certified bound, the physical premises, and the physico-formal capstone -/
       9954  
       9955  /-- A CERTIFIED OBSERVATIONAL BOUND: the residual observable R, the sensitivity ε, the certificate R ≤ ε, and the
       9956      name of the dataset that issued it. A measurement is a premise by its nature; this is the type it is entered as. -/
       9957  structure CertifiedObservationalBound where
       9958    R : Nat
       9959    ε : Nat
       9960    certificate : R ≤ ε
       9961    dataset : String
       9962  
       9963  /-- The detection gap: the uniform floor a realized charged carrier puts under the residual observable,
       9964      δ = n₀ · r₀ · (T₀ · ln 2). -/
       9965  def detectionGap (n0 r0 T0 : Nat) : Nat := n0 * r0 * landauerHeatPerEvent T0
       9966  
       9967  /-- The gap is positive exactly when its three floors are. -/
       9968  theorem detectionGap_pos {n0 r0 T0 : Nat} (hn : n0 > 0) (hr : r0 > 0) (hT : T0 > 0) : detectionGap n0 r0 T0 > 0 :=
       9969    Nat.mul_pos (Nat.mul_pos hn hr) (Nat.mul_pos hT (by decide))
       9970  
       9971  /-- THE SIGNAL FLOOR OF A REALIZED CHARGED CARRIER, from the three floors and the coupling: population × rate × heat
       9972      per event is at least n₀ · r₀ · (T₀ · ln 2), and the residual covers it. -/
       9973  theorem signal_floor {R n0 r0 T0 T : Nat} (population rate : PhysicalCarrier → Nat) (c : PhysicalCarrier)
       9974      (h_pop : population c ≥ n0) (h_rate : rate c ≥ r0) (h_temp : T ≥ T0)
       9975      (h_couple : R ≥ LeastErasureDoF.residual (population c) (rate c) (landauerHeatPerEvent T)) :
       9976      R ≥ detectionGap n0 r0 T0 :=
       9977    Nat.le_trans (Nat.mul_le_mul (Nat.mul_le_mul h_pop h_rate) (heat_floor_from_temperature h_temp)) h_couple
       9978  
       9979  /-- EVERY VIOLATION EXCEEDS THE DETECTION GAP. Two physical premises, named: the vacuum instantiates the carrier of
       9980      every read zero (h_realize); a realized charged carrier puts the floor δ under R (h_signal). Then a read zero
       9981      off the line forces R ≥ δ. That the zero's carrier is charged is theorem (VIII-c), not premise. -/
       9982  theorem every_violation_exceeds_detection_gap
       9983      {Zζ : Config} {R δ : Nat} (realized : PhysicalCarrier → Prop)
       9984      (h_realize : ∀ p, Zζ p → realized (map_zero_to_carrier p))
       9985      (h_signal  : ∀ c, realized c → ¬ Neutral c → R ≥ δ)
       9986      (p : Point) (hp : Zζ p) (hoff : ¬ onLine p) : R ≥ δ :=
       9987    h_signal _ (h_realize p hp) (mathematical_violation_forces_physical_discard p hoff).1

      10156    intro hnone
      10157    apply hno

      10165          (h_signal _ hr (mathematical_violation_forces_physical_discard p hoff).1) B.certificate) h_gap)
      10166          (Nat.lt_irrefl _)⟩).elim

## The apparatus cargo

Part VIII-b belongs to the formal closure, as the file assigns it, and is set here beside the physical carrier, its own copy of the carrier type being written by the same constructors; its Stage 2 theorem, `ApparatusCargo.stage2_optional_corroboration`, prints the physical premises in its signature and concludes from the reading, the bound, the gap and its pointwise discharge; it is the file’s optional corroboration and enters no closure stated here. It formalizes the local verification event itself. A $\texttt{VerificationEvent}$ carries a state $\mathrm{before}$, a state $\mathrm{after}$, and the field $\mathrm{after} = \mathrm{annihilate}(\mathrm{before})$.

**Theorem 9.16** (`local_computation_is_forgetting`, `computation_enacts_stage1`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> $\varnothing$\])**.** Every verification event lands on the annihilation of its state. Every event supplies a $\mathrm{Stage1}$ witness: forgetting done and `ApparatusCargo.physicalFloor` witnessed at the state it lands on, the floor there being that some carrier state equals that state.

The formal loop of Part X, the cargo loop and the retrospective seal, uses no physical observation; the file marks Parts VII and VIII as the formal loop’s optional retrospective corroboration, fenced conditional theorems the loop does not consume, and their physical premises stand here as the physical closure for the reader who takes physics as arbiter. The joint seal of Theorem 7.28, in §X-l, reads the concrete capstone at the look back beside the loop and is consumed only by the complex extensions.

**Listing 38. The apparatus cargo: the event and Stage 1 (Part VIII-b)** (master lines 10359 to 10409)

      10359  /-! ## core · the carrier, the event, Stage 1 -/
      10360  
      10361  /-- THE APPARATUS CARRIER. Two constructors: a self-conjugate state at a
      10362      height, or a member of a conjugate pair of magnitude m + 1 at a height
      10363      with the sign that tells it from its partner. -/
      10364  inductive PhysicalCarrier where
      10365    | selfConjugate (t : Int)
      10366    | conjugatePair (m : Nat) (t : Int) (sign : Bool)
      10367  
      10368  /-- Annihilation, the physical discard: a member of a pair goes to the neutral
      10369      state at its height; a neutral state stays. The sign is kept nowhere. -/
      10370  def annihilate : PhysicalCarrier → PhysicalCarrier
      10371    | .selfConjugate t => .selfConjugate t
      10372    | .conjugatePair _ t _ => .selfConjugate t
      10373  
      10374  /-- A verification event: the apparatus moves from `before` to `after`,
      10375      and `after` is the annihilation of `before` — one label forgotten. -/
      10376  structure VerificationEvent where
      10377    before : PhysicalCarrier
      10378    after : PhysicalCarrier
      10379    h_forget : after = annihilate before
      10380  
      10381  /-- THE LOCAL COMPUTATION IS A FORGETTING: the event's own field. -/
      10382  theorem local_computation_is_forgetting (e : VerificationEvent) :
      10383      e.after = annihilate e.before :=
      10384    e.h_forget
      10385  
      10386  /-- The physical floor: some state is realized. -/
      10387  def physicalFloor (realized : PhysicalCarrier → Prop) : Prop := ∃ c, realized c
      10388  
      10389  /-- The event witnesses the floor at the state it lands on. -/
      10390  theorem event_witnesses_floor (e : VerificationEvent)
      10391      (realized : PhysicalCarrier → Prop) (h : realized e.after) :
      10392      physicalFloor realized :=
      10393    ⟨e.after, h⟩
      10394  
      10395  /-- STAGE 1: forgetting done, floor witnessed. -/
      10396  structure Stage1 where
      10397    event : VerificationEvent
      10398    forgetting_done : event.after = annihilate event.before
      10399    floor_witnessed : physicalFloor (fun c => c = event.after)
      10400  
      10401  /-- Stage 1 closes on its own fields: forgetting done and floor witnessed. -/
      10402  theorem stage1_closes (s : Stage1) :
      10403      s.event.after = annihilate s.event.before ∧
      10404      physicalFloor (fun c => c = s.event.after) :=
      10405    ⟨s.forgetting_done, s.floor_witnessed⟩
      10406  
      10407  /-- THE COMPUTATION ENACTS STAGE 1: every verification event supplies one. -/
      10408  def computation_enacts_stage1 (e : VerificationEvent) : Stage1 :=
      10409    ⟨e, e.h_forget, ⟨e.after, rfl⟩⟩

# The Master Closure

**Theorem 10.1** (`the_flipped_formal_master_closure`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** The following hold as one conjunction: the constructed root $\mathrm{RA}_0$ (`TOE0.root_on_the_constructed_domain`); the prime-side hypothesis `PrimeFreedom.RH` forces the line on its chart, the forcing half of `PrimeFreedom.rh_is_the_weakest_forcing_premise`; the unconditional route is blocked on the discrete chart (`RememberedOffered.the_unconditional_route_is_blocked`); at every reflection-closed configuration $S$ of Part III’s chart the form of a proof is the hypothesis: an act at $S$ is a field of the value at $S$, any premise yielding the value at $S$, or its negation, yields a field of the value, or of its negation, at $S$, and least erasure, the root read twice, the zero reports and the prime bound are the value (`RememberedOffered.the_form_is_the_hypothesis`); every verification event is a forgetting and enacts Stage 1 (`ApparatusCargo`); the freedom root and Stage 1 are inhabited (`BoundChain`); for every discrete configuration $S$, $\mathrm{Value}(\mathrm{Rec}S)$, $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}S)$, its self-verification, the identification at the record, and the transport measure; the eleven-part complex binding (`BoundChainMathlib.zeta_binding`) paired with the theorem that `RiemannHypothesis` follows in one term from the 1-bit bridge (`BoundChainMathlib.rh_from_the_cargo_loop`); and the native complex block $\neg\forall S,\ \mathrm{Closed}(S) \to \mathrm{Value}(S)$ over $\mathbb{C}$.

The compiler prints the cone of the master closure as \[`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`\] and the file pins it. Two of the four divisions of Table 1 enter by conjuncts, the foundation by its root, its forcing premise, its discrete block and the form of proof at every closed configuration of Part III’s chart, from Parts I to III, and the formal side by the apparatus cargo of Part VIII-b, the discrete arch, the complex binding paired with `rh_from_the_cargo_loop`, and the native complex block; the master closure of Part XI is the theorem itself. The physical side, Parts VII and VIII, is bound by its own closure, the physico-formal closure of Theorem 9.17, pinned at the same cone, its capstones pinned at the empty cone. Forty-three results of Part X that stand outside the complex binding are bound into one theorem beside the master closure, and the two closures with the extensions into another.

**Theorem 10.2** (`the_complex_extensions`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** The following forty-three hold as one conjunction, each by its exact type: the transfer status; the three analytic-face laws; `record_decides_nothing`; `offline_zero_iff_not_rh` and `no_offline_refuter_seals_rh`; `classes_coincide_under_ra_zeta`; the strip closure in its two forms (Theorem 7.3); the orbit collapse on every reflection-closed set, at the record and in its conditional form (Theorems 7.10 and 7.11); the discrete chart homomorphism (Theorem 7.15); the closure of the zeros under $s \mapsto 1-s$ (Theorem 7.6); Schwarz reflection (Theorem 7.4); the closure of the zeros under the fold (Theorem 7.7); retraction injectivity of the zeros as the hypothesis, and its conditional form (Theorem 7.12); the carrier in the plane (Theorem 7.16); strip confinement in its two forms (Theorem 7.8); the socket at the zeros (Theorem 7.13); the unconditional retrospective seal (Theorem 7.20); the canonical apex (Theorem 7.22); the separation of one record by the witness over $\mathbb{C}$ (Theorem 7.24); the canonical normal-form bridge (Theorem 7.25); the analytic target reduction (Theorem 7.27); the joint physico-formal seal (Theorem 7.28); the Round 2 halt, the residual monism and Round 2 complete (Theorem 7.29); the analytic route sealed (Theorem 7.30); the look-back at the Ground-On-Line locus and its loop (Theorem 7.32); the strict strip of the nontrivial zeros and of the completed zeros, and their coincidence (Theorem 7.33); the zero-free band, its equivalence with the hypothesis, the band twin and the self-recognition of the zeros (Theorem 7.34); and the self-recognition closure (Theorem 7.35).

**Theorem 10.3** (`the_twin_binder_one_locus`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** The physico-formal closure (Theorem 9.17), the master closure (Theorem 10.1) and the complex extensions (Theorem 10.2) hold as one conjunction, each by its exact type.

The compiler prints the cone of both as \[`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`\] and the file pins them. The twin binder is one theorem of the file: the physical closure and the formal closure, each with its premises printed in its own signatures, and the two bridges between them, bound in one conjunction, checked by one kernel, terminating on one locus (Section 11).
