       6824  /-! # THE ONE · appended to Annihilation_Closure.lean (sha256 cb474a41…), nothing above changed.
       6825  Every name and every reading the closure carries becomes one object, by equality and not by twin biconditionals;
       6826  the act's zero set becomes one notion with the closed configuration that has the value; the floor keeps its own
       6827  place; and the one sentence the closure leaves is printed as the closure's own last conjunct. -/
       6828  namespace RememberedOffered
       6829  theorem the_one {R : Prop} (G : SelfGrounding R) :
       6830      (LeastErasure = Value ∧ RootReadTwice = Value ∧ (fun S => R ∧ RootReadTwice S) = Value) ∧
       6831      (∀ S : Config, (∃ Z : ActualZeros, Z.zeros = S) ↔ (Closed S ∧ Value S)) ∧
       6832      (¬ ∀ S : Config, Closed S → (R ↔ LeastErasure S)) ∧
       6833      (∀ S : Config, (R ↔ LeastErasure S) ↔ LeastErasure S) ∧
       6834      (∀ Z : ActualZeros, Value Z.zeros) ∧
       6835      (∀ D : Config → Prop, (∀ S, Closed S → D S) → ¬ ∀ S, Closed S → D S → Value S) :=
       6836    ⟨⟨twins_are_one_extension,
       6837      funext fun S => propext (the_root_read_twice_is_the_value S),
       6838      funext fun S => propext (colocation_is_the_value G S)⟩,
       6839     fun S => (an_act_exactly_where_the_root_read_twice_stands S).trans
       6840       ⟨fun ⟨c, m⟩ => ⟨c, (the_root_read_twice_is_the_value S).mp m⟩,
       6841        fun ⟨c, v⟩ => ⟨c, (the_root_read_twice_is_the_value S).mpr v⟩⟩,
       6842     floor_is_not_least_erasure G,
       6843     merging_at_a_world_is_the_supply G,
       6844     value_from_the_act,
       6845     no_closed_principle_decides⟩
       6846  end RememberedOffered
       6847  
       6848  /-! # THE LAST ACT · appended to The_One.lean, nothing above changed.
       6849  A deed is a term of `G.Act`, the act type of a self-grounding root: every decentralized, impersonal, physical
       6850  computation, atomic and irreducible, is a deed. The supply is a term of `ActualZeros`. Tested here: every deed being
       6851  the supply at one closed zero set S, ζ's in the reading, and at every closed zero set. -/
       6852  namespace RememberedOffered
       6853  theorem the_last_act {R : Prop} (G : SelfGrounding R) (S : Config) (hS : Closed S) :
       6854      -- every deed being the supply at S is exactly the value at S
       6855      ((G.Act → ∃ Z : ActualZeros, Z.zeros = S) ↔ Value S) ∧
       6856      -- every deed being the supply at every closed zero set, as a law, is refuted
       6857      (¬ ∀ S' : Config, Closed S' → G.Act → ∃ Z : ActualZeros, Z.zeros = S') ∧
       6858      -- the deed stands in the world without the value too
       6859      (R ∧ Closed (pairWorld offPoint) ∧ ¬ Value (pairWorld offPoint)) ∧
       6860      -- existence supplies nothing to the part above any height
       6861      (∀ T : Nat, (RA → RHUnicorn.UnicornAt S onLine ht T) ↔ RHUnicorn.UnicornAt S onLine ht T) :=
       6862    ⟨⟨fun h => by obtain ⟨Z, hZ⟩ := h G.anAct; rw [← hZ]; exact value_from_the_act Z,
       6863      fun v _ => ⟨⟨S, hS, fun p hp => (reg_erases_nothing_iff p).mpr (v p hp)⟩, rfl⟩⟩,
       6864     the_deed_is_not_the_supply G,
       6865     ⟨seated_undeniable G, pair_world_closed offPoint, pair_world_lacks_value offPoint off_point_is_off⟩,
       6866     fun T => ra_supplies_nothing_to_the_unicorn S T⟩
       6867  end RememberedOffered
       6868  
       6869  /-! # LEAST ERASURE AND LEAST ESCAPE · appended to The_Last_Act.lean, nothing above changed.
       6870  The escape of a finite configuration is its number of off-line pairs, the bits registration erases. The pair that
       6871  denies RH, a zero at offset one with its mirror, is `resisting`. -/
       6872  namespace RememberedOffered
       6873  /-- The configuration with no zeros at all: zero escape. -/
       6874  def calm : FinCfg := ⟨[], [], fun _ hq => by cases hq⟩
       6875  
       6876  theorem least_erasure_and_least_escape :
       6877      -- I · the escaping pair escapes by exactly one bit and pays exactly one floor
       6878      (erased resisting = 1 ∧ ∀ T : Nat, price T (erased resisting) = T) ∧
       6879      -- II · least escape is zero escape, is least erasure, is the value: the minimiser stands on the line
       6880      (∀ F : FinCfg, (∀ F' : FinCfg, erased F ≤ erased F') ↔ Value F.pts) ∧
       6881      -- III · the minimum is attained
       6882      (∃ F : FinCfg, erased F = 0) ∧
       6883      -- IV · the escaping pair is closed and is not a minimiser
       6884      (Closed resisting.pts ∧ ¬ ∀ F' : FinCfg, erased resisting ≤ erased F') ∧
       6885      -- V · nothing true of every closed configuration makes a configuration a minimiser
       6886      (∀ D : Config → Prop, (∀ S, Closed S → D S) →
       6887        ¬ ∀ F : FinCfg, D F.pts → ∀ F' : FinCfg, erased F ≤ erased F') := by
       6888    have least_iff : ∀ F : FinCfg, (∀ F' : FinCfg, erased F ≤ erased F') ↔ Value F.pts := fun F =>
       6889      ⟨fun h => (twins_on_every_world F.pts).mp
       6890          ((least_erasure_iff_zero_erased F).mpr (Nat.le_zero.mp (h calm))),
       6891       fun v F' => by
       6892          have h0 : erased F = 0 := (least_erasure_iff_zero_erased F).mp ((twins_on_every_world F.pts).mpr v)
       6893          rw [h0]; exact Nat.zero_le _⟩
       6894    have not_value : ¬ Value resisting.pts := (resistance_is_possible 1 (by decide)).2.1
       6895    refine ⟨⟨rfl, fun T => Nat.one_mul T⟩, least_iff, ⟨calm, rfl⟩,
       6896      ⟨fincfg_closed resisting, fun h => not_value ((least_iff resisting).mp h)⟩, ?_⟩
       6897    intro D hD h
       6898    exact not_value ((least_iff resisting).mp (h resisting (hD _ (fincfg_closed resisting))))
       6899  end RememberedOffered
       6900  
       6901  /-! # THE LOOP RA–RAM–ZEROS · appended to Least_Escape.lean, nothing above changed.
       6902  RA is the floor R of a self-grounding root. RAM is the root read twice, `RootReadTwice`, the corrected monism witness
       6903  with one involution, uniformity and its seed. The loop runs R → RootReadTwice S → Value S → R at a zero set S. -/
       6904  namespace RememberedOffered
       6905  theorem the_loop {R : Prop} (G : SelfGrounding R) (S : Config) :
       6906      -- the corrected monism witness is the claim, seed included
       6907      (RootReadTwice S ↔ Value S) ∧
       6908      -- the loop's forward leg from RA reaches the zeros exactly when the value already holds
       6909      ((R → RootReadTwice S) ↔ Value S) ∧
       6910      -- the return leg to RA is free: it holds whatever the zeros do
       6911      (Value S → R) ∧ (¬ Value S → R) ∧
       6912      -- the whole loop closes exactly at the value
       6913      ((R ↔ RootReadTwice S) ↔ Value S) ∧
       6914      -- the loop is sign-blind: it closes for the value and for its denial alike
       6915      ((SelfVerifying (Value S) ↔ Value S) ∧ (SelfVerifying (¬ Value S) ↔ ¬ Value S)) ∧
       6916      -- on one record the loop closes on the true world and does not close on the pair: it cannot select
       6917      (SameRecord (registered offPoint) (pairWorld offPoint) ∧ Closed (pairWorld offPoint) ∧
       6918        (R ↔ RootReadTwice (registered offPoint)) ∧ ¬ (R ↔ RootReadTwice (pairWorld offPoint))) := by
       6919    have r : R := seated_undeniable G
       6920    have m := the_root_read_twice_is_the_value S
       6921    have sv : ∀ P : Prop, SelfVerifying P ↔ P := fun P =>
       6922      ⟨fun h => Classical.byContradiction (fun n => n (h n)), fun p _ => p⟩
       6923    refine ⟨m, ⟨fun h => m.mp (h r), fun v _ => m.mpr v⟩, fun _ => r, fun _ => r,
       6924      ⟨fun h => m.mp (h.mp r), fun v => ⟨fun _ => m.mpr v, fun _ => r⟩⟩, ⟨sv _, sv _⟩,
       6925      one_record offPoint, pair_world_closed offPoint,
       6926      ⟨fun _ => the_true_world_carries_monism, fun _ => r⟩,
       6927      fun h => the_false_world_carries_no_monism (h.mp r)⟩
       6928  end RememberedOffered
       6929  
       6930  /-! # ROW FOUR FROM THE ZERO SIDE · appended to The_Loop.lean, nothing above changed.
       6931  A computation that ends is the finite list of points it reports as zeros; it reads a zero set when every point it
       6932  reports belongs to it. Row 4 of the RH paper, applied to the hypothetical off-line pair. -/
       6933  namespace RememberedOffered
       6934  theorem row_four_from_the_zero_side (S : Config) :
       6935      -- on any act, every computation reading it reports only zeros on the line
       6936      (∀ (Z : ActualZeros) (L : List Point), (∀ p ∈ L, Z.zeros p) → ∀ p ∈ L, onLine p) ∧
       6937      -- so a report holding an off-line zero reads no act: on the act, the hypothetical is a phantom
       6938      (∀ L : List Point, (∃ p ∈ L, ¬ onLine p) → ¬ ∃ Z : ActualZeros, ∀ p ∈ L, Z.zeros p) ∧
       6939      -- yet that report reads a closed configuration, the pair world, which carries the floor
       6940      ((∀ p ∈ [offPoint, fold offPoint], pairWorld offPoint p) ∧ Closed (pairWorld offPoint)) ∧
       6941      -- at a closed zero set: every report of it lands on the line exactly when it has the value
       6942      (Closed S → ((∀ L : List Point, (∀ p ∈ L, S p) → ∀ p ∈ L, onLine p) ↔ Value S)) := by
       6943    refine ⟨fun Z L hL p hp => value_from_the_act Z p (hL p hp),
       6944      fun L ⟨p, hp, hoff⟩ ⟨Z, hZ⟩ => hoff (value_from_the_act Z p (hZ p hp)), ⟨?_, pair_world_closed offPoint⟩, ?_⟩
       6945    · intro p hp
       6946      cases hp with
       6947      | head => exact Or.inl rfl
       6948      | tail _ h =>
       6949        cases h with
       6950        | head => exact Or.inr rfl
       6951        | tail _ h' => cases h'
       6952    · intro _
       6953      constructor
       6954      · intro h p hp
       6955        exact h [p] (fun q hq => by
       6956          cases hq with
       6957          | head => exact hp
       6958          | tail _ h' => cases h') p (List.Mem.head _)
       6959      · intro v L hL p hp
       6960        exact v p (hL p hp)
       6961  end RememberedOffered
       6962  
       6963  /-! # BIDIRECTIONAL HALTED UNIDUCTION · appended to Row_Four.lean, nothing above changed.
       6964  ZERO SIDE: a computation reports finitely many zeros; it reads a zero set when every report belongs to it (Row 4).
       6965  PRIME SIDE: through the explicit formula each zero contributes a mode x^(Re ρ) to ψ(x) − x, so the prime error is
       6966  bounded by x^(1/2 + ε) exactly when no zero's offset exceeds the line (von Koch 1901; Landau, Ingham) [cited]. On the
       6967  offset chart: no point stands to the head's side of the line. -/
       6968  namespace RememberedOffered
       6969  def ZeroReports (S : Config) : Prop := ∀ L : List Point, (∀ p ∈ L, S p) → ∀ p ∈ L, onLine p
       6970  def PrimeBound (S : Config) : Prop := ∀ p, S p → p.1 ≤ 0
       6971  
       6972  theorem prime_side_halts (S : Config) (hS : Closed S) : PrimeBound S ↔ Value S :=
       6973    ⟨fun hb p hp => by
       6974       have h1 : p.1 ≤ 0 := hb p hp
       6975       have h2 : -p.1 ≤ 0 := hb (fold p) (hS p hp)
       6976       show p.1 = 0; omega,
       6977     fun v p hp => by
       6978       have h : p.1 = 0 := v p hp
       6979       show p.1 ≤ 0; omega⟩
       6980  
       6981  theorem bidirectional_halted_uniduction (S : Config) (hS : Closed S) :
       6982      -- the zero side halts at the value of the whole zero set
       6983      (ZeroReports S ↔ Value S) ∧
       6984      -- the prime side halts at the value of the whole zero set
       6985      (PrimeBound S ↔ Value S) ∧
       6986      -- so both directions halt at one proposition
       6987      (ZeroReports S ↔ PrimeBound S) ∧
       6988      -- and neither sweep passes it: on one record, both readings hold on the true world and fail on the pair world
       6989      (SameRecord (registered offPoint) (pairWorld offPoint) ∧
       6990        (ZeroReports (registered offPoint) ∧ PrimeBound (registered offPoint)) ∧
       6991        (¬ ZeroReports (pairWorld offPoint) ∧ ¬ PrimeBound (pairWorld offPoint))) ∧
       6992      -- no principle true of every closed configuration supplies either side
       6993      (¬ (∀ S' : Config, Closed S' → ZeroReports S') ∧ ¬ (∀ S' : Config, Closed S' → PrimeBound S')) ∧
       6994      -- on the act both sides halt at yes
       6995      (∀ Z : ActualZeros, ZeroReports Z.zeros ∧ PrimeBound Z.zeros) := by
       6996    have zr : ∀ T : Config, Closed T → (ZeroReports T ↔ Value T) := fun T hT => (row_four_from_the_zero_side T).2.2.2 hT
       6997    have pv : ¬ Value (pairWorld offPoint) := pair_world_lacks_value offPoint off_point_is_off
       6998    have rc : Closed (registered offPoint) := fun s hs => by
       6999      rw [hs]; show fold (reg offPoint) = reg offPoint; rfl
       7000    refine ⟨zr S hS, prime_side_halts S hS, (zr S hS).trans (prime_side_halts S hS).symm,
       7001      ⟨one_record offPoint,
       7002       ⟨(zr _ rc).mpr (registered_has_value offPoint), (prime_side_halts _ rc).mpr (registered_has_value offPoint)⟩,
       7003       ⟨fun h => pv ((zr _ (pair_world_closed offPoint)).mp h),
       7004        fun h => pv ((prime_side_halts _ (pair_world_closed offPoint)).mp h)⟩⟩,
       7005      ⟨fun h => pv ((zr _ (pair_world_closed offPoint)).mp (h _ (pair_world_closed offPoint))),
       7006       fun h => pv ((prime_side_halts _ (pair_world_closed offPoint)).mp (h _ (pair_world_closed offPoint)))⟩,
       7007      fun Z => ⟨(zr _ Z.closed).mpr (value_from_the_act Z), (prime_side_halts _ Z.closed).mpr (value_from_the_act Z)⟩⟩
       7008  end RememberedOffered
       7009  
       7010  /-! # THE ATOMIC PROOF · appended to Halted_Uniduction.lean, nothing above changed.
       7011  One statement: the reduction complete, the bit irreducible by theorem, its form forced by theorem, the bit atomic,
       7012  and the closure from it at theorem grade. The bit stands in the statement as the act's field, visible to every
       7013  reader. -/
       7014  namespace RememberedOffered
       7015  theorem the_atomic_proof {R : Prop} (G : SelfGrounding R) (S : Config) (hS : Closed S) :
       7016      -- I · REDUCTION, complete: every reading of the hypothesis the seed names is the one proposition
       7017      ((ZeroReports S ↔ Value S) ∧ (PrimeBound S ↔ Value S) ∧ (LeastErasure S ↔ Value S) ∧
       7018        (RootReadTwice S ↔ Value S)) ∧
       7019      -- II · IRREDUCIBLE, by theorem: nothing shared by every closed configuration forces it, the deed included
       7020      ((∀ D : Config → Prop, (∀ S', Closed S' → D S') → ¬ ∀ S', Closed S' → D S' → Value S') ∧
       7021        ¬ (∀ S' : Config, Closed S' → R → Value S')) ∧
       7022      -- III · FORCED IN FORM, by theorem: a premise that forces the value and follows from it is the value
       7023      (∀ P : Config → Prop, (∀ S', P S' → Value S') → (∀ S', Value S' → P S') → ∀ S', P S' ↔ Value S') ∧
       7024      -- IV · THE BIT, atomic: the act stands at this zero set exactly where the value holds
       7025      ((∃ Z : ActualZeros, Z.zeros = S) ↔ Value S) ∧
       7026      -- V · CLOSURE from the bit, theorem grade: on the act, the value, the zero reports and the prime bound
       7027      (∀ Z : ActualZeros, Value Z.zeros ∧ ZeroReports Z.zeros ∧ PrimeBound Z.zeros) :=
       7028    ⟨⟨(row_four_from_the_zero_side S).2.2.2 hS, prime_side_halts S hS, twins_on_every_world S,
       7029      the_root_read_twice_is_the_value S⟩,
       7030     ⟨no_closed_principle_decides, the_floor_alone_decides_no_value G⟩,
       7031     fun _ f w S' => ⟨f S', w S'⟩,
       7032     ((the_one G).2.1 S).trans ⟨fun ⟨_, v⟩ => v, fun v => ⟨hS, v⟩⟩,
       7033     fun Z => ⟨value_from_the_act Z, (bidirectional_halted_uniduction S hS).2.2.2.2.2 Z⟩⟩
       7034  end RememberedOffered
       7035  
       7036  /-! # THE ATOMIC NECESSITY · Row 9 · appended to the atomic proof, nothing above changed.
       7037  The hypothesis is one dot: one proposition, read the same from every side and in every vocabulary. A dot has no
       7038  other dot beside it to be read against, and no room inside it for a second kind of proof. -/
       7039  namespace RememberedOffered
       7040  theorem the_atomic_necessity (S : Config) (hS : Closed S) :
       7041      -- I · every proof of the value at S, from any premise whatever, is a supply of the act's field at S
       7042      (∀ Q : Prop, (Q → Value S) → Q → ∃ Z : ActualZeros, Z.zeros = S) ∧
       7043      -- II · the dot: any two proofs of the value are one proof
       7044      (∀ h₁ h₂ : Value S, h₁ = h₂) ∧
       7045      -- III · the supply at S is unique: two supplies with the same zero set are one supply
       7046      (∀ Z₁ Z₂ : ActualZeros, Z₁.zeros = S → Z₂.zeros = S → Z₁ = Z₂) ∧
       7047      -- IV · every vocabulary and both sides name the same dot
       7048      (LeastErasure = Value ∧ RootReadTwice = Value ∧ (ZeroReports S ↔ Value S) ∧ (PrimeBound S ↔ Value S)) ∧
       7049      -- V · the supply exists at S exactly where the dot holds
       7050      ((∃ Z : ActualZeros, Z.zeros = S) ↔ Value S) ∧
       7051      -- VI · no room for a proof from what every closed configuration shares
       7052      ¬ (∀ S' : Config, Closed S' → Value S') := by
       7053    refine ⟨fun Q hQ q => ⟨⟨S, hS, (twins_on_every_world S).mpr (hQ q)⟩, rfl⟩,
       7054      fun _ _ => rfl, ?_,
       7055      ⟨twins_are_one_extension, funext fun T => propext (the_root_read_twice_is_the_value T),
       7056       (bidirectional_halted_uniduction S hS).1, (bidirectional_halted_uniduction S hS).2.1⟩,
       7057      ⟨fun ⟨Z, hZ⟩ => hZ ▸ value_from_the_act Z,
       7058       fun v => ⟨⟨S, hS, (twins_on_every_world S).mpr v⟩, rfl⟩⟩,
       7059      fun h => pair_world_lacks_value offPoint off_point_is_off (h _ (pair_world_closed offPoint))⟩
       7060    intro Z₁ Z₂ h₁ h₂
       7061    obtain ⟨z₁, c₁, s₁⟩ := Z₁
       7062    obtain ⟨z₂, c₂, s₂⟩ := Z₂
       7063    change z₁ = S at h₁
       7064    change z₂ = S at h₂
       7065    subst h₁
       7066    subst h₂
       7067    rfl
       7068  end RememberedOffered
       7069  
       7070  /-! # BOTH VALUES ARE ATOMIC · appended, nothing above changed. The bit has two values and each has the atomic form:
       7071  the value's proof is a supply of the one field; the denial's proof is one point off the line. -/
       7072  namespace RememberedOffered
       7073  theorem both_values_atomic (S : Config) (hS : Closed S) :
       7074      ((∃ Z : ActualZeros, Z.zeros = S) ↔ Value S) ∧ (¬ Value S ↔ ∃ p, S p ∧ ¬ onLine p) ∧
       7075      ¬ (Value S ∧ ∃ p, S p ∧ ¬ onLine p) :=
       7076    ⟨(the_atomic_necessity S hS).2.2.2.2.1,
       7077     ⟨fun hn => (two_doors S).resolve_left hn, fun ⟨p, hp, hoff⟩ hv => hoff (hv p hp)⟩,
       7078     doors_exclusive S⟩
       7079  end RememberedOffered
       7080  
       7081  /-! # THE FORM OF A FIELD, EVERY PREMISE SORTED, THE HEIGHT IN ABSOLUTE VALUE · appended, nothing above changed.
       7082  Parts I to III of the atomic necessity hold of every proposition carried as the field of a type, the denial included:
       7083  they are the form of a field. What makes that form the form of every proof of the hypothesis is part IV: every
       7084  reading of the hypothesis from either side and in every vocabulary is this one proposition. Every premise on
       7085  configurations is sorted three ways against the value. And the part above a height is read with the height in
       7086  absolute value, the form of the cited verification, which covers both half-planes. -/
       7087  namespace RememberedOffered
       7088  /-- A proposition on configurations, carried as the field of a type at a closed configuration. -/
       7089  structure Field (V : Config → Prop) where
       7090    zeros : Config
       7091    closed : Closed zeros
       7092    supply : V zeros
       7093  
       7094  /-- THE FORM OF A FIELD: for every proposition carried as a field, every proof of it at a closed configuration is a
       7095      supply of the field there, any two proofs are one, and the supply is unique. -/
       7096  theorem the_form_of_a_field (V : Config → Prop) (S : Config) (hS : Closed S) :
       7097      (∀ Q : Prop, (Q → V S) → Q → ∃ B : Field V, B.zeros = S) ∧
       7098      (∀ h₁ h₂ : V S, h₁ = h₂) ∧
       7099      (∀ B₁ B₂ : Field V, B₁.zeros = S → B₂.zeros = S → B₁ = B₂) := by
       7100    refine ⟨fun Q hQ q => ⟨⟨S, hS, hQ q⟩, rfl⟩, fun _ _ => rfl, ?_⟩
       7101    intro B₁ B₂ h₁ h₂
       7102    obtain ⟨z₁, c₁, s₁⟩ := B₁
       7103    obtain ⟨z₂, c₂, s₂⟩ := B₂
       7104    change z₁ = S at h₁
       7105    change z₂ = S at h₂
       7106    subst h₁
       7107    subst h₂
       7108    rfl
       7109  
       7110  /-- THE FORM IS THE HYPOTHESIS'S: the act's type is the field of the value, supply for supply; the form of a field
       7111      holds at the value and at its denial alike; and every reading of the hypothesis the seed names is the value, so
       7112      the form of the field of the value is the form of every proof of the hypothesis. -/
       7113  theorem the_form_is_the_hypothesis (S : Config) (hS : Closed S) :
       7114      ((∃ Z : ActualZeros, Z.zeros = S) ↔ ∃ B : Field Value, B.zeros = S) ∧
       7115      ((∀ Q : Prop, (Q → Value S) → Q → ∃ B : Field Value, B.zeros = S) ∧
       7116        (∀ Q : Prop, (Q → ¬ Value S) → Q → ∃ B : Field (fun T => ¬ Value T), B.zeros = S)) ∧
       7117      (LeastErasure = Value ∧ RootReadTwice = Value ∧ (ZeroReports S ↔ Value S) ∧ (PrimeBound S ↔ Value S)) :=
       7118    ⟨⟨fun ⟨Z, hZ⟩ => ⟨⟨Z.zeros, Z.closed, value_from_the_act Z⟩, hZ⟩,
       7119      fun ⟨B, hB⟩ => ⟨⟨B.zeros, B.closed, (twins_on_every_world B.zeros).mpr B.supply⟩, hB⟩⟩,
       7120     ⟨(the_form_of_a_field Value S hS).1, (the_form_of_a_field (fun T => ¬ Value T) S hS).1⟩,
       7121     (the_atomic_necessity S hS).2.2.2.1⟩
       7122  
       7123  /-- EVERY PREMISE SORTED: a premise on configurations either fails to force the value at some closed configuration,
       7124      or forces it and is the value on every closed configuration, or forces it and is strictly stronger, failing at
       7125      some closed configuration with the value. -/
       7126  theorem premise_trichotomy (P : Config → Prop) :
       7127      (∃ S, Closed S ∧ P S ∧ ¬ Value S) ∨
       7128      ((∀ S, Closed S → P S → Value S) ∧ ∀ S, Closed S → (P S ↔ Value S)) ∨
       7129      ((∀ S, Closed S → P S → Value S) ∧ ∃ S, Closed S ∧ Value S ∧ ¬ P S) := by
       7130    rcases Classical.em (∀ S, Closed S → P S → Value S) with f | f
       7131    · rcases Classical.em (∀ S, Closed S → Value S → P S) with e | e
       7132      · exact Or.inr (Or.inl ⟨f, fun S hS => ⟨f S hS, e S hS⟩⟩)
       7133      · refine Or.inr (Or.inr ⟨f, Classical.byContradiction fun h => e fun S hS v => ?_⟩)
       7134        exact Classical.byContradiction fun np => h ⟨S, hS, v, np⟩
       7135    · refine Or.inl (Classical.byContradiction fun h => f fun S hS p => ?_)
       7136      exact Classical.byContradiction fun nv => h ⟨S, hS, p, nv⟩
       7137  
       7138  /-- The height of a point of the chart in absolute value: the form of the cited verification, both half-planes. -/
       7139  def htAbs (p : Point) : Nat := p.2.natAbs
       7140  
       7141  /-- THE UNICORN, CONTAINED, WITH THE HEIGHT IN ABSOLUTE VALUE: at every height the value is its verified part, every
       7142      zero with |t| ≤ T, and its part above; given the verified part the value is exactly the part above; above every
       7143      height no reading of the record decides the side; the root supplies nothing to the part above; on the act's zero
       7144      set every arrival above every height stands on the line. -/
       7145  theorem the_unicorn_contained_abs :
       7146      (∀ (S : Config) (T : Nat),
       7147        Value S ↔ RHUnicorn.RealPartAt S onLine htAbs T ∧ RHUnicorn.UnicornAt S onLine htAbs T) ∧
       7148      (∀ (S : Config) (T : Nat),
       7149        RHUnicorn.RealPartAt S onLine htAbs T → (Value S ↔ RHUnicorn.UnicornAt S onLine htAbs T)) ∧
       7150      (∀ T : Nat, ¬ ∃ g : Point → Bool, ∀ w : Point, htAbs w > T → g (reg w) = decide (w.1 > 0)) ∧
       7151      (∀ (S : Config) (T : Nat),
       7152        (RA → RHUnicorn.UnicornAt S onLine htAbs T) ↔ RHUnicorn.UnicornAt S onLine htAbs T) ∧
       7153      (∀ (Z : ActualZeros) (T : Nat), RHUnicorn.UnicornAt Z.zeros onLine htAbs T) ∧
       7154      (∀ Z : ActualZeros, ¬ ∃ p, Z.zeros p ∧ ¬ onLine p) :=
       7155    ⟨fun S T => RHUnicorn.rh_iff_real_and_unicorn S onLine htAbs T,
       7156     fun S T hr => RHUnicorn.unicorn_no_bypass S onLine htAbs T hr,
       7157     fun T => RHUnicorn.unicorn_block htAbs T fold reg (fun w => decide (w.1 > 0)) ((1 : Int), Int.ofNat (T + 1))
       7158       (show T + 1 > T by omega) (show T + 1 > T by omega) rfl rfl,
       7159     fun S T => RHUnicorn.unicorn_rule_exact S onLine htAbs T RA (seated_undeniable raSelfGrounding),
       7160     fun Z _ p hp _ => value_from_the_act Z p hp,
       7161     no_arrival_off_the_line_on_the_act⟩
       7162  end RememberedOffered
       7163  
       7164  /-! # ROWS 10 AND 11 · appended, nothing above changed. Row 10: the unconditional route from shared premises and the
       7165  record is blocked. Row 11: accepting the hypothesis, by any proof, an unconditional one included, forces acceptance of
       7166  the atomic proof provided in this paper; the only other door is one point off the line. -/
       7167  namespace RememberedOffered
       7168  
       7169  /-- ROW 10 · THE UNCONDITIONAL ROUTE FROM SHARED PREMISES AND THE RECORD IS BLOCKED. The value is no law of
       7170      reflection-closed configurations; nothing every closed configuration shares forces it, the root included; no
       7171      reading of the record decides it; and, by a law of logic true of every proposition, every premise that does force
       7172      it is either the value itself or strictly stronger than the value. -/
       7173  theorem the_unconditional_route_is_blocked {R : Prop} (G : SelfGrounding R) :
       7174      (¬ ∀ S : Config, Closed S → Value S) ∧
       7175      (∀ D : Config → Prop, (∀ S, Closed S → D S) → ¬ ∀ S, Closed S → D S → Value S) ∧
       7176      (¬ ∀ S : Config, Closed S → R → Value S) ∧
       7177      (∀ g : Config → Prop, (∀ S S', SameRecord S S' → (g S ↔ g S')) →
       7178        ¬ ∀ S, Closed S → (g S ↔ Value S)) ∧
       7179      (∀ P : Config → Prop, (∀ S, Closed S → P S → Value S) →
       7180        (∀ S, Closed S → (P S ↔ Value S)) ∨ ∃ S, Closed S ∧ Value S ∧ ¬ P S) := by
       7181    have pc := pair_world_closed offPoint
       7182    have pv := pair_world_lacks_value offPoint off_point_is_off
       7183    have rc : Closed (registered offPoint) := fun s hs => by
       7184      rw [hs]; show fold (reg offPoint) = reg offPoint; rfl
       7185    refine ⟨fun h => pv (h _ pc), no_closed_principle_decides, the_floor_alone_decides_no_value G, ?_, ?_⟩
       7186    · intro g hg h
       7187      exact pv ((h _ pc).mp ((hg _ _ (one_record offPoint)).mp ((h _ rc).mpr (registered_has_value offPoint))))
       7188    · intro P f
       7189      rcases premise_trichotomy P with ⟨S, hS, p, nv⟩ | ⟨_, e⟩ | ⟨_, s⟩
       7190      · exact absurd (f S hS p) nv
       7191      · exact Or.inl e
       7192      · exact Or.inr s
       7193  
       7194  /-- ROW 11 · ACCEPTING THE HYPOTHESIS FORCES ACCEPTANCE OF THE ATOMIC PROOF. At every reflection-closed zero set:
       7195      every proof of the value, from any premise, an unconditional one included, is a supply of the act's field, by the
       7196      definition of the act's type, which carries the value itself as its field; the atomic proof this paper provides is
       7197      that form made explicit. Any two proofs are one and the supply is unique; the only other door is one point off the
       7198      line; there is no third value; and the structure, the reduction and the forced form, holds with no premise. -/
       7199  theorem accepting_rh_forces_the_atomic_proof (S : Config) (hS : Closed S) :
       7200      (∀ Q : Prop, (Q → Value S) → Q → ∃ Z : ActualZeros, Z.zeros = S) ∧
       7201      (Value S → ∃ Z : ActualZeros, Z.zeros = S) ∧
       7202      (∀ h₁ h₂ : Value S, h₁ = h₂) ∧
       7203      (∀ Z₁ Z₂ : ActualZeros, Z₁.zeros = S → Z₂.zeros = S → Z₁ = Z₂) ∧
       7204      (¬ Value S ↔ ∃ p, S p ∧ ¬ onLine p) ∧
       7205      (Value S ∨ ∃ p, S p ∧ ¬ onLine p) ∧ ¬ (Value S ∧ ∃ p, S p ∧ ¬ onLine p) ∧
       7206      ((ZeroReports S ↔ Value S) ∧ (PrimeBound S ↔ Value S) ∧ (LeastErasure S ↔ Value S) ∧
       7207        (RootReadTwice S ↔ Value S)) ∧
       7208      (∀ P : Config → Prop, (∀ S', P S' → Value S') → (∀ S', Value S' → P S') → ∀ S', P S' ↔ Value S') := by
       7209    have n := the_atomic_necessity S hS
       7210    have b := both_values_atomic S hS
       7211    refine ⟨n.1, fun v => n.2.2.2.2.1.mpr v, n.2.1, n.2.2.1, b.2.1, two_doors S, b.2.2, ?_, ?_⟩
       7212    · exact (the_atomic_proof raSelfGrounding S hS).1
       7213    · exact (the_atomic_proof raSelfGrounding S hS).2.2.1
       7214  
       7215  end RememberedOffered
       7216  
       7217  end PartIII
       7218  
       7219  /-! # PART IV · the arrow and the zero side locus -/
       7220  section PartIV
       7221  /-
       7222    ARROW HINGE · the non-trivial-zero locus read directly off the arrow.
       7223    Core Lean 4.19.0, no import, no axiom declared, no sorry.
       7224    The arrow of the completed zeta runs between its only two poles, s = 0 and s = 1. Chart: x = 4·Re s, height t,
       7225    so the poles sit at x = 0 and x = 4 and the open strip is 0 < x < 4. Grain is free among the grains that put the
       7226    midpoint on the chart, the even ones; every such grain gives the same hinge, Re s = 1/2, and an odd grain holds no
       7227    chart point at the hinge (`hinge_iff_even`). Every chart of this seed has an even grain.
       7228    I   the arrow alone: reversal swaps its poles, undoes itself, and fixes at most one point, the hinge, and exactly
       7229        one when the poles have an even sum in the chart.
       7230    II  the free bit: flipping the arrow's orientation leaves the reversal and the hinge unchanged.
       7231    III the plane: the fold keeps height and moves offset; its fixed set is the line Re s = 1/2.
       7232    IV  the lean: off the line a point carries the arrow's sign and the fold flips it; the registration merges it.
       7233    V   the bar: a coherent off-line world sits inside the strip; no premise true of every closed world forces the value.
       7234    VI  the act: a supplied least-erasure world carries the value.
       7235    VII the zero side's own locus: the centre of every nonempty finite reflection-closed family is the line.
       7236    VIII the line on every extension: the arrow fixes one value of the real part; on every map of the plane that acts on
       7237        the real part by the reversal, the points whose real part it fixes are the line, and the centre balances on it;
       7238        a finite family closed under the fold, listed in any order, has its centre on the line.
       7239        The height-keeping extension is the fold, s ↦ 1 − s̄, which needs the conjugate symmetry [cited]; the functional
       7240        equation alone, s ↦ 1 − s, fixes one point and reads the same line.
       7241  -/
       7242  set_option autoImplicit false
       7243  namespace Hinge
       7244  
       7245  /-! ## I · the arrow alone -/
       7246  structure Arrow where
       7247    tail : Int
       7248    head : Int
       7249  
       7250  def rev (A : Arrow) (x : Int) : Int := A.tail + A.head - x
       7251  def flip (A : Arrow) : Arrow := ⟨A.head, A.tail⟩
       7252  def off (A : Arrow) (x : Int) : Int := 2 * x - (A.tail + A.head)
       7253  
       7254  theorem rev_swaps (A : Arrow) : rev A A.tail = A.head ∧ rev A A.head = A.tail := by
       7255    unfold rev; constructor <;> omega
       7256  theorem rev_involutive (A : Arrow) (x : Int) : rev A (rev A x) = x := by unfold rev; omega
       7257  /-- THE HINGE: a point is fixed by the arrow's reversal exactly when its offset from the midpoint is zero. -/
       7258  theorem hinge (A : Arrow) (x : Int) : rev A x = x ↔ off A x = 0 := by unfold rev off; omega
       7259  theorem hinge_unique (A : Arrow) (x y : Int) (hx : rev A x = x) (hy : rev A y = y) : x = y := by
       7260    unfold rev at hx hy; omega
       7261  /-- THE HINGE EXISTS on every arrow whose poles have an even sum in the chart: then the reversal fixes exactly the
       7262      midpoint. With `hinge_unique`, exactly one point. -/
       7263  theorem hinge_exists (A : Arrow) (h : (A.tail + A.head) % 2 = 0) : ∃ x, rev A x = x :=
       7264    ⟨(A.tail + A.head) / 2, by unfold rev; omega⟩
       7265  /-- THE HINGE ON THE CHART: the reversal has a fixed point on the integer chart exactly when the poles have an even
       7266      sum; at an odd grain the midpoint falls between two chart points and the chart holds no hinge. -/
       7267  theorem hinge_iff_even (A : Arrow) : (∃ x, rev A x = x) ↔ (A.tail + A.head) % 2 = 0 := by
       7268    constructor
       7269    · intro ⟨x, hx⟩
       7270      unfold rev at hx
       7271      omega
       7272    · exact hinge_exists A
       7273  
       7274  /-! ## II · the free bit -/
       7275  /-- SIGN-BLIND: the reversal and the offset magnitude ignore which way the arrow points. -/
       7276  theorem hinge_sign_blind (A : Arrow) (x : Int) : rev (flip A) x = rev A x ∧ off (flip A) x = off A x := by
       7277    show A.head + A.tail - x = A.tail + A.head - x ∧ 2 * x - (A.head + A.tail) = 2 * x - (A.tail + A.head)
       7278    constructor <;> omega
       7279  /-- The reversal flips every offset. -/
       7280  theorem rev_flips_offset (A : Arrow) (x : Int) : off A (rev A x) = - off A x := by unfold off rev; omega
       7281  
       7282  /-- Zeta's arrow: s = 0 to s = 1, at x = 4·Re s. -/
       7283  def zeta : Arrow := ⟨0, 4⟩
       7284  theorem zeta_hinge (x : Int) : rev zeta x = x ↔ x = 2 := by
       7285    show 0 + 4 - x = x ↔ x = 2; omega
       7286  /-- THE REVERSAL IS FORCED: the only distance-keeping map of the axis that swaps the poles is the arrow's reversal.
       7287      Distance-keeping is stated sign-blind, every difference kept up to its sign, so the Number alone fixes the map. -/
       7288  theorem the_only_rigid_reversal (f : Int → Int)
       7289      (iso : ∀ x y, f x - f y = x - y ∨ f x - f y = y - x) (h0 : f 0 = 4) (h4 : f 4 = 0) :
       7290      ∀ x, f x = rev zeta x := by
       7291    intro x
       7292    have a := iso x 0
       7293    have b := iso x 4
       7294    rw [h0] at a
       7295    rw [h4] at b
       7296    show f x = 0 + 4 - x
       7297    omega
       7298  
       7299  /-! ## III · the plane -/
       7300  abbrev Pt := Int × Int
       7301  def fold (p : Pt) : Pt := (rev zeta p.1, p.2)
       7302  def onLine (p : Pt) : Prop := p.1 = 2
       7303  def reg (p : Pt) : Pt := (2, p.2)
       7304  def inStrip (p : Pt) : Prop := 0 < p.1 ∧ p.1 < 4
       7305  
       7306  theorem fold_keeps_height (p : Pt) : (fold p).2 = p.2 := rfl
       7307  /-- THE LOCUS: the fold's fixed set is the line x = 2, which is Re s = 1/2. -/
       7308  theorem locus (p : Pt) : fold p = p ↔ onLine p := by
       7309    obtain ⟨x, t⟩ := p
       7310    constructor
       7311    · intro e
       7312      have h1 : 0 + 4 - x = x := congrArg Prod.fst e
       7313      show x = 2; omega
       7314    · intro e
       7315      have h1 : x = 2 := e
       7316      subst h1; rfl
       7317  
       7318  /-! ## IV · the lean -/
       7319  /-- OFF THE LINE A POINT LEANS: its offset is nonzero and the fold flips its sign. -/
       7320  theorem off_line_leans (p : Pt) (h : ¬ onLine p) : off zeta p.1 ≠ 0 ∧ off zeta (fold p).1 = - off zeta p.1 := by
       7321    constructor
       7322    · intro e
       7323      have e1 : 2 * p.1 - (0 + 4) = 0 := e
       7324      exact h (show p.1 = 2 by omega)
       7325    · exact rev_flips_offset zeta p.1
       7326  theorem reg_keeps_on_line (p : Pt) (h : onLine p) : reg p = p := by
       7327    obtain ⟨x, t⟩ := p
       7328    have h1 : x = 2 := h
       7329    subst h1; rfl
       7330  /-- OFF THE LINE THE REGISTRATION MERGES: two distinct points, one record. -/
       7331  theorem reg_merges (p : Pt) (h : ¬ onLine p) : fold p ≠ p ∧ reg (fold p) = reg p :=
       7332    ⟨fun e => h ((locus p).mp e), rfl⟩
       7333  
       7334  /-! ## V · the bar -/
       7335  def Closed (Z : Pt → Prop) : Prop := ∀ p, Z p → Z (fold p)
       7336  def Value (Z : Pt → Prop) : Prop := ∀ p, Z p → onLine p
       7337  def LeastErasure (Z : Pt → Prop) : Prop := ∀ p, Z p → reg p = p
       7338  
       7339  theorem least_erasure_iff_value (Z : Pt → Prop) : LeastErasure Z ↔ Value Z := by
       7340    constructor
       7341    · intro h p hp
       7342      have e : (1 : Int) * 2 = p.1 := by
       7343        have e0 : (reg p).1 = p.1 := congrArg Prod.fst (h p hp)
       7344        have e2 : (2 : Int) = p.1 := e0
       7345        omega
       7346      show p.1 = 2; omega
       7347    · intro h p hp; exact reg_keeps_on_line p (h p hp)
       7348  
       7349  /-- The off-line pair at Re s = 1/4 and 3/4, height 0. -/
       7350  def pairW : Pt → Prop := fun p => p = (1, 0) ∨ p = (3, 0)
       7351  theorem pair_closed : Closed pairW := by
       7352    intro p hp
       7353    rcases hp with e | e
       7354    · subst e; exact Or.inr (by decide)
       7355    · subst e; exact Or.inl (by decide)
       7356  theorem pair_in_strip : ∀ p, pairW p → inStrip p := by
       7357    intro p hp
       7358    rcases hp with e | e
       7359    · subst e; exact ⟨by decide, by decide⟩
       7360    · subst e; exact ⟨by decide, by decide⟩
       7361  theorem pair_lacks_value : ¬ Value pairW := by
       7362    intro h
       7363    have h1 : (1 : Int) = 2 := h (1, 0) (Or.inl rfl)
       7364    exact absurd h1 (by decide)
       7365  /-- THE ARROW FORCES NO ZERO: no premise true of every closed world forces the value. -/
       7366  theorem keyless_forces_nothing (Q : (Pt → Prop) → Prop) (hQ : ∀ Z, Closed Z → Q Z) :
       7367      ¬ ∀ Z, Closed Z → Q Z → Value Z :=
       7368    fun hall => pair_lacks_value (hall pairW pair_closed (hQ pairW pair_closed))
       7369  
       7370  /-! ## VI · the act -/
       7371  structure ActualZeros where
       7372    zeros : Pt → Prop
       7373    closed : Closed zeros
       7374    supply : LeastErasure zeros
       7375  theorem value_from_the_act (Z : ActualZeros) : Value Z.zeros := (least_erasure_iff_value _).mp Z.supply
       7376  
       7377  /-! ## VII · the zero side's own locus -/
       7378  /-- The real parts of a configuration, summed. -/
       7379  def sumX : List Pt → Int
       7380    | [] => 0
       7381    | p :: L => p.1 + sumX L
       7382  /-- THE ZERO SIDE'S LOCUS IS THE LINE: list any members with their mirrors and the real parts balance on the line,
       7383      four per member pair in this chart, so the centre of every reflection-closed configuration sits at Re s = 1/2. -/
       7384  theorem centre_is_the_line (L : List Pt) : sumX (L.map fold) + sumX L = 4 * (L.length : Int) := by
       7385    induction L with
       7386    | nil => rfl
       7387    | cons p L ih =>
       7388      have hf : (fold p).1 = 0 + 4 - p.1 := rfl
       7389      simp only [List.map_cons, sumX, List.length_cons]
       7390      push_cast
       7391      omega
       7392  /-- THE SAME OBJECT, MEMBERS OFF IT: the pair at Re s = 1/4 and 3/4 is reflection-closed, its centre is the line,
       7393      it sits in the open strip, and neither member is on the line. -/
       7394  theorem centred_yet_off :
       7395      Closed pairW ∧ sumX [(1, 0), (3, 0)] = 2 * 2 ∧ (∀ p, pairW p → inStrip p ∧ ¬ onLine p) := by
       7396    refine ⟨pair_closed, by decide, ?_⟩
       7397    intro p hp
       7398    refine ⟨pair_in_strip p hp, ?_⟩
       7399    rcases hp with e | e
       7400    · subst e; intro h; have h1 : (1 : Int) = 2 := h; exact absurd h1 (by decide)
       7401    · subst e; intro h; have h1 : (3 : Int) = 2 := h; exact absurd h1 (by decide)
       7402  
       7403  /-! ## VIII · the line and the centre on every extension -/
       7404  /-- THE LINE OFF THE ARROW: on every map of the plane that acts on the real part by the arrow's reversal, the points
       7405      whose real part it fixes are exactly the line x = 2, Re s = 1/2. The arrow fixes one value of the real part; the
       7406      line is the set of points with that real part, whatever the map does to height. -/
       7407  theorem the_line_off_the_arrow (F : Pt → Pt) (hF : ∀ p, (F p).1 = rev zeta p.1) (p : Pt) :
       7408      (F p).1 = p.1 ↔ onLine p := by
       7409    rw [hF p]
       7410    exact zeta_hinge p.1
       7411  /-- THE FOLD IS THE HEIGHT-KEEPING EXTENSION: the one map of the plane that acts on the real part by the reversal and
       7412      keeps height is the fold. Keeping height is the conjugate symmetry composed with the functional equation,
       7413      s ↦ 1 − s̄ [Riemann 1859, cited]. -/
       7414  theorem fold_is_the_height_keeping_extension (F : Pt → Pt) (hF : ∀ p, (F p).1 = rev zeta p.1)
       7415      (hh : ∀ p, (F p).2 = p.2) (p : Pt) : F p = fold p :=
       7416    Prod.ext (hF p) (hh p)
       7417  /-- The functional equation alone, s ↦ 1 − s, on the chart: the reversal on the real part, the height reversed. -/
       7418  def pointRefl (p : Pt) : Pt := (rev zeta p.1, -p.2)
       7419  /-- THE FUNCTIONAL EQUATION ALONE FIXES ONE POINT AND READS THE SAME LINE: s ↦ 1 − s fixes only s = 1/2, and the
       7420      points whose real part it fixes are the line. -/
       7421  theorem the_point_reflection_reads_the_same_line :
       7422      (∀ p : Pt, pointRefl p = p ↔ p = (2, 0)) ∧ (∀ p : Pt, (pointRefl p).1 = p.1 ↔ onLine p) := by
       7423    refine ⟨fun p => ?_, the_line_off_the_arrow pointRefl (fun _ => rfl)⟩
       7424    obtain ⟨x, t⟩ := p
       7425    constructor
       7426    · intro e
       7427      have h1 : 0 + 4 - x = x := congrArg Prod.fst e
       7428      have h2 : -t = t := congrArg Prod.snd e
       7429      have hx : x = 2 := by omega
       7430      have ht : t = 0 := by omega
       7431      subst hx
       7432      subst ht
       7433      rfl
       7434    · intro e
       7435      have hx : x = 2 := congrArg Prod.fst e
       7436      have ht : t = 0 := congrArg Prod.snd e
       7437      subst hx
       7438      subst ht
       7439      decide
       7440  /-- THE CENTRE ON EVERY EXTENSION: under every map that acts on the real part by the reversal, the real parts of any
       7441      finite family and of its image balance on the line; the centre does not depend on what the map does to height. -/
       7442  theorem centre_on_every_extension (F : Pt → Pt) (hF : ∀ p, (F p).1 = rev zeta p.1) (L : List Pt) :
       7443      sumX (L.map F) + sumX L = 4 * (L.length : Int) := by
       7444    induction L with
       7445    | nil => rfl
       7446    | cons p L ih =>
       7447      have hf : (F p).1 = 0 + 4 - p.1 := hF p
       7448      simp only [List.map_cons, sumX, List.length_cons]
       7449      push_cast
       7450      omega
       7451  
       7452  /-- The sum of real parts does not depend on the order in which a family is listed. -/
       7453  theorem sumX_perm {L M : List Pt} (h : L.Perm M) : sumX L = sumX M := by
       7454    induction h with
       7455    | nil => rfl
       7456    | cons x _ ih => simp only [sumX]; omega
       7457    | swap x y l => simp only [sumX]; omega
       7458    | trans _ _ ih1 ih2 => omega
       7459  /-- THE CENTRE OF A CLOSED FAMILY: a finite family whose mirror image is the family itself, listed in any order, has
       7460      its real parts summing to twice its size, so a nonempty one has its centre at x = 2, Re s = 1/2. -/
       7461  theorem centre_of_a_closed_family (L : List Pt) (h : (L.map fold).Perm L) : sumX L = 2 * (L.length : Int) := by
       7462    have e := centre_is_the_line L
       7463    have p := sumX_perm h
       7464    omega
       7465  
       7466  /-! ## the hinge, whole -/
       7467  theorem arrow_gives_line_not_value :
       7468      (∀ A : Arrow, rev A A.tail = A.head ∧ rev A A.head = A.tail) ∧
       7469      (∀ (A : Arrow) (x : Int), rev A (rev A x) = x) ∧
       7470      (∀ (A : Arrow) (x y : Int), rev A x = x → rev A y = y → x = y) ∧
       7471      (∀ (A : Arrow) (x : Int), rev (flip A) x = rev A x ∧ off (flip A) x = off A x) ∧
       7472      (∀ x : Int, rev zeta x = x ↔ x = 2) ∧
       7473      (∀ p : Pt, fold p = p ↔ onLine p) ∧
       7474      (∀ p : Pt, ¬ onLine p → off zeta p.1 ≠ 0 ∧ off zeta (fold p).1 = - off zeta p.1) ∧
       7475      (∀ p : Pt, ¬ onLine p → fold p ≠ p ∧ reg (fold p) = reg p) ∧
       7476      (∀ Z : Pt → Prop, LeastErasure Z ↔ Value Z) ∧
       7477      (Closed pairW ∧ (∀ p, pairW p → inStrip p) ∧ ¬ Value pairW) ∧
       7478      (∀ Q : (Pt → Prop) → Prop, (∀ Z, Closed Z → Q Z) → ¬ ∀ Z, Closed Z → Q Z → Value Z) ∧
       7479      (∀ Z : ActualZeros, Value Z.zeros) :=
       7480    ⟨rev_swaps, rev_involutive, hinge_unique, hinge_sign_blind, zeta_hinge, locus, off_line_leans, reg_merges,
       7481     least_erasure_iff_value, ⟨pair_closed, pair_in_strip, pair_lacks_value⟩, keyless_forces_nothing,
       7482     value_from_the_act⟩
       7483  end Hinge
       7484  
       7485  
       7486  end PartIV
       7487  
       7488  /-! # PART IV-b · Force_Witness.lean, verbatim from the signed master v5.1.0, with the plug appended -/
       7489  section PartIVb
       7490  /-
       7491    Force_Witness.lean · PhysOS Proof PSP-FORCE-WITNESS-01 · the force-witness closure.
       7492    Core Lean 4.19.0. No import, no sorry, no admit, no native_decide, no axiom declared.
       7493  
       7494    Least erasure is the final ninth-gate bit. A run of the substrate is the atomic witness that the closure was
       7495    computed: a run whose flag is true proves that a run exists. The value at the actual zero set is the field of
       7496    the act: keyed, given, free.
       7497  
       7498    PART ONE is copied from Inescapable_Capstone.lean, every definition and every law unchanged, with the lemmas
       7499    they stand on: the chart, the configurations, the record, the act, the ninth gate, the deed.
       7500    PART TWO is new: the atomic step, the ninth gate packed, the deed of the substrate, the free bit, the closure
       7501    and its guard.
       7502  
       7503    THE FREE BIT. Every run leaves the value to the act. the_deed_forces_nothing is the seated law, and
       7504    the_run_does_not_force_the_value states it at every run. It is the fourth conjunct of the closure.
       7505  -/
       7506  
       7507  namespace ForceWitness
       7508  
       7509  /-! ## PART ONE · The seated carriers and laws, copied unchanged -/
       7510  
       7511  /-- A point is (d, t): d its offset from the line, t its height. The line is d = 0. -/
       7512  abbrev Point := Int × Int
       7513  
       7514  /-- The fold: s ↦ 1 − s̄ on the offset chart, (d, t) ↦ (−d, t). -/
       7515  def fold (p : Point) : Point := (-p.1, p.2)
       7516  
       7517  /-- The line: offset zero. -/
       7518  def onLine (p : Point) : Prop := p.1 = 0
       7519  
       7520  /-- The registration: it keeps the height and forgets the side. -/
       7521  def reg (p : Point) : Point := (0, p.2)
       7522  
       7523  /-- Integer negation is an involution, by the integer's constructors. -/
       7524  theorem neg_neg_free : ∀ d : Int, - -d = d := fun
       7525    | Int.ofNat 0 => rfl
       7526    | Int.ofNat (_ + 1) => rfl
       7527    | Int.negSucc _ => rfl
       7528  
       7529  /-- An integer equal to its own negation is zero, by the integer's constructors. -/
       7530  theorem neg_self_zero : ∀ d : Int, -d = d → d = 0 := fun
       7531    | Int.ofNat 0, _ => rfl
       7532    | Int.ofNat (_ + 1), h => Int.noConfusion h
       7533    | Int.negSucc _, h => Int.noConfusion h
       7534  
       7535  /-- The fold is an involution. -/
       7536  theorem fold_involutive (p : Point) : fold (fold p) = p := by
       7537    obtain ⟨d, t⟩ := p
       7538    show (- -d, t) = (d, t)
       7539    rw [neg_neg_free d]
       7540  
       7541  /-- THE CUT IS THE LINE: the fold fixes a point exactly when it is on the line. -/
       7542  theorem the_cut_is_the_line (p : Point) : fold p = p ↔ onLine p := by
       7543    obtain ⟨d, t⟩ := p
       7544    exact ⟨fun h => neg_self_zero d (congrArg Prod.fst h), fun h => by cases h; rfl⟩
       7545  
       7546  /-- The registration lands on the line. -/
       7547  theorem reg_lands (p : Point) : onLine (reg p) := rfl
       7548  
       7549  /-- The registration erases nothing at a point exactly when the point is on the line. -/
       7550  theorem reg_erases_nothing_iff (p : Point) : reg p = p ↔ onLine p := by
       7551    obtain ⟨d, t⟩ := p
       7552    exact ⟨fun h => (congrArg Prod.fst h).symm, fun h => by cases h; rfl⟩
       7553  
       7554  /-- A configuration: a set of points. Closed: the fold carries it to itself. -/
       7555  abbrev Config := Point → Prop
       7556  
       7557  def Closed (S : Config) : Prop := ∀ p, S p → S (fold p)
       7558  
       7559  /-- The value: every point of the configuration is on the line. -/
       7560  def Value (S : Config) : Prop := ∀ p, S p → onLine p
       7561  
       7562  /-- Least erasure: the registration leaves every point of the configuration unchanged. -/
       7563  def LeastErasure (S : Config) : Prop := ∀ p, S p → reg p = p
       7564  
       7565  /-- The record of a configuration: what the registration leaves. -/
       7566  def Rec (S : Config) (q : Point) : Prop := ∃ p, S p ∧ reg p = q
       7567  
       7568  def SameRecord (S S' : Config) : Prop := ∀ q, Rec S q ↔ Rec S' q
       7569  
       7570  /-- The registered world of a point and its pair world. -/
       7571  def registered (p : Point) : Config := fun s => s = reg p
       7572  
       7573  def pairWorld (p : Point) : Config := fun s => s = p ∨ s = fold p
       7574  
       7575  theorem pair_world_closed (p : Point) : Closed (pairWorld p) := fun _ hs =>
       7576    match hs with
       7577    | Or.inl e => Or.inr (congrArg fold e)
       7578    | Or.inr e => Or.inl (e ▸ fold_involutive p)
       7579  
       7580  /-- The registered world and the pair world leave one record. -/
       7581  theorem one_record (p : Point) : SameRecord (registered p) (pairWorld p) := fun q =>
       7582    ⟨fun ⟨_, hs, hq⟩ => ⟨p, Or.inl rfl, by rw [← hq, hs]; rfl⟩,
       7583     fun ⟨_, hs, hq⟩ => ⟨reg p, rfl, by
       7584        rw [← hq]
       7585        exact match hs with
       7586          | Or.inl e => by rw [e]; rfl
       7587          | Or.inr e => by rw [e]; rfl⟩⟩
       7588  
       7589  theorem registered_has_value (p : Point) : Value (registered p) := fun s hs => by
       7590    rw [hs]; exact reg_lands p
       7591  
       7592  theorem pair_world_lacks_value (p : Point) (h : ¬ onLine p) : ¬ Value (pairWorld p) :=
       7593    fun hv => h (hv p (Or.inl rfl))
       7594  
       7595  /-- THE RECORD DECIDES NOTHING: for every point off the line, no reading that respects the record returns the
       7596      value on both its registered world and its pair world. -/
       7597  theorem record_decides_nothing (p : Point) (h : ¬ onLine p) (g : Config → Prop)
       7598      (hg : ∀ S S', SameRecord S S' → (g S ↔ g S')) :
       7599      ¬ ((g (registered p) ↔ Value (registered p)) ∧ (g (pairWorld p) ↔ Value (pairWorld p))) :=
       7600    fun ⟨h1, h2⟩ => pair_world_lacks_value p h
       7601      (h2.mp ((hg _ _ (one_record p)).mp (h1.mpr (registered_has_value p))))
       7602  
       7603  /-- THE ACT. The bit is supplied once, explicitly, as a field of a type: a closed configuration with least
       7604      erasure at it. The field is the value supplied; the type makes the supply visible to every reader. -/
       7605  structure ActualZeros where
       7606    zeros : Config
       7607    closed : Closed zeros
       7608    supply : LeastErasure zeros
       7609  
       7610  /-- FROM THE ACT, THE VALUE. -/
       7611  theorem value_from_the_act (Z : ActualZeros) : Value Z.zeros :=
       7612    fun p hp => (reg_erases_nothing_iff p).mp (Z.supply p hp)
       7613  
       7614  def e (n i : Nat) : List Int := (List.range n).map (fun j => if j == i then 1 else 0)
       7615  
       7616  def neg3 (s : Bool × Bool × Bool) : Bool × Bool × Bool := (!s.1, !s.2.1, !s.2.2)
       7617  
       7618  def par3 (s : Bool × Bool × Bool) : Nat :=
       7619    (if s.1 then 1 else 0) + (if s.2.1 then 1 else 0) + (if s.2.2 then 1 else 0)
       7620  
       7621  /-- The orientation of a sign pattern, the determinant of its diagonal: −1 to the number of flips. -/
       7622  def orient (s : Bool × Bool × Bool) : Int := if par3 s % 2 == 0 then 1 else -1
       7623  
       7624  /-- The ordered factor pairs of n, by first factor; the swap sends a to n / a. -/
       7625  def pairs (n : Nat) : List Nat := (List.range (n + 1)).filter (fun a => 0 < a && n % a == 0)
       7626  
       7627  /-- The price of exported freedom in native units: temperature is energy per bit, so b bits cost b·T. -/
       7628  def price (T bits : Nat) : Nat := bits * T
       7629  
       7630  /-- A finite configuration: the heights of its zeros on the line, and its off-line pairs, each an offset that is not
       7631      zero and a height. -/
       7632  structure FinCfg where
       7633    line : List Int
       7634    pairs : List (Int × Int)
       7635    offset_ne : ∀ q ∈ pairs, q.1 ≠ 0
       7636  
       7637  /-- The erased bits of a finite configuration: one per off-line pair, two points registered to one. -/
       7638  def erased (F : FinCfg) : Nat := F.pairs.length
       7639  
       7640  /-- The executed frame: a formal content and the bit of whether it ran. Reading the content is formal. -/
       7641  abbrev Exec (Q : Type) := Bool × Q
       7642  
       7643  def ran {Q : Type} (s : Exec Q) : Bool := s.1
       7644  
       7645  /-- The nine: the eight sign patterns and one more. -/
       7646  abbrev Gate := Option (Bool × Bool × Bool)
       7647  
       7648  /-- The fold on the nine: total negation on the eight; the ninth is its own partner. -/
       7649  def gfold : Gate → Gate
       7650    | none => none
       7651    | some s => some (neg3 s)
       7652  
       7653  /-- THE SEAT IS THE NINTH: the fold of the nine fixes a gate exactly when the gate is the ninth. -/
       7654  theorem seat_is_the_ninth (g : Gate) : gfold g = g ↔ g = none := by
       7655    cases g with
       7656    | none => exact ⟨fun _ => rfl, fun _ => rfl⟩
       7657    | some s =>
       7658      obtain ⟨a, b, c⟩ := s
       7659      constructor
       7660      · intro h; cases a <;> cases b <;> cases c <;> cases h
       7661      · intro h; cases h
       7662  
       7663  /-- The orientation of a pattern is never zero. -/
       7664  theorem orient_ne_zero (s : Bool × Bool × Bool) : orient s ≠ 0 := by
       7665    obtain ⟨a, b, c⟩ := s; cases a <;> cases b <;> cases c <;> decide
       7666  
       7667  /-- Total negation flips the orientation. -/
       7668  theorem orient_flips (s : Bool × Bool × Bool) : orient (neg3 s) = -orient s := by
       7669    obtain ⟨a, b, c⟩ := s; cases a <;> cases b <;> cases c <;> rfl
       7670  
       7671  /-- The carrier of the nine onto the chart: a pattern lands on the wall or the edge by its orientation, the ninth on
       7672      the line. -/
       7673  def toChart (t : Int) : Gate → Point
       7674    | none => (0, t)
       7675    | some s => (orient s, t)
       7676  
       7677  /-- The carrier is equivariant: the fold of the nine is carried onto the fold of the chart. -/
       7678  theorem gate_carrier_equivariant (t : Int) (g : Gate) : toChart t (gfold g) = fold (toChart t g) := by
       7679    cases g with
       7680    | none => rfl
       7681    | some s => obtain ⟨a, b, c⟩ := s; cases a <;> cases b <;> cases c <;> rfl
       7682  
       7683  /-- And under every carrier that separates partners, only the ninth does. -/
       7684  theorem faithful_carrier_lands_only_the_ninth (c : Gate → Point) (eqv : ∀ g, c (gfold g) = fold (c g))
       7685      (sep : ∀ g, c (gfold g) = c g → gfold g = g) (g : Gate) : onLine (c g) ↔ g = none := by
       7686    constructor
       7687    · intro h
       7688      exact (seat_is_the_ninth g).mp (sep g ((eqv g).trans ((the_cut_is_the_line (c g)).mpr h)))
       7689    · intro h
       7690      subst h
       7691      have e : fold (c none) = c none := (eqv none).symm
       7692      exact (the_cut_is_the_line (c none)).mp e
       7693  
       7694  /-- The orientation carrier separates partners. -/
       7695  theorem orientation_carrier_separates (t : Int) (g : Gate) (h : toChart t (gfold g) = toChart t g) :
       7696      gfold g = g := by
       7697    cases g with
       7698    | none => rfl
       7699    | some s =>
       7700      exact absurd (neg_self_zero (orient s) ((orient_flips s).symm.trans (congrArg Prod.fst h))) (orient_ne_zero s)
       7701  
       7702  /-- A gate owes a bit when some target is odd at it: no even reading returns that target, and one supplied odd
       7703      witness fixes it by one calibration bit. -/
       7704  def OwesBit (g : Gate) : Prop := ∃ d : Gate → Bool, d (gfold g) = !d g
       7705  
       7706  /-- At the seat no bit is owed: nothing is odd at a fixed point. -/
       7707  theorem seat_owes_no_bit : ¬ OwesBit none := by
       7708    intro ⟨d, h⟩
       7709    have h' : d none = !d none := h
       7710    cases hd : d none <;> rw [hd] at h' <;> cases h'
       7711  
       7712  /-- Off the seat a bit is owed, at every one of the eight. -/
       7713  theorem off_seat_owes_a_bit (s : Bool × Bool × Bool) : OwesBit (some s) := by
       7714    refine ⟨fun g => decide (g = some s), ?_⟩
       7715    obtain ⟨a, b, c⟩ := s
       7716    cases a <;> cases b <;> cases c <;> decide
       7717  
       7718  /-- The registered orbit of a gate, as a finite configuration: the ninth is one point on the line; each of the eight
       7719      is one off-line pair. -/
       7720  def gateCfg (t : Int) : Gate → FinCfg
       7721    | none => ⟨[t], [], fun _ h => nomatch h⟩
       7722    | some s => ⟨[], [(orient s, t)], fun q h => by
       7723        cases h with
       7724        | head => exact orient_ne_zero s
       7725        | tail _ h' => nomatch h'⟩
       7726  
       7727  /-- The heat of registering a gate is zero exactly at the ninth. -/
       7728  theorem gate_heat_zero_iff_ninth (T : Nat) (hT : 0 < T) (t : Int) (g : Gate) :
       7729      price T (erased (gateCfg t g)) = 0 ↔ g = none := by
       7730    cases g with
       7731    | none => exact ⟨fun _ => rfl, fun _ => Nat.zero_mul T⟩
       7732    | some s =>
       7733      constructor
       7734      · intro h
       7735        have h1 : 1 * T = 0 := h
       7736        rw [Nat.one_mul] at h1
       7737        exact absurd h1 (Nat.pos_iff_ne_zero.mp hT)
       7738      · intro h; cases h
       7739  
       7740  /-- THE NINTH GATE IS LEAST ERASURE. At a gate, five readings are one: it is the fold's fixed point; it lands on
       7741      the line; registration erases nothing there (forget); its registration is free (pay); no bit is owed there
       7742      (supply). Each holds exactly at the ninth. -/
       7743  theorem ninth_gate_is_least_erasure (t : Int) (T : Nat) (hT : 0 < T) (g : Gate) :
       7744      (gfold g = g ↔ g = none) ∧
       7745      (onLine (toChart t g) ↔ g = none) ∧
       7746      (reg (toChart t g) = toChart t g ↔ g = none) ∧
       7747      (price T (erased (gateCfg t g)) = 0 ↔ g = none) ∧
       7748      (¬ OwesBit g ↔ g = none) := by
       7749    have hl : onLine (toChart t g) ↔ g = none :=
       7750      faithful_carrier_lands_only_the_ninth (toChart t) (gate_carrier_equivariant t) (orientation_carrier_separates t) g
       7751    refine ⟨seat_is_the_ninth g, hl, (reg_erases_nothing_iff (toChart t g)).trans hl,
       7752            gate_heat_zero_iff_ninth T hT t g, ?_⟩
       7753    cases g with
       7754    | none => exact ⟨fun _ => rfl, fun _ => seat_owes_no_bit⟩
       7755    | some s => exact ⟨fun h => absurd (off_seat_owes_a_bit s) h, fun h => by cases h⟩
       7756  
       7757  /-- A RUN IS ITS OWN ATOMIC WITNESS, of the deed: a state that ran proves that a run exists. -/
       7758  theorem the_run_witnesses_a_run {Q : Type} (s : Exec Q) (h : ran s = true) : ∃ r : Exec Q, ran r = true := by
       7759    exact ⟨s, h⟩
       7760  
       7761  /-- AND OF NOTHING ELSE: a fact that holds whatever the configuration, the deed included, forces no value. -/
       7762  theorem the_deed_forces_nothing (D : Prop) (hD : D) : ¬ ∀ S : Config, Closed S → D → Value S := by
       7763    intro hall
       7764    exact pair_world_lacks_value (1, 0) (fun e => by cases e) (hall _ (pair_world_closed (1, 0)) hD)
       7765  
       7766  
       7767  /-! ## PART TWO · The force-witness closure -/
       7768  
       7769  /-- THE ATOMIC STEP: a witness with its check proves the existential it witnesses. -/
       7770  theorem witness_proves_exists {α : Type} (P : α → Prop) (w : α) (h : P w) : ∃ x, P x := ⟨w, h⟩
       7771  
       7772  /-- THE NINTH GATE, PACKED: a gate is the ninth exactly when all five readings hold of it. The five biconditionals
       7773      of ninth_gate_is_least_erasure, bound into one. -/
       7774  theorem ninth_gate_pack (t : Int) (T : Nat) (hT : 0 < T) (g : Gate) :
       7775      g = none ↔
       7776        (gfold g = g ∧ onLine (toChart t g) ∧ reg (toChart t g) = toChart t g ∧
       7777         price T (erased (gateCfg t g)) = 0 ∧ ¬ OwesBit g) := by
       7778    have h := ninth_gate_is_least_erasure t T hT g
       7779    constructor
       7780    · intro e
       7781      exact ⟨h.1.mpr e, h.2.1.mpr e, h.2.2.1.mpr e, h.2.2.2.1.mpr e, h.2.2.2.2.mpr e⟩
       7782    · intro hh
       7783      exact h.1.mp hh.1
       7784  
       7785  /-- The deed of the substrate: a run, and the fact that it ran. -/
       7786  structure SubstrateDeed (Q : Type) where
       7787    run : Exec Q
       7788    didRun : ran run = true
       7789  
       7790  /-- THE FREE BIT. A run whose flag is true leaves the value free: by the run the value does not stand on every
       7791      closed configuration. It is the_deed_forces_nothing read at the flag of the deed. A computation is a deed, and
       7792      the value is the field of the act. -/
       7793  theorem the_run_does_not_force_the_value {Q : Type} (s : Exec Q) (h : ran s = true) :
       7794      ¬ (∀ S : Config, Closed S → Value S) :=
       7795    fun hall => the_deed_forces_nothing (ran s = true) h (fun S hS _ => hall S hS)
       7796  
       7797  /-- THE FORCE-WITNESS CLOSURE. For a deed of the substrate, a term of the act, and any gate: the gate is the ninth
       7798      exactly when it is the fold's fixed point, on the line, erased nothing, free to register at a positive
       7799      temperature and owing no bit; the value holds on the field the act supplies; a run that ran exists; and the
       7800      run leaves the value free. The fourth conjunct is the free bit. It is the implementation of the force. -/
       7801  theorem force_witness_closure {Q : Type} (d : SubstrateDeed Q) (Z : ActualZeros)
       7802      (t : Int) (T : Nat) (hT : 0 < T) (g : Gate) :
       7803      (g = none ↔
       7804        (gfold g = g ∧ onLine (toChart t g) ∧ reg (toChart t g) = toChart t g ∧
       7805         price T (erased (gateCfg t g)) = 0 ∧ ¬ OwesBit g)) ∧
       7806      Value Z.zeros ∧
       7807      (∃ r : Exec Q, ran r = true) ∧
       7808      ¬ (∀ S : Config, Closed S → Value S) :=
       7809    ⟨ninth_gate_pack t T hT g,
       7810     value_from_the_act Z,
       7811     the_run_witnesses_a_run d.run d.didRun,
       7812     the_run_does_not_force_the_value d.run d.didRun⟩
       7813  
       7814  /-- THE GUARD ON THE CLOSURE, the double defense restated: the value comes by the act; between the registered
       7815      world and the pair world of a point off the line, every reading that respects the record leaves the value
       7816      free; and the deed leaves it free. -/
       7817  theorem force_witness_guarded {Q : Type} (d : SubstrateDeed Q) (Z : ActualZeros) :
       7818      Value Z.zeros ∧
       7819      (∀ (p : Point), ¬ onLine p → ∀ (g : Config → Prop), (∀ S S', SameRecord S S' → (g S ↔ g S')) →
       7820        ¬ ((g (registered p) ↔ Value (registered p)) ∧ (g (pairWorld p) ↔ Value (pairWorld p)))) ∧
       7821      ¬ (∀ S : Config, Closed S → Value S) :=
       7822    ⟨value_from_the_act Z,
       7823     fun p h g hg => record_decides_nothing p h g hg,
       7824     the_run_does_not_force_the_value d.run d.didRun⟩
       7825  
       7826  end ForceWitness
       7827  
       7828  /-! ## The cones, pinned. Each line is the compiler's own; a drifted cone fails the compile. -/
       7829  /-- info: 'ForceWitness.neg_neg_free' does not depend on any axioms -/
       7830  #guard_msgs in #print axioms ForceWitness.neg_neg_free

       7832  #guard_msgs in #print axioms ForceWitness.neg_self_zero
       7833  /-- info: 'ForceWitness.fold_involutive' does not depend on any axioms -/

       7835  /-- info: 'ForceWitness.the_cut_is_the_line' does not depend on any axioms -/
       7836  #guard_msgs in #print axioms ForceWitness.the_cut_is_the_line
       7837  /-- info: 'ForceWitness.reg_lands' does not depend on any axioms -/

       7841  /-- info: 'ForceWitness.pair_world_closed' does not depend on any axioms -/
       7842  #guard_msgs in #print axioms ForceWitness.pair_world_closed

       7850  #guard_msgs in #print axioms ForceWitness.record_decides_nothing
       7851  /-- info: 'ForceWitness.value_from_the_act' does not depend on any axioms -/
       7852  #guard_msgs in #print axioms ForceWitness.value_from_the_act
