       9131  /-! # PART VII · THE HARDENING · the identification, the bridge, the bound and the capstone, every input printed
       9132  
       9133    OPTIONAL CORROBORATION, NOT REQUIRED FOR THE FORMAL LOOP. The five-way fixed-point
       9134    loop (Part X § X-d) stands on Parts I and X; the master closure (Part XI) stands on
       9135    Parts I to III, the apparatus cargo of Part VIII-b, and Parts IX and X. Part VII's
       9136    hardening and Part VIII's physico-formal carrier are corroborating developments; the
       9137    formal loop does not depend on them.
       9138  
       9139    Added 11 October 2026 for edition 2.0.3 of The Atomic Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, on the Final Scribal
       9140    Recommendation of the audit of 10 October 2026. Nothing above this line changed: Parts I to VI are byte-identical
       9141    to RH_Both_Sides_Seed.lean of 8 October 2026 (sha256 cb719eab915a9973…). Core Lean 4.19.0, no import, no axiom
       9142    declared, no sorry, no admit, no native_decide.
       9143  
       9144    What this part does, and in this order:
       9145    VII-a  carries the kernel of the companion paper, Least Erasure from Degrees of Freedom and Heat, repaired to
       9146           compile in core Lean (the shipped v2.0.1 kernel used the Mathlib tactic by_contra and left one conjunction
       9147           unsolved, so its master seal depended on sorryAx under Lean 4.19.0), with the quantitative companion
       9148           density_bound_from_residual_bound added and the master seal extended to seven claims;
       9149    VII-b  states the identification exactly: on the chart, least erasure of a configuration IS its value, for every
       9150           configuration, by theorem; so the one thing to be granted is the reading, that the classical hypothesis is
       9151           the value of the configuration at which the zeros of ζ are read (Section 11 of the paper). The field
       9152           `supply` of `ActualZeros` is shown to be the premise packaged, by its type;
       9153    VII-c  writes the bridge as six named arrows composed by theorem, the rate and the heat feeding the signal, and
       9154           proves the uniform threshold δ = n₀·r₀·q₀ independent of which carrier and which zero;
       9155    VII-d  keeps the heat theorem at its exact strength: the exact-null case and the finite-sensitivity case apart;
       9156    VII-e  THE CAPSTONE, classical_rh_from_identification_gap_and_bound, with its five inputs printed, and its
       9157           exploded form with the nine inputs of the Recommendation; the exact-null route beside it with ITS premise
       9158           printed; and no_third_position: given the identification, the bound and the gap, the denial of the
       9159           hypothesis and the bridge cannot both stand;
       9160    VII-f  what the capstone does not do, by theorem: the reading and the bridge are keyed, each fails on a closed
       9161           configuration of the interface, so neither is a theorem of the seed and each is a premise, named;
       9162    VII-g  the hardened closure, binding the two-sided closure and the capstones by their exact types, and the cones.
       9163  
       9164    The reading of the empty cone: `#print axioms` names the axioms a proof depends on. It says nothing about the
       9165    hypotheses in the signature. Every hypothesis of the capstone is an input the reader grants or refuses by name.
       9166  
       9167    NOTE: in the flipped formal register, the observational bridge parameters of this part
       9168    (the six arrows, the bound, the capstone inputs) are SUPERSEDED in the core arch by the formalized
       9169    compute cargo — `ApparatusCargo` (seed Part VIII-b), `BoundChain` (Part IX), `BoundChainMathlib` (Part X).
       9170    They remain in this file, untouched, as fenced conditional theorems (optional retrospective corroboration),
       9171    matching the status of `ApparatusCargo.stage2_optional_corroboration`. -/
       9172  section PartVII
       9173  set_option autoImplicit false
       9174  
       9175  /-! ## VII-a · the least-erasure kernel of the companion paper, repaired, with the quantitative companion -/
       9176  namespace LeastErasureDoF
       9177  
       9178  def ln2_scaled : Nat := 693147
       9179  def scale : Nat := 1000000
       9180  def cmb_mK : Nat := 2725
       9181  
       9182  /-- A system relative to a record: macro states distinguished, binary labels free, micro states in total. -/
       9183  structure System where
       9184    distinct : Nat
       9185    free : Nat
       9186    total : Nat
       9187    inv : total = distinct * Nat.pow 2 free
       9188  
       9189  /-- A recoding that halves the record and frees one label, total preserved. -/
       9190  structure DiscardProcess where
       9191    before : System
       9192    after : System
       9193    h_distinct : before.distinct = 2 * after.distinct
       9194    h_free : after.free = before.free + 1
       9195    h_total : before.total = after.total
       9196    h_gt : before.distinct > after.distinct
       9197  
       9198  /-- An erasure: the record kept, one free label lost, the total halved. -/
       9199  structure EraseProcess where
       9200    before : System
       9201    after : System
       9202    h_distinct : before.distinct = after.distinct
       9203    h_free : before.free = after.free + 1
       9204    h_total : before.total = 2 * after.total
       9205    h_gt : before.total > after.total
       9206  
       9207  /-- A discard halves the record and frees one label. Repaired: the shipped proof did not discharge this conjunction. -/
       9208  theorem discard_is_free (p : DiscardProcess) :
       9209      p.after.distinct * 2 = p.before.distinct ∧
       9210      p.after.free = p.before.free + 1 :=
       9211    ⟨(Nat.mul_comm _ _).trans p.h_distinct.symm, p.h_free⟩
       9212  
       9213  def sysEntropy (s : System) : Nat := s.free * ln2_scaled
       9214  
       9215  theorem sysEntropy_decrease (p : EraseProcess) :
       9216      sysEntropy p.after + ln2_scaled = sysEntropy p.before := by
       9217    unfold sysEntropy
       9218    rw [p.h_free, Nat.succ_mul]
       9219  
       9220  /-- The lower bound is witnessed by the choice heat = T · ln2_scaled. The process is not consulted: the kernel
       9221      records that a number meeting the bound exists, nothing more. The physical necessity, joint conservation of
       9222      probability with the second law, is carried in the prose of the companion paper at its own grade. -/
       9223  theorem heat_from_joint_conservation (_p : EraseProcess) (T : Nat) :
       9224      ∃ heat : Nat, heat ≥ T * ln2_scaled :=
       9225    ⟨T * ln2_scaled, Nat.le_refl _⟩
       9226  
       9227  theorem heat_positive (_p : EraseProcess) (T : Nat) (hT : T > 0) :
       9228      ∃ heat : Nat, heat > 0 ∧ heat ≥ T * ln2_scaled :=
       9229    ⟨T * ln2_scaled, Nat.mul_pos hT (by decide), Nat.le_refl _⟩
       9230  
       9231  theorem landauer_special_case (p : EraseProcess) (_h : p.before.free = 1) :
       9232      ∃ heat : Nat, heat ≥ cmb_mK * ln2_scaled :=
       9233    heat_from_joint_conservation p cmb_mK
       9234  
       9235  /-- The residual observable of the counting model: population × rate × heat per event. -/
       9236  def residual (density rate heat : Nat) : Nat := density * rate * heat
       9237  
       9238  theorem residual_pos {density rate heat : Nat}
       9239      (hd : density > 0) (hr : rate > 0) (hh : heat > 0) :
       9240      residual density rate heat > 0 := by
       9241    unfold residual
       9242    have h1 : density * rate > 0 := Nat.mul_pos hd hr
       9243    exact Nat.mul_pos h1 hh
       9244  
       9245  /-- THE EXACT-NULL CASE. Residual exactly zero, rate and heat positive: the population is zero. Repaired: the
       9246      shipped proof used by_contra, a Mathlib tactic, and so did not compile in core Lean. -/
       9247  theorem null_forces_zero {density rate heat : Nat}
       9248      (hr : rate > 0) (hh : heat > 0) (h0 : residual density rate heat = 0) :
       9249      density = 0 := by
       9250    cases density with
       9251    | zero => rfl
       9252    | succ d =>
       9253      have hpos := residual_pos (Nat.succ_pos d) hr hh
       9254      rw [h0] at hpos
       9255      exact absurd hpos (Nat.lt_irrefl 0)
       9256  
       9257  /-- THE FINITE-SENSITIVITY CASE, the quantitative companion. Residual at most ε, rate at least r₀, heat at
       9258      least q₀: the population times the two floors, ρ · r₀ · q₀, is at most ε. This is what a null result at finite sensitivity
       9259      supports. It is not density = 0, and the paper never rewrites it as density = 0. Stated multiplicatively so
       9260      that no integer division rounds anything: the bound is exact in the kernel's units. -/
       9261  theorem density_bound_from_residual_bound {density rate heat r0 q0 ε : Nat}
       9262      (hR : residual density rate heat ≤ ε) (hr : rate ≥ r0) (hq : heat ≥ q0) :
       9263      density * r0 * q0 ≤ ε :=
       9264    Nat.le_trans (Nat.mul_le_mul (Nat.mul_le_mul_left density hr) hq) hR
       9265  
       9266  /-- The same bound read as a quotient, density ≤ ε / (r₀ q₀), for positive floors. Integer division floors, so
       9267      this form is weaker than the multiplicative one; it is the form the Recommendation names. Its cone carries
       9268      propext through the core lemma on division, and is pinned below as such. -/
       9269  theorem density_le_div {density rate heat r0 q0 ε : Nat}
       9270      (hR : residual density rate heat ≤ ε) (hr : rate ≥ r0) (hq : heat ≥ q0)
       9271      (hr0 : r0 > 0) (hq0 : q0 > 0) :
       9272      density ≤ ε / (r0 * q0) :=
       9273    (Nat.le_div_iff_mul_le (Nat.mul_pos hr0 hq0)).mpr
       9274      (Nat.mul_assoc density r0 q0 ▸ density_bound_from_residual_bound hR hr hq)
       9275  
       9276  def Discards (p : EraseProcess) (label : Nat) : Prop :=
       9277    label < p.before.distinct ∧ p.before.distinct > 0
       9278  
       9279  def NullForcesZeroOn (label : Nat) : Prop :=
       9280    ∃ p : EraseProcess, Discards p label ∧ residual 1 1 ln2_scaled > 0
       9281  
       9282  theorem boundary_holds :
       9283      ∀ (label : Nat), ¬ (∃ p : EraseProcess, Discards p label) →
       9284        ¬ NullForcesZeroOn label := by
       9285    intro label hNo hYes
       9286    unfold NullForcesZeroOn at hYes
       9287    obtain ⟨p, hp, _⟩ := hYes
       9288    exact hNo ⟨p, hp⟩
       9289  
       9290  /-- The Noether skeleton. Both predicates are True: the kernel keeps only the shape of the statement, a
       9291      symmetry yields a conserved current, and proves nothing about any dynamics. Stated so, not otherwise. -/
       9292  def ContinuousSymmetry (_ξ : Nat) : Prop := True
       9293  def Conserved (_curr : Nat) : Prop := True
       9294  
       9295  theorem noether_current :
       9296      ∀ (ξ : Nat), ContinuousSymmetry ξ →
       9297        ∃ curr : Nat, Conserved curr :=
       9298    fun _ _ => ⟨0, trivial⟩
       9299  
       9300  /-- THE MASTER SEAL, seven claims: the six of the companion paper and the quantitative companion. -/
       9301  theorem the_master_seal :
       9302      (∀ p : DiscardProcess, p.after.distinct * 2 = p.before.distinct ∧ p.after.free = p.before.free + 1) ∧
       9303      (∀ _p : EraseProcess, ∀ T : Nat, ∃ heat : Nat, heat ≥ T * ln2_scaled) ∧
       9304      (∀ p : EraseProcess, p.before.free = 1 → ∃ heat : Nat, heat ≥ cmb_mK * ln2_scaled) ∧
       9305      (∀ density rate heat : Nat, density > 0 → rate > 0 → heat > 0 → residual density rate heat > 0) ∧
       9306      (∀ label : Nat, ¬ (∃ p : EraseProcess, Discards p label) → ¬ NullForcesZeroOn label) ∧
       9307      (∀ ξ : Nat, ContinuousSymmetry ξ → ∃ curr : Nat, Conserved curr) ∧
       9308      (∀ density rate heat r0 q0 ε : Nat, residual density rate heat ≤ ε → rate ≥ r0 → heat ≥ q0 →
       9309        density * r0 * q0 ≤ ε) := by
       9310    refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
       9311    · exact fun p => discard_is_free p
       9312    · exact fun p T => heat_from_joint_conservation p T
       9313    · exact fun p h => landauer_special_case p h
       9314    · exact fun _ _ _ hd hr hh => residual_pos hd hr hh
       9315    · exact fun label => boundary_holds label
       9316    · exact fun ξ h => noether_current ξ h
       9317    · exact fun _ _ _ _ _ _ hR hr hq => density_bound_from_residual_bound hR hr hq
       9318  
       9319  end LeastErasureDoF
       9320  
       9321  namespace Hardening
       9322  open RememberedOffered
       9323  
       9324  /-! ## VII-b · the identification, stated exactly -/
       9325  
       9326  /-- On the chart, the registration fixes a point exactly when the point stands on the line. This is the whole of
       9327      `zeta_fixed_locus_correct` that the chart can carry: the line of the chart is d = 0, and Section 11 of the
       9328      paper reads Re s = 1/2 onto it by the reader's rule. -/
       9329  theorem zeta_fixed_locus_on_the_chart (p : Point) : reg p = p ↔ onLine p :=
       9330    reg_erases_nothing_iff p
       9331  
       9332  /-- Least erasure of a configuration is the value of that configuration, for every configuration, the one at
       9333      which the zeros of ζ are read included. No hypothesis. -/
       9334  theorem le_iff_value (S : Config) : LeastErasure S ↔ Value S :=
       9335    ⟨fun h p hp => (reg_erases_nothing_iff p).mp (h p hp),
       9336     fun h p hp => (reg_erases_nothing_iff p).mpr (h p hp)⟩
       9337  
       9338  /-- THE IDENTIFICATION, REDUCED TO THE READING. Whoever grants that the classical hypothesis is the value of the
       9339      configuration at which the zeros of ζ are read has, by theorem, granted that it is least erasure of that
       9340      configuration. The reading is the one input; nothing else is identified by name. -/
       9341  theorem classical_rh_iff_le_of_reading {ClassicalRH : Prop} {Zζ : Config}
       9342      (h_read : ClassicalRH ↔ Value Zζ) : ClassicalRH ↔ LeastErasure Zζ :=
       9343    h_read.trans (le_iff_value Zζ).symm
       9344  
       9345  /-- The field `supply` is the premise, by its type. Its presence in an act establishes nothing about which
       9346      configuration the act carries. -/
       9347  theorem supply_is_the_premise (A : ActualZeros) : LeastErasure A.zeros :=
       9348    A.supply
       9349  
       9350  /-- An act exists at a configuration exactly when the configuration is closed and least erasure holds there:
       9351      the act is the premise packaged, and the package adds nothing. -/
       9352  theorem the_act_is_the_premise_packaged (S : Config) :
       9353      (∃ A : ActualZeros, A.zeros = S) ↔ (Closed S ∧ LeastErasure S) :=
       9354    ⟨fun ⟨A, h⟩ => h ▸ ⟨A.closed, A.supply⟩,
       9355     fun ⟨hc, hle⟩ => ⟨⟨S, hc, hle⟩, rfl⟩⟩
       9356  
       9357  /-! ## VII-c · the bridge: six named arrows, composed by theorem -/
       9358  section Bridge
       9359  variable {Carrier : Type}
       9360  
       9361  /-- The floor one realized carrier puts under the residual observable: population × rate × heat per event. -/
       9362  theorem carrier_floor (density rate heat : Carrier → Nat) {n0 r0 q0 : Nat} (c : Carrier)
       9363      (hd : density c ≥ n0) (hr : rate c ≥ r0) (hq : heat c ≥ q0) :
       9364      LeastErasureDoF.residual (density c) (rate c) (heat c) ≥ n0 * r0 * q0 := by
       9365    unfold LeastErasureDoF.residual
       9366    exact Nat.mul_le_mul (Nat.mul_le_mul hd hr) hq
       9367  
       9368  /-- The threshold is positive exactly when the population floor, the rate floor and the heat floor are. -/
       9369  theorem gap_positive {n0 r0 q0 : Nat} (hn : n0 > 0) (hr : r0 > 0) (hq : q0 > 0) : n0 * r0 * q0 > 0 :=
       9370    Nat.mul_pos (Nat.mul_pos hn hr) hq
       9371  
       9372  /-- THE BRIDGE, COMPOSED. Six arrows, each a named hypothesis the reader grants or refuses:
       9373      h_carrier  a failure of least erasure at the read configuration realizes a carrier in the measured domain;
       9374      h_erase    a realized carrier irreversibly loses its which-branch label, kept in no other register;
       9375      h_pop      an erasing carrier is a population of at least n₀;
       9376      h_rate     an erasing carrier runs at a rate of at least r₀ during the observation;
       9377      h_heat     an erasing carrier deposits at least q₀ per event (Landauer, q₀ = k_B T ln 2 in the kernel's units);
       9378      h_couple   the residual observable covers the carrier's contribution: R ≥ population × rate × heat.
       9379      Conclusion: a failure of least erasure forces R ≥ n₀ r₀ q₀. The threshold does not depend on the carrier
       9380      and does not depend on which point stands off the line: it is uniform over the class the hypotheses name.
       9381      Positive rate and positive heat alone do not reach the conclusion; the population floor and the coupling are
       9382      needed and are named. -/
       9383  theorem off_line_zero_forces_observable_signal
       9384      {Zζ : Config} {R n0 r0 q0 : Nat}
       9385      (Realizes Erases : Carrier → Prop) (density rate heat : Carrier → Nat)
       9386      (h_carrier : ¬ LeastErasure Zζ → ∃ c, Realizes c)
       9387      (h_erase   : ∀ c, Realizes c → Erases c)
       9388      (h_pop     : ∀ c, Erases c → density c ≥ n0)
       9389      (h_rate    : ∀ c, Erases c → rate c ≥ r0)
       9390      (h_heat    : ∀ c, Erases c → heat c ≥ q0)
       9391      (h_couple  : ∀ c, Erases c → R ≥ LeastErasureDoF.residual (density c) (rate c) (heat c)) :
       9392      ¬ LeastErasure Zζ → R ≥ n0 * r0 * q0 := by
       9393    intro hnot
       9394    obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := h_carrier hnot
       9395    have he := h_erase c hc
       9396    exact Nat.le_trans (carrier_floor density rate heat c (h_pop c he) (h_rate c he) (h_heat c he)) (h_couple c he)
       9397  
       9398  end Bridge
       9399  
       9400  /-! ## VII-d · the heat theorem at its exact strength: the two cases, kept apart -/
       9401  
       9402  /-- Exact null: residual = 0 with positive rate and heat forces the population to zero. -/
       9403  theorem density_zero_from_exact_null {ρ r q : Nat} (hr : r > 0) (hq : q > 0)
       9404      (h0 : LeastErasureDoF.residual ρ r q = 0) : ρ = 0 :=
       9405    LeastErasureDoF.null_forces_zero hr hq h0
       9406  
       9407  /-- Finite sensitivity: residual ≤ ε with rate ≥ r₀ and heat ≥ q₀ bounds the population: ρ · r₀ q₀ ≤ ε. -/
       9408  theorem density_bound_at_finite_sensitivity {ρ r q r0 q0 ε : Nat}
       9409      (hR : LeastErasureDoF.residual ρ r q ≤ ε) (hr : r ≥ r0) (hq : q ≥ q0) :
       9410      ρ * r0 * q0 ≤ ε :=
       9411    LeastErasureDoF.density_bound_from_residual_bound hR hr hq
       9412  
       9413  /-! ## VII-e · THE CAPSTONE, every input printed -/
       9414  
       9415  /-- THE CAPSTONE. Five inputs, each printed, none carried by a structure:
       9416      h_id      the identification: the classical hypothesis is least erasure at the read configuration;
       9417      h_bridge  the bridge: a failure of least erasure there forces the residual observable to at least δ;
       9418      h_bound   the observational bound: the residual observable is at most ε;
       9419      h_gap     the gap: ε < δ;
       9420      h_pos     the threshold is positive (implied by h_gap over the naturals; printed because the Recommendation
       9421                prints it).
       9422      Conclusion: the classical hypothesis. The proof is pointwise and constructive: at each read point the
       9423      registration either fixes the point, or it does not and the bridge puts the residual at δ > ε ≥ R.
       9424      The cone is empty. An empty cone says the proof uses no axiom; it does not discharge a hypothesis. -/
       9425  theorem classical_rh_from_identification_gap_and_bound
       9426      {ClassicalRH : Prop} {Zζ : Config} {R δ ε : Nat}
       9427      (h_id     : ClassicalRH ↔ LeastErasure Zζ)
       9428      (h_bridge : ¬ LeastErasure Zζ → R ≥ δ)
       9429      (h_bound  : R ≤ ε)
       9430      (h_gap    : ε < δ)
       9431      (h_pos    : 0 < δ) :
       9432      ClassicalRH := by
       9433    have _hδ : δ ≠ 0 := Nat.pos_iff_ne_zero.mp h_pos
       9434    apply h_id.mpr
       9435    intro p hp
       9436    match decEq (reg p) p with
       9437    | isTrue h => exact h
       9438    | isFalse h =>
       9439      have hnot : ¬ LeastErasure Zζ := fun hle => h (hle p hp)
       9440      have hRδ : R ≥ δ := h_bridge hnot
       9441      exact absurd (Nat.lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.le_trans hRδ h_bound) h_gap) (Nat.lt_irrefl δ)
       9442  
       9443  /-- THE CAPSTONE, EXPLODED: the nine inputs of the Final Scribal Recommendation. The reading, the six arrows of
       9444      the bridge, the bound, and the gap against the composed threshold n₀ r₀ q₀. -/
       9445  theorem classical_rh_from_the_arrows
       9446      {Carrier : Type} {ClassicalRH : Prop} {Zζ : Config} {R n0 r0 q0 ε : Nat}
       9447      (Realizes Erases : Carrier → Prop) (density rate heat : Carrier → Nat)
       9448      (h_read    : ClassicalRH ↔ Value Zζ)
       9449      (h_carrier : ¬ LeastErasure Zζ → ∃ c, Realizes c)
       9450      (h_erase   : ∀ c, Realizes c → Erases c)
       9451      (h_pop     : ∀ c, Erases c → density c ≥ n0)
       9452      (h_rate    : ∀ c, Erases c → rate c ≥ r0)
       9453      (h_heat    : ∀ c, Erases c → heat c ≥ q0)
       9454      (h_couple  : ∀ c, Erases c → R ≥ LeastErasureDoF.residual (density c) (rate c) (heat c))
       9455      (h_bound   : R ≤ ε)
       9456      (h_gap     : ε < n0 * r0 * q0) :
       9457      ClassicalRH :=
       9458    classical_rh_from_identification_gap_and_bound
       9459      (classical_rh_iff_le_of_reading h_read)
       9460      (off_line_zero_forces_observable_signal Realizes Erases density rate heat
       9461        h_carrier h_erase h_pop h_rate h_heat h_couple)
       9462      h_bound h_gap (Nat.lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.zero_le ε) h_gap)
       9463  
       9464  /-- THE EXACT-NULL ROUTE, the Mandate II of the second edition, with its premise printed. If a failure of least
       9465      erasure realizes a population of positive size, rate and heat whose contribution the residual covers, and the
       9466      residual is EXACTLY zero, the hypothesis follows. The premise R = 0 is not what a measurement at finite
       9467      sensitivity reports; the paper's closure runs on the gap route above, and this theorem records where the
       9468      second edition's wording stood. -/
       9469  theorem classical_rh_from_identification_and_exact_null
       9470      {ClassicalRH : Prop} {Zζ : Config} {R : Nat}
       9471      (h_id     : ClassicalRH ↔ LeastErasure Zζ)
       9472      (h_bridge : ¬ LeastErasure Zζ → ∃ ρ r q : Nat, ρ > 0 ∧ r > 0 ∧ q > 0 ∧ R ≥ LeastErasureDoF.residual ρ r q)
       9473      (h_null   : R = 0) :
       9474      ClassicalRH := by
       9475    apply h_id.mpr
       9476    intro p hp
       9477    match decEq (reg p) p with
       9478    | isTrue h => exact h
       9479    | isFalse h =>
       9480      have hnot : ¬ LeastErasure Zζ := fun hle => h (hle p hp)
       9481      obtain ⟨ρ, r, q, hρ, hr, hq, hR⟩ := h_bridge hnot
       9482      have hpos := LeastErasureDoF.residual_pos hρ hr hq
       9483      rw [h_null] at hR
       9484      exact absurd (Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le hpos hR) (Nat.lt_irrefl 0)
       9485  
       9486  /-- NO THIRD POSITION. Given the identification, the bound and the gap, the denial of the hypothesis and the
       9487      bridge cannot both stand. A reader who denies the hypothesis has named the bridge as the arrow that fails;
       9488      a reader who grants the bridge has granted the hypothesis. Constructive; the cone is empty. -/
       9489  theorem no_third_position
       9490      {ClassicalRH : Prop} {Zζ : Config} {R δ ε : Nat}
       9491      (h_id    : ClassicalRH ↔ LeastErasure Zζ)
       9492      (h_bound : R ≤ ε)
       9493      (h_gap   : ε < δ) :
       9494      ¬ (¬ ClassicalRH ∧ (¬ LeastErasure Zζ → R ≥ δ)) := by
       9495    intro ⟨hno, h_bridge⟩
       9496    have hnot : ¬ LeastErasure Zζ := fun hle => hno (h_id.mpr hle)
       9497    exact absurd (Nat.lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.le_trans (h_bridge hnot) h_bound) h_gap) (Nat.lt_irrefl δ)
       9498  
       9499  /-! ## VII-f · what the capstone does not do, by theorem: its inputs are keyed -/
       9500  
       9501  /-- The pair world of the off point is closed and lacks least erasure. -/
       9502  theorem pair_world_lacks_le : Closed (pairWorld offPoint) ∧ ¬ LeastErasure (pairWorld offPoint) :=
       9503    ⟨pair_world_closed offPoint,
       9504     fun hle => off_point_is_off ((reg_erases_nothing_iff offPoint).mp (hle offPoint (Or.inl rfl)))⟩
       9505  
       9506  /-- THE READING IS KEYED. No theorem of the interface identifies an arbitrary proposition with least erasure at
       9507      an arbitrary closed configuration: for the true proposition and the pair world the identification fails. The
       9508      identification is therefore an input, granted for the reading of Section 11 and for nothing else. -/
       9509  theorem the_reading_is_keyed :
       9510      ∃ (P : Prop) (S : Config), Closed S ∧ ¬ (P ↔ LeastErasure S) :=
       9511    ⟨True, pairWorld offPoint, pair_world_lacks_le.1,
       9512     fun h => pair_world_lacks_le.2 (h.mp trivial)⟩
       9513  
       9514  /-- THE BRIDGE IS KEYED. No theorem of the interface makes a failure of least erasure lift the residual: on the
       9515      pair world with R = 0 and δ = 1 the bridge fails. The bridge is therefore an input: derived from the physics
       9516      at the grade of its arrows, or granted by name, never read off the chart. -/
       9517  theorem the_bridge_is_keyed :
       9518      ∃ (S : Config) (R δ : Nat), Closed S ∧ ¬ LeastErasure S ∧ ¬ (¬ LeastErasure S → R ≥ δ) :=
       9519    ⟨pairWorld offPoint, 0, 1, pair_world_lacks_le.1, pair_world_lacks_le.2,
       9520     fun h => Nat.not_succ_le_zero 0 (h pair_world_lacks_le.2)⟩
       9521  
       9522  /-- THE BOUND DOES NOT CLOSE ALONE. A bound R ≤ ε with no bridge leaves least erasure undecided: the pair world
       9523      is closed, lacks least erasure, and is consistent with every bound. -/
       9524  theorem the_bound_alone_decides_nothing (ε : Nat) :
       9525      ∃ S : Config, Closed S ∧ ¬ LeastErasure S ∧ (0 : Nat) ≤ ε :=
       9526    ⟨pairWorld offPoint, pair_world_lacks_le.1, pair_world_lacks_le.2, Nat.zero_le ε⟩
       9527  
       9528  /-! ## VII-g · the hardened closure -/
       9529  
       9530  /-- THE HARDENED CLOSURE. The two-sided closure of Part VI, the seven-claim master seal of the companion kernel,
       9531      the identification reduced to the reading, the act as the premise packaged, the bridge composed, the two
       9532      cases of the heat theorem, the capstone in both forms, the exact-null route, no third position, and the three
       9533      keyed-input theorems, each by its exact type. -/
       9534  theorem the_hardened_closure :
       9535      (type_of% @BothSides.the_two_sided_closure) ∧
       9536      (type_of% @LeastErasureDoF.the_master_seal) ∧
       9537      (type_of% @classical_rh_iff_le_of_reading) ∧
       9538      (type_of% @the_act_is_the_premise_packaged) ∧
       9539      (type_of% @off_line_zero_forces_observable_signal) ∧
       9540      (type_of% @density_zero_from_exact_null) ∧
       9541      (type_of% @density_bound_at_finite_sensitivity) ∧
       9542      (type_of% @classical_rh_from_identification_gap_and_bound) ∧
       9543      (type_of% @classical_rh_from_the_arrows) ∧
       9544      (type_of% @classical_rh_from_identification_and_exact_null) ∧
       9545      (type_of% @no_third_position) ∧
       9546      (type_of% @the_reading_is_keyed) ∧
       9547      (type_of% @the_bridge_is_keyed) ∧
       9548      (type_of% @the_bound_alone_decides_nothing) :=
       9549    ⟨@BothSides.the_two_sided_closure, @LeastErasureDoF.the_master_seal,
       9550     @classical_rh_iff_le_of_reading, @the_act_is_the_premise_packaged,
       9551     @off_line_zero_forces_observable_signal, @density_zero_from_exact_null,
       9552     @density_bound_at_finite_sensitivity, @classical_rh_from_identification_gap_and_bound,
       9553     @classical_rh_from_the_arrows, @classical_rh_from_identification_and_exact_null,
       9554     @no_third_position, @the_reading_is_keyed, @the_bridge_is_keyed, @the_bound_alone_decides_nothing⟩
       9555  
       9556  end Hardening
       9557  end PartVII

       9649  /-! # PART VIII · the physico-formal carrier — OPTIONAL CORROBORATION, NOT REQUIRED FOR THE FORMAL LOOP -/
       9650  /-!
       9651    PART VIII · THE PHYSICO-FORMAL CARRIER.
       9652  
       9653    Part VII took the carrier as a type variable and six arrows as hypotheses. Part VIII replaces the variable by a
       9654    type given by its constructors, `PhysicalCarrier`: a self-conjugate state at a height (the neutral sector), or a
       9655    member of a conjugate pair at a height with the sign that tells it from its partner (the charged sector). Charge
       9656    conjugation `C` and annihilation `annihilate` are defined on it by cases; the physical carrier is then an instance
       9657    of the seed's own carrier abstraction (Part II, `PrimeFreedom.Carrier`): `C` is a fold, `annihilate` its
       9658    registration, and every law of that namespace holds on the carrier by theorem.
       9659  
       9660    The map from a zero to its carrier, `map_zero_to_carrier`, is total by the integer's constructors and a bijection
       9661    with the chart; it carries the fold to charge conjugation, the line to the neutral sector, and the registration to
       9662    annihilation. On this map two of Part VII's six arrows are theorems: an off-line zero is carried to the charged
       9663    sector (h_carrier), where annihilation does not fix it and sends it and its partner to one state, so one label is
       9664    lost and kept nowhere on the carrier (h_erase). A third, h_heat, is Landauer's law entered as a definition,
       9665    `landauerHeatPerEvent T = T · ln 2`, with a temperature floor: the arrow is then the monotonicity of a product.
       9666  
       9667    What remains is physics, and is printed as hypotheses of the capstone: h_realize, that the vacuum instantiates
       9668    the carrier of every read zero; h_pop and h_rate, the population and rate floors of a realized charged carrier;
       9669    h_temp, the temperature floor; h_couple, that the residual observable covers the carrier's contribution; the
       9670    reading h_read; and a certified bound B. No definition below makes any of these true. A theorem that the universe
       9671    realizes a state is not available to any logic: it enters as an axiom, which this file declares none of; as a
       9672    hypothesis, which is what is done here; or as a definition that is the claim restated, which the Final Scribal
       9673    Recommendation forbids (no hidden premise in a structure field). The theorems of VIII-f record, by witness, that
       9674    the realization predicate is the input: one choice of it makes h_realize hold at every configuration, another
       9675    makes it fail at the pair world.
       9676  
       9677    NOTE: in the flipped formal register, the observational inputs of this part
       9678    (h_realize, h_pop, h_rate, h_temp, h_couple, h_read, the certified bound B) are SUPERSEDED in the
       9679    core arch by the formalized compute cargo — the local `VerificationEvent` enacting `Stage1`
       9680    (`ApparatusCargo`), the formal registration projection, and `BoundChainMathlib`'s proved links
       9681    (`h_read_proved`, `h_id_proved`) over ℂ. The eight empirical inputs, including
       9682    `CertifiedObservationalBound`, bath temperatures, Landauer heat floors, carrier population and
       9683    rate floors, and residual flux couplings, are retired from the active arch and remain in this
       9684    file, untouched, as fenced conditional theorems (optional retrospective corroboration),
       9685    matching the status of `ApparatusCargo.stage2_optional_corroboration`.
       9686  -/
       9687  section PartVIII
       9688  namespace PhysicoFormal
       9689  open RememberedOffered
       9690  
       9691  /-! ## VIII-a · the carrier, by constructors; conjugation and annihilation, by cases -/
       9692  
       9693  /-- THE PHYSICAL CARRIER. A state of the sector in which a zero is realized is one of two kinds:
       9694      `selfConjugate t`, a state at height t that charge conjugation fixes, the neutral sector; or
       9695      `conjugatePair m t sign`, a member of the conjugate pair of magnitude m + 1 at height t, with `sign` the one
       9696      label that tells it from its partner, the charged sector. A type given by its constructors, inhabited at every
       9697      height; which of its states the vacuum instantiates is the premise h_realize of VIII-e, not a field here. -/
       9698  inductive PhysicalCarrier where
       9699    | selfConjugate (t : Int)
       9700    | conjugatePair (m : Nat) (t : Int) (sign : Bool)
       9701  
       9702  /-- Charge conjugation: it fixes the neutral sector and flips the sign in the charged sector. -/
       9703  def C : PhysicalCarrier → PhysicalCarrier
       9704    | .selfConjugate t => .selfConjugate t
       9705    | .conjugatePair m t s => .conjugatePair m t (!s)
       9706  
       9707  theorem C_involutive (c : PhysicalCarrier) : C (C c) = c := by
       9708    cases c with
       9709    | selfConjugate t => rfl
       9710    | conjugatePair m t s => cases s <;> rfl
       9711  
       9712  /-- The neutral sector: the self-conjugate states. -/
       9713  def Neutral : PhysicalCarrier → Prop
       9714    | .selfConjugate _ => True
       9715    | .conjugatePair _ _ _ => False
       9716  
       9717  /-- The neutral sector is exactly the fixed locus of charge conjugation. -/
       9718  theorem neutral_iff_C_fixed (c : PhysicalCarrier) : Neutral c ↔ C c = c := by
       9719    cases c with
       9720    | selfConjugate t => exact ⟨fun _ => rfl, fun _ => trivial⟩
       9721    | conjugatePair m t s => exact ⟨fun h => h.elim, fun h => by cases s <;> cases h⟩
       9722  
       9723  /-- Fixedness under charge conjugation is decided on the carrier, by cases. -/
       9724  theorem carrier_em (c : PhysicalCarrier) : C c = c ∨ C c ≠ c := by
       9725    cases c with
       9726    | selfConjugate t => exact Or.inl rfl
       9727    | conjugatePair m t s => exact Or.inr (fun h => by cases s <;> cases h)
       9728  
       9729  /-- Annihilation, the physical discard: a member of a pair goes to the neutral state at its height; a neutral state
       9730      stays. The sign is kept in no register of the carrier. -/
       9731  def annihilate : PhysicalCarrier → PhysicalCarrier
       9732    | .selfConjugate t => .selfConjugate t
       9733    | .conjugatePair _ t _ => .selfConjugate t
       9734  
       9735  theorem annihilate_lands (c : PhysicalCarrier) : C (annihilate c) = annihilate c := by
       9736    cases c <;> rfl
       9737  
       9738  theorem annihilate_fixes (c : PhysicalCarrier) (h : C c = c) : annihilate c = c := by
       9739    cases c with
       9740    | selfConjugate t => rfl
       9741    | conjugatePair m t s => cases s <;> cases h
       9742  
       9743  theorem annihilate_forgets (c : PhysicalCarrier) : annihilate (C c) = annihilate c := by
       9744    cases c <;> rfl
       9745  
       9746  /-- Annihilation fixes a state exactly when the state is neutral. -/
       9747  theorem annihilate_fixes_iff_neutral (c : PhysicalCarrier) : annihilate c = c ↔ Neutral c := by
       9748    cases c with
       9749    | selfConjugate t => exact ⟨fun _ => trivial, fun _ => rfl⟩
       9750    | conjugatePair m t s => exact ⟨fun h => (by cases h), fun h => h.elim⟩
       9751  
       9752  /-- A conjugate pair is two states with one image under annihilation: the sign is the bit that annihilation erases. -/
       9753  theorem pair_is_two_states_one_image (m : Nat) (t : Int) :
       9754      PhysicalCarrier.conjugatePair m t true ≠ PhysicalCarrier.conjugatePair m t false ∧
       9755      annihilate (.conjugatePair m t true) = annihilate (.conjugatePair m t false) :=
       9756    ⟨fun h => (by cases h), rfl⟩
       9757  
       9758  /-- THE PHYSICAL CARRIER IS AN INSTANCE OF THE SEED'S CARRIER ABSTRACTION (Part II): charge conjugation is a fold. -/
       9759  def carrierFold : PrimeFreedom.Carrier.Fold PhysicalCarrier := ⟨C, C_involutive⟩
       9760  
       9761  /-- Annihilation is a registration for that fold: it lands on the neutral sector, fixes it, and forgets the sign. -/
       9762  def carrierReg : PrimeFreedom.Carrier.Registration carrierFold :=
       9763    ⟨annihilate, annihilate_lands, annihilate_fixes, annihilate_forgets⟩
       9764  
       9765  /-- THE CLOSURE ON THE PHYSICAL CARRIER: the four laws Part II proves on any carrier, instantiated on this one by
       9766      theorem. Least erasure is the value; the value is lossless registration; the lossless member of a record is
       9767      unique; every charged state gives two worlds of one record that differ in the value. -/
       9768  theorem the_closure_on_the_physical_carrier :
       9769      type_of% (PrimeFreedom.Carrier.the_closure_on_any_carrier carrierReg carrier_em) :=
       9770    PrimeFreedom.Carrier.the_closure_on_any_carrier carrierReg carrier_em
       9771  
       9772  /-! ## VIII-b · the map from a zero to its carrier, total and bijective, equivariant -/
       9773  
       9774  /-- THE MAP FROM A ZERO TO ITS CARRIER. A point of the chart at offset d and height t goes: on the line, to the
       9775      self-conjugate state at t; at offset n + 1, to the positive member of the pair of magnitude n + 1 at t; at offset
       9776      −(n + 1), to the negative member. Total, by the integer's three constructors. -/
       9777  def map_zero_to_carrier : Point → PhysicalCarrier
       9778    | (Int.ofNat 0, t) => .selfConjugate t
       9779    | (Int.ofNat (n + 1), t) => .conjugatePair n t true
       9780    | (Int.negSucc n, t) => .conjugatePair n t false
       9781  
       9782  /-- The inverse: a carrier state read back as a point of the chart. -/
       9783  def carrier_to_zero : PhysicalCarrier → Point
       9784    | .selfConjugate t => (Int.ofNat 0, t)
       9785    | .conjugatePair n t true => (Int.ofNat (n + 1), t)
       9786    | .conjugatePair n t false => (Int.negSucc n, t)
       9787  
       9788  theorem map_left_inverse (p : Point) : carrier_to_zero (map_zero_to_carrier p) = p := by
       9789    obtain ⟨d, t⟩ := p
       9790    cases d with
       9791    | ofNat n => cases n <;> rfl
       9792    | negSucc n => rfl
       9793  
       9794  theorem map_right_inverse (c : PhysicalCarrier) : map_zero_to_carrier (carrier_to_zero c) = c := by
       9795    cases c with
       9796    | selfConjugate t => rfl
       9797    | conjugatePair n t s => cases s <;> rfl
       9798  
       9799  /-- The map is injective: two zeros with one carrier are one zero. -/
       9800  theorem map_injective (p q : Point) (h : map_zero_to_carrier p = map_zero_to_carrier q) : p = q := by
       9801    rw [← map_left_inverse p, ← map_left_inverse q, h]
       9802  
       9803  /-- The map is surjective: every carrier state is the carrier of a zero. -/
       9804  theorem map_surjective (c : PhysicalCarrier) : ∃ p, map_zero_to_carrier p = c :=
       9805    ⟨carrier_to_zero c, map_right_inverse c⟩
       9806  
       9807  /-- EQUIVARIANCE. The fold of the chart is charge conjugation on the carrier: s ↦ 1 − s̄ is C. -/
       9808  theorem map_fold (p : Point) : map_zero_to_carrier (fold p) = C (map_zero_to_carrier p) := by
       9809    obtain ⟨d, t⟩ := p
       9810    cases d with
       9811    | ofNat n => cases n <;> rfl
       9812    | negSucc n => rfl
       9813  
       9814  /-- The line of the chart is the neutral sector of the carrier. -/
       9815  theorem map_neutral_iff_onLine (p : Point) : Neutral (map_zero_to_carrier p) ↔ onLine p := by
       9816    obtain ⟨d, t⟩ := p
       9817    cases d with
       9818    | ofNat n =>
       9819      cases n with
       9820      | zero => exact ⟨fun _ => rfl, fun _ => trivial⟩
       9821      | succ n => exact ⟨fun h => h.elim, fun h => by cases h⟩
       9822    | negSucc n => exact ⟨fun h => h.elim, fun h => by cases h⟩
       9823  
       9824  /-- The registration of the chart is annihilation on the carrier. -/
       9825  theorem map_reg (p : Point) : map_zero_to_carrier (reg p) = annihilate (map_zero_to_carrier p) := by
       9826    obtain ⟨d, t⟩ := p
       9827    cases d with
       9828    | ofNat n => cases n <;> rfl
       9829    | negSucc n => rfl
       9830  
       9831  /-- Least erasure on the chart is least erasure on the carrier, configuration by configuration, through the map. -/
       9832  theorem le_transports (S : Config) :
       9833      LeastErasure S ↔ ∀ p, S p → annihilate (map_zero_to_carrier p) = map_zero_to_carrier p := by
       9834    constructor
       9835    · intro h p hp
       9836      rw [← map_reg, h p hp]
       9837    · intro h p hp
       9838      exact (reg_erases_nothing_iff p).mpr ((map_neutral_iff_onLine p).mp
       9839        ((annihilate_fixes_iff_neutral _).mp (h p hp)))
       9840  
       9841  /-! ## VIII-c · the mathematical violation forces the physical discard -/
       9842  
       9843  /-- MATHEMATICAL VIOLATION FORCES PHYSICAL DISCARD. A zero off the line is carried to the charged sector; there
       9844      charge conjugation moves it, annihilation does not fix it, and annihilation sends it and its conjugate partner
       9845      to one state. One label, the sign, is lost and kept in no register of the carrier. Theorem; no premise. This
       9846      is h_carrier and h_erase of Part VII, discharged on the concrete carrier. -/
       9847  theorem mathematical_violation_forces_physical_discard (p : Point) (h : ¬ onLine p) :
       9848      ¬ Neutral (map_zero_to_carrier p) ∧
       9849      C (map_zero_to_carrier p) ≠ map_zero_to_carrier p ∧
       9850      annihilate (map_zero_to_carrier p) ≠ map_zero_to_carrier p ∧
       9851      annihilate (C (map_zero_to_carrier p)) = annihilate (map_zero_to_carrier p) :=
       9852    have hn : ¬ Neutral (map_zero_to_carrier p) := fun hN => h ((map_neutral_iff_onLine p).mp hN)
       9853    ⟨hn,
       9854     fun hC => hn ((neutral_iff_C_fixed _).mpr hC),
       9855     fun hA => hn ((annihilate_fixes_iff_neutral _).mp hA),
       9856     annihilate_forgets _⟩
       9857  
       9858  /-- ON THE LINE NOTHING IS DISCARDED: the carrier is neutral and annihilation fixes it. -/
       9859  theorem on_line_discards_nothing (p : Point) (h : onLine p) :
       9860      Neutral (map_zero_to_carrier p) ∧ annihilate (map_zero_to_carrier p) = map_zero_to_carrier p :=
       9861    have hN := (map_neutral_iff_onLine p).mpr h
       9862    ⟨hN, (annihilate_fixes_iff_neutral _).mpr hN⟩
       9863  
       9864  /-! ## VIII-d · the energetic bookkeeping: labels, entropy, heat -/
       9865  
       9866  /-- LANDAUER'S LAW, ENTERED AS A DEFINITION: the heat of erasing one label at temperature T is T · ln 2 in the
       9867      kernel's units (ln 2 scaled by 10⁶). It is a physical law, not derived here; the kernel's
       9868      `heat_from_joint_conservation` carries only its shape, and no theorem below pretends otherwise. What the
       9869      theorems derive is the count of labels and that the heat is positive exactly when the count is. -/
       9870  def landauerHeatPerEvent (T : Nat) : Nat := T * LeastErasureDoF.ln2_scaled
       9871  
       9872  /-- The heat of erasing b labels at temperature T. -/
       9873  def landauerHeat (bits T : Nat) : Nat := bits * landauerHeatPerEvent T
       9874  
       9875  /-- The heat is the seed's price (Part III, `price`) at the temperature T · ln 2. -/
       9876  theorem landauerHeat_is_price (bits T : Nat) : landauerHeat bits T = price (landauerHeatPerEvent T) bits := rfl
       9877  
       9878  /-- The per-event heat is monotone in the temperature: a temperature floor is a heat floor. This is h_heat of
       9879      Part VII, derived from the law and the floor. -/
       9880  theorem heat_floor_from_temperature {T T0 : Nat} (h : T ≥ T0) :
       9881      landauerHeatPerEvent T ≥ landauerHeatPerEvent T0 :=
       9882    Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ h
       9883  
       9884  /-- The per-event heat at the CMB temperature of the kernel is positive. -/
       9885  theorem heat_at_cmb_positive : landauerHeatPerEvent LeastErasureDoF.cmb_mK > 0 :=
       9886    Nat.mul_pos (by decide) (by decide)
       9887  
       9888  /-- A FINITE CONFIGURATION AS A SYSTEM OF THE KERNEL: one record per height on the line and one per pair; one free
       9889      label, the sign, per pair; the total the product. -/
       9890  def systemOf (F : FinCfg) : LeastErasureDoF.System :=
       9891    ⟨F.line.length + F.pairs.length, F.pairs.length,
       9892     (F.line.length + F.pairs.length) * 2 ^ F.pairs.length, rfl⟩
       9893  
       9894  /-- The same records with every sign gone: the system after annihilation. -/
       9895  def systemAfter (F : FinCfg) : LeastErasureDoF.System :=
       9896    ⟨F.line.length + F.pairs.length, 0, (F.line.length + F.pairs.length) * 2 ^ 0, rfl⟩
       9897  
       9898  /-- The entropy the kernel assigns to the configuration is one ln 2 per pair, and after annihilation it is zero:
       9899      the entropy drop of the discard is the erased count times ln 2. -/
       9900  theorem entropy_of_discard (F : FinCfg) :
       9901      LeastErasureDoF.sysEntropy (systemOf F) = erased F * LeastErasureDoF.ln2_scaled ∧
       9902      LeastErasureDoF.sysEntropy (systemAfter F) = 0 :=
       9903    ⟨rfl, Nat.zero_mul _⟩
       9904  
       9905  /-- One annihilation is one erasure of the kernel: a system with one more label and twice the total, taken to
       9906      this system. Records kept, one label lost, total halved. -/
       9907  def oneAnnihilation (s : LeastErasureDoF.System) (hs : s.distinct > 0) : LeastErasureDoF.EraseProcess :=
       9908    { before := ⟨s.distinct, s.free + 1, 2 * s.total, by
       9909        have h_inv : s.total = s.distinct * Nat.pow 2 s.free := s.inv
       9910        have h1 : 2 * s.total = 2 * (s.distinct * Nat.pow 2 s.free) :=
       9911          congrArg (fun x => 2 * x) h_inv
       9912        have h2 : 2 * (s.distinct * Nat.pow 2 s.free) = (s.distinct * Nat.pow 2 s.free) + (s.distinct * Nat.pow 2 s.free) :=
       9913          Nat.two_mul _
       9914        have h3 : (Nat.pow 2 s.free) * 2 = (Nat.pow 2 s.free) + (Nat.pow 2 s.free) := Nat.mul_two _
       9915        have h4 : s.distinct * ((Nat.pow 2 s.free) * 2) = s.distinct * ((Nat.pow 2 s.free) + (Nat.pow 2 s.free)) :=
       9916          congrArg (fun x => s.distinct * x) h3
       9917        have h5 : s.distinct * ((Nat.pow 2 s.free) + (Nat.pow 2 s.free))
       9918            = s.distinct * (Nat.pow 2 s.free) + s.distinct * (Nat.pow 2 s.free) :=
       9919          Nat.left_distrib _ _ _
       9920        have h6 : s.distinct * ((Nat.pow 2 s.free) * 2) = (s.distinct * Nat.pow 2 s.free) + (s.distinct * Nat.pow 2 s.free) :=
       9921          Eq.trans h4 h5
       9922        have h7 : 2 * (s.distinct * Nat.pow 2 s.free) = s.distinct * ((Nat.pow 2 s.free) * 2) :=
       9923          Eq.trans h2 (Eq.symm h6)
       9924        have h8 : s.distinct * ((Nat.pow 2 s.free) * 2) = s.distinct * Nat.pow 2 (s.free + 1) := rfl
       9925        exact Eq.trans (Eq.trans h1 h7) h8⟩
       9926      after := s
       9927      h_distinct := rfl
       9928      h_free := rfl
       9929      h_total := rfl
       9930      h_gt := by
       9931        show s.total < 2 * s.total
       9932        have hpos : 0 < s.total := by
       9933          rw [s.inv]; exact Nat.mul_pos hs (Nat.two_pow_pos _)
       9934        rw [Nat.two_mul]
       9935        exact Nat.lt_add_of_pos_left hpos }
       9936  
       9937  /-- The kernel's entropy law holds of each annihilation by instance. -/
       9938  theorem annihilation_drops_one_ln2 (s : LeastErasureDoF.System) (hs : s.distinct > 0) :
       9939      LeastErasureDoF.sysEntropy (oneAnnihilation s hs).after + LeastErasureDoF.ln2_scaled =
       9940        LeastErasureDoF.sysEntropy (oneAnnihilation s hs).before :=
       9941    LeastErasureDoF.sysEntropy_decrease _
       9942  
       9943  /-- DISCARD FORCES HEAT GENERATION. The annihilation of a finite configuration erases one label per off-line pair,
       9944      the seed's `erased`; at any positive temperature its Landauer heat is zero exactly at the value, and positive
       9945      whenever a point stands off the line. The count is theorem; the law is `landauerHeatPerEvent`. -/
       9946  theorem discard_forces_heat_generation (F : FinCfg) (T : Nat) (hT : 0 < T) :
       9947      (landauerHeat (erased F) T = 0 ↔ Value F.pts) ∧
       9948      (¬ Value F.pts → landauerHeat (erased F) T > 0) :=
       9949    have hq : 0 < landauerHeatPerEvent T := Nat.mul_pos hT (by decide)
       9950    have hiff : landauerHeat (erased F) T = 0 ↔ Value F.pts := price_zero_iff_value F _ hq
       9951    ⟨hiff, fun hv => Nat.pos_of_ne_zero (fun h0 => hv (hiff.mp h0))⟩
       9952  
       9953  /-! ## VIII-e · the certified bound, the physical premises, and the physico-formal capstone -/
       9954  
       9955  /-- A CERTIFIED OBSERVATIONAL BOUND: the residual observable R, the sensitivity ε, the certificate R ≤ ε, and the
       9956      name of the dataset that issued it. A measurement is a premise by its nature; this is the type it is entered as. -/
       9957  structure CertifiedObservationalBound where
       9958    R : Nat
       9959    ε : Nat
       9960    certificate : R ≤ ε
       9961    dataset : String
       9962  
       9963  /-- The detection gap: the uniform floor a realized charged carrier puts under the residual observable,
       9964      δ = n₀ · r₀ · (T₀ · ln 2). -/
       9965  def detectionGap (n0 r0 T0 : Nat) : Nat := n0 * r0 * landauerHeatPerEvent T0
       9966  
       9967  /-- The gap is positive exactly when its three floors are. -/
       9968  theorem detectionGap_pos {n0 r0 T0 : Nat} (hn : n0 > 0) (hr : r0 > 0) (hT : T0 > 0) : detectionGap n0 r0 T0 > 0 :=
       9969    Nat.mul_pos (Nat.mul_pos hn hr) (Nat.mul_pos hT (by decide))
       9970  
       9971  /-- THE SIGNAL FLOOR OF A REALIZED CHARGED CARRIER, from the three floors and the coupling: population × rate × heat
       9972      per event is at least n₀ · r₀ · (T₀ · ln 2), and the residual covers it. -/
       9973  theorem signal_floor {R n0 r0 T0 T : Nat} (population rate : PhysicalCarrier → Nat) (c : PhysicalCarrier)
       9974      (h_pop : population c ≥ n0) (h_rate : rate c ≥ r0) (h_temp : T ≥ T0)
       9975      (h_couple : R ≥ LeastErasureDoF.residual (population c) (rate c) (landauerHeatPerEvent T)) :
       9976      R ≥ detectionGap n0 r0 T0 :=
       9977    Nat.le_trans (Nat.mul_le_mul (Nat.mul_le_mul h_pop h_rate) (heat_floor_from_temperature h_temp)) h_couple
       9978  
       9979  /-- EVERY VIOLATION EXCEEDS THE DETECTION GAP. Two physical premises, named: the vacuum instantiates the carrier of
       9980      every read zero (h_realize); a realized charged carrier puts the floor δ under R (h_signal). Then a read zero
       9981      off the line forces R ≥ δ. That the zero's carrier is charged is theorem (VIII-c), not premise. -/
       9982  theorem every_violation_exceeds_detection_gap
       9983      {Zζ : Config} {R δ : Nat} (realized : PhysicalCarrier → Prop)
       9984      (h_realize : ∀ p, Zζ p → realized (map_zero_to_carrier p))
       9985      (h_signal  : ∀ c, realized c → ¬ Neutral c → R ≥ δ)
       9986      (p : Point) (hp : Zζ p) (hoff : ¬ onLine p) : R ≥ δ :=
       9987    h_signal _ (h_realize p hp) (mathematical_violation_forces_physical_discard p hoff).1
       9988  
       9989  /-- THE BRIDGE OF PART VII, DERIVED. From the two physical premises, a failure of least erasure at the read
       9990      configuration forces R ≥ δ: exactly h_bridge of `classical_rh_from_identification_gap_and_bound`. The step from
       9991      a failed universal to a witness is classical; the cone is printed. -/
       9992  theorem bridge_from_realization
       9993      {Zζ : Config} {R δ : Nat} (realized : PhysicalCarrier → Prop)
       9994      (h_realize : ∀ p, Zζ p → realized (map_zero_to_carrier p))
       9995      (h_signal  : ∀ c, realized c → ¬ Neutral c → R ≥ δ) :
       9996      ¬ LeastErasure Zζ → R ≥ δ := by
       9997    intro hnot
       9998    apply Classical.byContradiction
       9999    intro hlt
      10000    apply hnot
      10001    intro p hp
      10002    apply (reg_erases_nothing_iff p).mpr
      10003    apply Classical.byContradiction
      10004    intro hoff
      10005    exact hlt (every_violation_exceeds_detection_gap realized h_realize h_signal p hp hoff)
      10006  
      10007  /-- THE PHYSICO-FORMAL CLOSURE. The capstone, every input printed, the carrier concrete:
      10008      h_read     the reading: the classical hypothesis is the value of the configuration at which the zeros are read;
      10009      h_realize  the vacuum instantiates the carrier of every read zero                               (physics);
      10010      h_pop      a realized charged carrier is a population of at least n₀                            (physics);
      10011      h_rate     a realized charged carrier annihilates at a rate of at least r₀ during the observation (physics);
      10012      h_temp     the temperature during the observation is at least T₀                                (physics);
      10013      h_couple   the residual observable covers the carrier's contribution, population × rate × heat   (physics);
      10014      B          a certified bound R ≤ ε from a named dataset                                           (measurement);
      10015      h_gap      ε < δ = n₀ · r₀ · (T₀ · ln 2)                                                          (arithmetic on the two).
      10016      Discharged on the carrier, no longer hypotheses: that an off-line zero is realized as a charged state, that its
      10017      annihilation erases one label, and that the heat per label is T · ln 2 ≥ T₀ · ln 2.
      10018      Conclusion: the classical hypothesis. Pointwise and constructive; the cone is empty. An empty cone says the
      10019      proof uses no axiom; it discharges none of the eight inputs. -/
      10020  theorem classical_rh_from_physico_formal_closure
      10021      {ClassicalRH : Prop} {Zζ : Config} {n0 r0 T0 T : Nat}
      10022      (realized : PhysicalCarrier → Prop) (population rate : PhysicalCarrier → Nat)
      10023      (B : CertifiedObservationalBound)
      10024      (h_read    : ClassicalRH ↔ Value Zζ)
      10025      (h_realize : ∀ p, Zζ p → realized (map_zero_to_carrier p))
      10026      (h_pop     : ∀ c, realized c → ¬ Neutral c → population c ≥ n0)
      10027      (h_rate    : ∀ c, realized c → ¬ Neutral c → rate c ≥ r0)
      10028      (h_temp    : T ≥ T0)
      10029      (h_couple  : ∀ c, realized c → ¬ Neutral c →
      10030                     B.R ≥ LeastErasureDoF.residual (population c) (rate c) (landauerHeatPerEvent T))
      10031      (h_gap     : B.ε < detectionGap n0 r0 T0) :
      10032      ClassicalRH := by
      10033    apply h_read.mpr
      10034    intro p hp
      10035    match decEq p.1 0 with
      10036    | isTrue h => exact h
      10037    | isFalse hoff =>
      10038      have hc : ¬ Neutral (map_zero_to_carrier p) := (mathematical_violation_forces_physical_discard p hoff).1
      10039      have hr := h_realize p hp
      10040      have hfloor : B.R ≥ detectionGap n0 r0 T0 :=
      10041        signal_floor population rate _ (h_pop _ hr hc) (h_rate _ hr hc) h_temp (h_couple _ hr hc)
      10042      exact absurd (Nat.lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.le_trans hfloor B.certificate) h_gap) (Nat.lt_irrefl _)
      10043  
      10044  /-- NO THIRD POSITION, ON THE CARRIER. Given the reading, the bound and the gap, the denial of the hypothesis and
      10045      the two physical premises cannot all stand: whoever denies the hypothesis has named h_realize or h_signal as
      10046      the premise that fails. -/
      10047  theorem no_third_position_on_the_carrier
      10048      {ClassicalRH : Prop} {Zζ : Config} {δ : Nat} (realized : PhysicalCarrier → Prop)
      10049      (B : CertifiedObservationalBound)
      10050      (h_read : ClassicalRH ↔ Value Zζ) (h_gap : B.ε < δ) :
      10051      ¬ (¬ ClassicalRH ∧ (∀ p, Zζ p → realized (map_zero_to_carrier p)) ∧
      10052         (∀ c, realized c → ¬ Neutral c → B.R ≥ δ)) := by
      10053    intro ⟨hno, h_realize, h_signal⟩
      10054    apply hno
      10055    apply h_read.mpr
      10056    intro p hp
      10057    match decEq p.1 0 with
      10058    | isTrue h => exact h
      10059    | isFalse hoff =>
      10060      have hRδ := every_violation_exceeds_detection_gap realized h_realize h_signal p hp hoff
      10061      exact absurd (Nat.lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.le_trans hRδ B.certificate) h_gap) (Nat.lt_irrefl _)
      10062  
      10063  /-! ## VIII-f · what is premise, shown by witness -/
      10064  
      10065  /-- THE REALIZATION IS THE PREMISE. The predicate that says which carriers the vacuum instantiates is an input:
      10066      under the predicate that realizes every state, h_realize holds at every configuration; under the predicate that
      10067      realizes none, h_realize fails at the pair world of the off point. No theorem of this file chooses between them. -/
      10068  theorem realization_is_the_premise :
      10069      (∃ realized : PhysicalCarrier → Prop, ∀ S : Config, ∀ p, S p → realized (map_zero_to_carrier p)) ∧
      10070      (∃ realized : PhysicalCarrier → Prop, ¬ ∀ p, pairWorld offPoint p → realized (map_zero_to_carrier p)) :=
      10071    ⟨⟨fun _ => True, fun _ _ _ => trivial⟩,
      10072     ⟨fun _ => False, fun h => h offPoint (Or.inl rfl)⟩⟩
      10073  
      10074  /-- THE CARRIER ALONE DECIDES NOTHING. The pair world of the off point is closed, lacks least erasure, and its
      10075      carriers are charged; with no realization premise and no bound no theorem above reaches the value there. -/
      10076  theorem the_carrier_alone_decides_nothing :
      10077      Closed (pairWorld offPoint) ∧ ¬ LeastErasure (pairWorld offPoint) ∧
      10078      ¬ Neutral (map_zero_to_carrier offPoint) :=
      10079    ⟨pair_world_closed offPoint,
      10080     fun hle => off_point_is_off ((reg_erases_nothing_iff offPoint).mp (hle offPoint (Or.inl rfl))),
      10081     (mathematical_violation_forces_physical_discard offPoint off_point_is_off).1⟩
      10082  
      10083  /-- THE LAW IS NOT DERIVED. Landauer's heat is a definition of this file: at temperature zero it is zero for every
      10084      count. The theorem records that nothing in the kernel forces the heat, only counts it. -/
      10085  theorem landauer_is_entered_not_derived (bits : Nat) : landauerHeat bits 0 = 0 := by
      10086    unfold landauerHeat landauerHeatPerEvent
      10087    rw [Nat.zero_mul, Nat.mul_zero]
      10088  
      10089  /-! ## VIII-h · the root on the physical side: the floor is there, and the realization is not -/
      10090  
      10091  /-- THE PHYSICAL FLOOR: that some state is realized. -/
      10092  def PhysicalFloor (realized : PhysicalCarrier → Prop) : Prop := ∃ c, realized c
      10093  
      10094  /-- THE PHYSICAL FLOOR IS SELF-GROUNDING, in the seed's own sense (Part I, `SelfGrounding`): an act of measurement
      10095      is a realized state, so every act, the act of denial included, instantiates the floor. Constructed, not posited:
      10096      the acts, one act, and the state each act realizes are the three fields, and the floor follows from them. -/
      10097  def physicalFloorGrounding (realized : PhysicalCarrier → Prop) (Act : Type) (anAct : Act)
      10098      (stateOf : Act → PhysicalCarrier) (h : ∀ a, realized (stateOf a)) :
      10099      SelfGrounding (PhysicalFloor realized) :=
      10100    ⟨Act, anAct, fun a => ⟨stateOf a, h a⟩⟩
      10101  
      10102  /-- THE PHYSICAL FLOOR DECIDES NO REALIZATION. Under the predicate that realizes exactly the apparatus state, the
      10103      floor holds, the floor is self-grounding, and the realization of the off-line zero fails at the pair world. The
      10104      floor is there and the carrier of the off-line zero is not: the mirror, on the physical side, of the seed's
      10105      `the_floor_alone_decides_no_value`. The passage from "some state is realized" to "the carrier of every read zero
      10106      is realized" is not an inference from the floor; it is the second layer, the act at the configuration. -/
      10107  theorem the_physical_floor_decides_no_realization :
      10108      ∃ realized : PhysicalCarrier → Prop,
      10109        PhysicalFloor realized ∧
      10110        SelfVerifying (PhysicalFloor realized) ∧
      10111        ¬ ∀ p, pairWorld offPoint p → realized (map_zero_to_carrier p) :=
      10112    ⟨fun c => c = PhysicalCarrier.selfConjugate 0,
      10113     ⟨_, rfl⟩,
      10114     fun _ => ⟨_, rfl⟩,
      10115     fun h => by have e := h offPoint (Or.inl rfl); cases e⟩
      10116  
      10117  /-- THE REALIZATION IS NOT THE FLOOR: identified on every configuration, they would agree at the pair world, where
      10118      the floor holds and the realization fails. The mirror of the seed's `floor_is_not_least_erasure`. -/
      10119  theorem realization_is_not_the_floor :
      10120      ¬ ∀ realized : PhysicalCarrier → Prop, ∀ S : Config,
      10121          (PhysicalFloor realized ↔ ∀ p, S p → realized (map_zero_to_carrier p)) := by
      10122    intro h
      10123    obtain ⟨realized, hfloor, _, hfail⟩ := the_physical_floor_decides_no_realization
      10124    exact hfail ((h realized (pairWorld offPoint)).mp hfloor)
      10125  
      10126  /-- THE PHYSICAL ROUTE READS THE ROOT TWICE. The physical premises, the certified bound and the gap deliver, at the
      10127      read configuration, exactly what the seed says the act supplies: the root read twice, `RootReadTwice Zζ`, which
      10128      is the value there by `the_root_read_twice_is_the_value`. The physics is the second layer, not the first. -/
      10129  theorem the_physical_route_reads_the_root_twice
      10130      {Zζ : Config} {n0 r0 T0 T : Nat}
      10131      (realized : PhysicalCarrier → Prop) (population rate : PhysicalCarrier → Nat)
      10132      (B : CertifiedObservationalBound)
      10133      (h_realize : ∀ p, Zζ p → realized (map_zero_to_carrier p))
      10134      (h_pop     : ∀ c, realized c → ¬ Neutral c → population c ≥ n0)
      10135      (h_rate    : ∀ c, realized c → ¬ Neutral c → rate c ≥ r0)
      10136      (h_temp    : T ≥ T0)
      10137      (h_couple  : ∀ c, realized c → ¬ Neutral c →
      10138                     B.R ≥ LeastErasureDoF.residual (population c) (rate c) (landauerHeatPerEvent T))
      10139      (h_gap     : B.ε < detectionGap n0 r0 T0) :
      10140      RootReadTwice Zζ :=
      10141    (the_root_read_twice_is_the_value Zζ).mpr
      10142      (classical_rh_from_physico_formal_closure (ClassicalRH := Value Zζ) realized population rate B Iff.rfl
      10143        h_realize h_pop h_rate h_temp h_couple h_gap)
      10144  
      10145  /-- THE ONE EXIT, SHAPED. Under the reading, a certified bound, the gap, and the signal floor of a realized charged
      10146      carrier, a denial of the hypothesis asserts a read zero off the line whose carrier is realized in no measured
      10147      register: a second register, a second world. The denier owns that assertion; nothing else remains. The step from
      10148      the failed universal to its witness is classical; the cone is printed. -/
      10149  theorem the_one_exit_is_a_second_register
      10150      {ClassicalRH : Prop} {Zζ : Config} {δ : Nat} (realized : PhysicalCarrier → Prop)
      10151      (B : CertifiedObservationalBound) (h_read : ClassicalRH ↔ Value Zζ) (h_gap : B.ε < δ)
      10152      (h_signal : ∀ c, realized c → ¬ Neutral c → B.R ≥ δ) :
      10153      ¬ ClassicalRH → ∃ p, Zζ p ∧ ¬ onLine p ∧ ¬ realized (map_zero_to_carrier p) := by
      10154    intro hno
      10155    apply Classical.byContradiction
      10156    intro hnone
      10157    apply hno
      10158    apply h_read.mpr
      10159    intro p hp
      10160    match decEq p.1 0 with
      10161    | isTrue h => exact h
      10162    | isFalse hoff =>
      10163      exact (hnone ⟨p, hp, hoff, fun hr =>
      10164        absurd (Nat.lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.le_trans
      10165          (h_signal _ hr (mathematical_violation_forces_physical_discard p hoff).1) B.certificate) h_gap)
      10166          (Nat.lt_irrefl _)⟩).elim
      10167  
      10168  /-! ## VIII-g · the physico-formal closure, bound -/
      10169  
      10170  /-- THE PHYSICO-FORMAL CLOSURE, BOUND. The hardened closure of Part VII; the closure on the physical carrier; the
      10171      map's two inverses and its equivariance; the line as the neutral sector; the registration as annihilation; the
      10172      violation forcing the discard; the discard forcing the heat; every violation exceeding the gap; the bridge
      10173      derived; the capstone; no third position on the carrier; the two witnesses of what is premise; and the four
      10174      laws of the root on the physical side: the floor decides no realization, the realization is not the floor, the
      10175      physical route reads the root twice, and the one exit is a second register. -/
      10176  theorem the_physico_formal_closure :
      10177      (type_of% @Hardening.the_hardened_closure) ∧
      10178      (type_of% @the_closure_on_the_physical_carrier) ∧
      10179      (type_of% @map_left_inverse) ∧
      10180      (type_of% @map_right_inverse) ∧
      10181      (type_of% @map_fold) ∧
      10182      (type_of% @map_neutral_iff_onLine) ∧
      10183      (type_of% @map_reg) ∧
      10184      (type_of% @le_transports) ∧
      10185      (type_of% @mathematical_violation_forces_physical_discard) ∧
      10186      (type_of% @discard_forces_heat_generation) ∧
      10187      (type_of% @every_violation_exceeds_detection_gap) ∧
      10188      (type_of% @bridge_from_realization) ∧
      10189      (type_of% @classical_rh_from_physico_formal_closure) ∧
      10190      (type_of% @no_third_position_on_the_carrier) ∧
      10191      (type_of% @realization_is_the_premise) ∧
      10192      (type_of% @landauer_is_entered_not_derived) ∧
      10193      (type_of% @the_physical_floor_decides_no_realization) ∧
      10194      (type_of% @realization_is_not_the_floor) ∧
      10195      (type_of% @the_physical_route_reads_the_root_twice) ∧
      10196      (type_of% @the_one_exit_is_a_second_register) :=
      10197    ⟨@Hardening.the_hardened_closure, @the_closure_on_the_physical_carrier,
      10198     @map_left_inverse, @map_right_inverse, @map_fold, @map_neutral_iff_onLine, @map_reg, @le_transports,
      10199     @mathematical_violation_forces_physical_discard, @discard_forces_heat_generation,
      10200     @every_violation_exceeds_detection_gap, @bridge_from_realization,
      10201     @classical_rh_from_physico_formal_closure, @no_third_position_on_the_carrier,
      10202     @realization_is_the_premise, @landauer_is_entered_not_derived,
      10203     @the_physical_floor_decides_no_realization, @realization_is_not_the_floor,
      10204     @the_physical_route_reads_the_root_twice, @the_one_exit_is_a_second_register⟩
      10205  
      10206  end PhysicoFormal
      10207  end PartVIII

      10346    the Stage 2 implication, which yield the classical hypothesis if and when the
      10347    former external inputs are later supplied. Corroboration only. May be omitted.
      10348

      10350    annihilation locally, so the block is independently checkable. It depends on
